title: Sony's Midrange ANC Buds
text:
I have worked a lot with active noise canceling (ANC) headphones and ear buds, and I was excited to try these as Sony has really come on strong in recent years in this area. I usually do not wear ear buds, favoring full-sized over-the-ear can, but sometimes ear buds are the right answer. I am not unhappy with these.

There are two aspects of these that need discussion - the ANC function and the sound quality. I’ll cover each of these separately.

The ANC function is good but is not top-notch. That is, it’s very effective at killing off ambient sound and it allows for listening to music at lower volumes without letting in surrounding sounds like fans and air handlers in an office or road noise in a car. It is not as aggressive as some of Sony’s other offerings, but still far and away better than cheaper headphones and ear buds available.

I like the fact that I can touch one of the buds and the mode switches to allow more ambient noise through for conversation. This is a common feature for ANC phones of any type anymore, and this pair of buds implements this well.

The default sound profile is good but not perfect. The bass is good and not overdriven which is a refreshing change from most phones I have used. The midrange is a little off, with sound being a little muddy and with the slightest of distortion if you’re looking for it. The highs are not sharp and also seem a bit muted like the midrange, though it is not severe enough to write these off by any means. I have worked with ear buds that have better balanced sound profiles, but I have also heard much worse. Now, all that said, with Sony’s application it’s easy to access an equalizer to better balance the sound as desired. I have had no trouble tweaking the active profile in the equalizer to get these to sound better depending on the kind of music I’m listening to.

These are Sony’s midrange buds, and are sold at a midrange price point. If these were priced like their top-end buds I would be hesitant to recommend them. At the price point, though, they’re a good option and are better than most off-brand or cheap ear buds available.

title: Extra gimmick/tool to keep thieves away
text:
We mounted one on each of our Lectric Xp bikes. With a few real thick zip ties (the ones included are useless) they fit perfectly and solidly in the bike rack. And once you load your cargo or in my case mount a thin board on top of the rack. There will be no access for anyone to reach or destroy the alarm if it goes off. It is the perfect fit and hiding spot for those with a similar bike or rack set up. Although, I know some hide it in the seat above the post. It has enough air gap to hear the horn/alarm and can't be messed with or even found/seen.

Now as for how well the alarm works. It arms and works great as a bell with the 3 tone options. No idea if it will deter thieves. But I know I would not be able to waste much time trying to cut any locks with this alarm blaring for the 30 seconds it takes to reset.

You can see in my photos that it fits perfectly flush on the rear rack. So it is easy to place cargo on the rack and not touch the alarm. I installed it facing down to the fender. There is only a 2 inch gap between the fender and rack so the alarm does not touch the fender and not enough room to reach alarm this way either. Once I mount the wood panel to the rack. It will be totally covered and unreachable to the average person. Sure it will add a extra step should I need to change the batteries. But minor detail. And should this post reveal a way to defeat the location. Still likely to get enough eyes on the thief to show anyone around that a bike is being stolen. Bike is only used in daytime and mostly for trail riding.

For the price. This is a worth it expense to try for a well rounded security in conjunction with one or two bike lock methods. We have three!

title: Not disappointed
text:
I am not going to cover every feature in detail since other reviews have some an excellent job of that. My points of comparison are a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite 10.4-inch Android Tablet 128GB that I purchased in June 2021, and my first large format Galaxy, the Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet that I purchased in June 2015.

This one is a major performance improvement over the most recent (June 2021) Galaxy, and better in all respects than the much older 12.2 Galaxy I purchased in June 2015.

I was totally pleased with the Tab S6, but missed the larger screen of the Tab Pro 12.2. This screen is significantly more vivid than the 12.2 Tab Pro, and the 256gb memory in this one pretty much assures that the performance is significantly better than either the 32GB Tab Pro or the 128GB Tab S6. But that is expected.

What I truly love about this tablet over the older large format one is the body is sturdy and not prone to bending. That is why my Tab Pro ultimately failed: the body was so thin that it flexed and at some point it started acting crazy. It would have cost more to repair it than to purchase the Tab S6. Prior to purchasing this one I made sure that that issue had been resolved. Yes, it's not as light, but it more than makes up for it in sheer speed, superior display, and even sound quality.

If you want or need a large format tablet that is reasonably priced and provides excellent battery life and performance this is worth considering.

title: A basic projector with great brightness and full HD resolution
text:
The WEWATCH Video Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth is a basic projector that has all of the necessary features that one needs.

The description of this product may lead you to think otherwise, but this projector is not really a "smart" projector. It does not run on Android and the built-in user interface is quite basic. Yes, it will play videos and show photos from USB drives and it has WIFI... for whatever reason (I didn't really look into it because I simply plugged in a FireTV). The bluetooth, on the other hand, does have a function. I'll get into that in a bit.

So for video input, you have two full sized HDMI ports, a VGA (for those ancient laptops that your office may have lying around?) and a USB port which outputs enough amperage to run a fireTV, so no additional power adapter necessary.

There is no automatic keystone adjustment, but what is there works well. You can adjust the four corners up and down, although I found that it still seems to have some bloating in the middle no matter how I adjust it (could be a problem with my projection screen and projector positioning). A tip for doing the adjustment: If you aren't able to move the corners in the direction that you need, try adjusting the zoom first. By zooming out, it allows the corners to be pulled up or down more.

Audio is as expected in that it is not winning any awards. It can get pretty loud, but it still sounds empty. This is where bluetooth or the 3.5 mm headphone jack comes in. For wireless audio, you can either pair a bluetooth speaker/soundbar to the projector itself or you can pair the speakers directly to the FireTV or whatever dongle you're using. The advantage of pairing the speakers to the projector is that they will work for both HDMI inputs. If you really wanted to get full surround, you'll have to extract the audio out of the HDMI wire. Basically plug the HDMI into an audio receiver, then the audio receiver to the projector. The receiver can take care of decoding the surround depending on your setup.

For the brightness, the 1100LM beats out many other projectors of this price and resolution. You can really tell that the picture just pops. It will work well enough in a dimly lit room, but you can only truly appreciate it when the lights are completely off.

Overall, this is a low-priced projector that will work well for outdoor, temporary use, or even a permanent setup inside the home.

title: AWESOME ETHERNET SWITCH & POWER SUPPLY!
text:
This small, silent, unmanaged 1000 Mbps Ethernet switch has 4 super fast ports (the other 1 is for your input) that not only provide high speed internet but automatically detect if the plugged in device needs power and, if so, how much!

I did thorough testing on this unit over the last couple of months and I am thoroughly impressed by the performance.

By utilizing the built in chip this switch will provide up to 30 watts to every Ethernet device connected but will not provide any power to devices that do not require power or more than is required. I found that this switch works absolutely flawlessly.

Having the capability to provide super fast internet speed and power at the same time makes this switch perfect for both business environments and as a hub for security systems.

I’ve tested my unit extensively using different security cameras and the results are nothing short of incredible. While most security cameras can be run via WiFi, nearly all of them still require a power adapter be plugged in. By utilizing this hub, security breaches are all but eliminated - by utilizing Ethernet instead of Wifi transmission your local storage unit makes it so there is no easy out of network access. In addition, transfer speed, resolution and picture quality is greatly increased - making the entire system more useful. In my experience, I found power is much easier to manage doing it this way as opposed to having to run separate power supplies to each camera.

This POE switch provides ample power for four security cameras, even those with pan / tilt capabilities. It is easy to install, requires little space and is reliable. While I had not used this brand in the past I will not hesitate to in the future.

This is an all around outstanding product that I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend. This unit is sure to hold up well and perform even better.

I regularly update my reviews to reflect any changes I may discover and to include helpful tips you may need if you purchase the product. title: Excellent For My Niche Use But Only Entry Level For General Use
text:
As an old, retired guy, tech factors into my daily life in two important ways. The first way is that I spend hours every day online, playing my favorite MMO. The second is that my extended family, spread across the United States, stays in touch via social media. The very specific niche I got this tablet to fill was for a way to get social media notifications that wouldn't disrupt my gaming. I first tried an Amazon 7" Fire Tablet. The audio notification on that tablet died after the first day or two. There was also no way I could find to turn off the sleep function. The tablet kept shutting down so I couldn't just look over to visually see if there any notifications.

This Android tablet works perfectly to fill that niche. It sits quietly next to my main computer screen and gives a soft audio notification when I get an email or a text message. A glance shows me the first lines of the text or email, letting me know if a quick response is needed or not. The notifications were easy to set up and the sleep function is set to Never. So this tablet does exactly what I want it too.

There are some issues with it that you should be aware of though. For one thing, it charges slowly but drains quickly. For another, turning it back on sometimes takes a bit of extra button pushing. It looks like it is coming on but then shuts off again. At times I've had to hit the power button 4-5 times before it turns all the way on. Videos are just on the edge of being grainy while the audio is distinctly tinny, without any depth. I sometimes listen to audiobooks while gaming but the sound is just too tinny and irritating to listen to them on this tablet.

Since this product does exactly what I want it to, I have to give it a 4 star rating. Other than my specific niche use though, this is a basic, entry level product, which is why I can't give it 5 stars. It just doesn't have the high end quality of far more expensive tablets.

title: Convenient design, but seriously underpowered
text:
The design concept is great: six widely spaced power outlets, plus six usb charge ports in a compact, lightweight brick. And with the limited tryout I gave it, I can say that it works at least partially. The problem I have is with the ratings. The total current rating is 10 amp (or 1200 watt if you prefer to think that way), so don't be planning to plug in six power-demanding devices. (Six laptops, or three laptops plus three displays, would probably be fine.) The USB power rating is even worse: the max per port is 2.4A, and the total over all six ports is 3.4A (no, I'm not kidding), or 17W. So if you use all the ports to charge your phone, kindle, tablet, earbud, etc., don't expect fast charging. A good multiport USB power brick should give you roughly 10W per port, so for six ports it should have been 60 or more watts. (There are 65W chargers on Amazon.)

So overall recommendation is to give this a pass: you can do better by buying a decent power strip to meet your power distribution needs, and a separate USB power brick to cover those needs.

title: Are These Dangerous or Are the Designers Stupid?
text: I have a problem with the way ALL surge protectors are designed. Why can't they add plates with holes on each end so we can screw them into or onto cabinets, under counters, etc.? I am disabled and cannot get down onto or up off the floor. I have to keep these on table tops so I can plug in the endless chargers necessitated by modern technology. Since tech companies can't be consistent in how they shape and size transformers (I use all Apple products, and they can't be consistent within their own company), we have to be creative to get even three plugs to fit into a six-outlet adapter. Then the stupid surge protector falls on the floor, and we have to fish it out from under and behind furniture, along with transformers/plugs that have all been pulled out and then do the whole jigsaw puzzle again. The third time a day this happens, I let loose some serious profanity about the people who design the surge protectors. WE NEED TO BE ABLE TO ATTACH THEM TO/UNDER COUNTERS SO THEY STAY WHERE WE NEED THEM. How difficult is that for these brain trusts to figure out? It makes me wonder if surge protectors are such a fire hazard on the whole that it's dangerous to attach them to structures, which means they are actually too dangerous to use. What's the story? Are surge protectors dangerous, or are their designers just stupid?

title: Still wobbly, lots of adjustability options
text:
I wanted to use the ULANZI T2 Adjustable Tablet Holder to suspend my iPad Air 4 over my bed. I’ve already tried using a gooseneck holder to hold my iPad, but it was wobbly and every time I moved, the iPad bounced. So I thought the spring-loaded design of this one would prevent wobbling.

There are no assembly instructions inside the box. It’s not rocket science, but I shouldn’t have to look at the product page to figure out how to put it together. Instructions would also be helpful to show all the adjustability options for the various angles.

The mounting clamp only has a usable opening of 1¾ inches, so I’d advise double checking the width of where you want to mount it. I have a desk beside my bed that I used to mount the tablet holder, and I lucked out that the front of the desk didn’t have a metal frame underneath it. Otherwise, it wouldn’t have fit.

The tablet holder part held my iPad Air, with my iPad in a thin TPU case. The sides of the tablet holder have silicone pads (the clamp does too) to prevent scratching the tablet. But the grips aren’t too deep, so they won’t accommodate a thick case or device.

Unfortunately, this metal tablet holder had the same problem as the gooseneck one: it’s wobbly. It starts out okay, but I have to keep tightening the various screws, or my iPad wobbles. I also feel like it’s unsteady when stretched to the maximum length, so that impacts how I have to position the tablet holder.

title: Lightweight, portable monitor
text:
The BOIFUN Portable Monitor really IS portable. It’s not that much bigger than my 13-inch MacBook Pro, and it weighs less. I could see packing the monitor for a trip, to use for work and play. I have used the monitor with my Mac and my Nintendo Switch, and it works great with both devices.

The monitor has USB-C and Mini HDMI input options. It comes with cables for both options, which I appreciated. That’s one small downside, you’ll need to make sure to take the Mini HDMI cable with you.

I used the USB-C input with my Mac, it worked. I used the Mini HDMI to HDMI input for my Nintendo Switch, it worked. With both devices, the picture on the monitor was clear and bright. The monitor is plug and play, no instructions really needed.

I did some online Splatoon matches with my Switch to see if there would be any noticeable lag or freezing on the monitor, there were no problems. The game looked great, although the built-in speakers are very tinny.

I do have a few complaints about the monitor. The “smart cover” is super basic. The pictures show folding the cover and using it as a stand, propping the monitor against it. Like a tablet smart cover. But that’s seemingly impossible to do. The cover is very floppy, with no support to hold itself in any stand-shape. The box does include a basic plastic stand, but I wish I could use the cover as pictured, since the stand is one more thing to pack if I go somewhere.

Also, the cover is like a file folder. There’s no way to attach it to the monitor. It relies on magnets alone to stay in place. I wish it had some sort of clip or strap inside, to secure the monitor.

Secondly, the input ports are on opposite sides. The USB-C port is on the same side as the power port, but the Mini HDMI port is on the other side. So if you want to use the monitor in landscape position, you’re limited by input type.

The monitor is powered via USB-C, a cable and wall adapter are included. The wall adapter is a basic 5V USB-A wall adapter. I like that it isn’t some proprietary charging cable.

The main problem that I fine with them is when mounted outdoors they tend to fail after 2 to 3 months sometimes in other cases they last as long as a year but in every case they end up failing.

The really frustrating thing is that once they die there’s no way to bring them back and the battery life just doesn’t seem to last past a few months of outdoor abuse.

When paired with a solar charger they actually do quite well and are not problem to keep outside for Several weeks without charging.

The main drawback to this type of system is that it only records when there’s motion this is in order to save battery life and it has a small chip that does motion to Engage the camera once there’s actually motion going on.

Because of this many people are surprised that they can’t look at a point in time and see what was going on they have to only look at the motion events that are raised by the camera. title: Cute budget keyboard / mouse set bot nothing beyond
text:
I think this set is very cute in terms of design with some hidden features that is not marketed. So here is what I think.

Build Quality & Design:
I think the color is personal preference, but still think the white-pastel baby pink theme is very cute. Other than that, it doesn't have any unnecessary design element. The finish material is somewhat cheap plastic, but when you consider for $15 keyboard AND mouse set, it is extremely well done. As you can see from photo, they prepared USB-B home on the back, next to battery. Most other companies do that under the mouse, so this was very interesting choice of design. Definitely, it is somewhat inconvenient, if you have to use this set in multiple computer. Other than that, it doesn't bother me at all.

Functionality:
Again, this is somewhat personal preference, this keyboard makes very low hitting sound except the spacebar. I have no idea why they built this way. So it is too much for silence keyboard because of the spacebar but it sounds very dull if you like to hear the mechanical sound of typing. This keyboard doesn't have 6 key island (insert/home/page/delet/end key, normally placed on top of cursor arrows.) If you need for these keys frequently, then this keyboard is not for you. It does have fn-key function so you can use these keys somehow, but it's somewhat inconvenient. Also, they placed backspace twice (one in the conventional place and in the number pad under + sign. This set needs 4 AAA battery, which I think it's a little excessive.

Ergonomics:
Both the keyboard and mouse are very thin, so it feels somewhat inconvenient. Especially the mouse looks and feels very similar to the old apple mouse, adding considerable pressure on wrist. If you are okay with Apple mouse then you will like it. (But not me.)

Buy it if you need : a set of keyboard & mouse with limited budget with extremely cute colors
Don't if you want: ergonomic, full keyboard or if need to use your computer for long time

title: For nerds
text:
I was literally just thinking I wanted something like this, and then I found it. Who knew someone would make this?

Yes, you can use adapters to find out the power draw of other USB types.

Yes, it is super simple and just shows you volts, amps, and watts, and power direction. Easy to read screen, the whole thing is as small as a traditional USB flash drive.

The one thing I might like is if it came with a flexible cable to actually plug into the outlet, so that you're not putting any force on the port sticking out, but I guess just using a cable might be more prudent so that you can replace it if it ever wears out. It might be worthwhile to come with some well-thought-out adapters, so that you can easily piece together what you need to read different port types. I like this because you have so many different amperages that ports can deliver and devices can pull, and you don't always get a clear description of what a product can do, so with this, you can see it for yourself.

title: Excellent Streaming / Retro Box
text:
Picked up originally to give to my son for his first computer....but....Yeah, now it's for the whole family. It's under the TV in the living room next to our XBOX. Haha. I gotta say I'm super impressed for the price. The i5 may be older, but this box is capable of running emulated games up to PS2 at 1X resolution....I was genuinely surprised how well it handles those games even after seeing videos of it in action.

Office Use - Absolutely great. Programs open quickly and you can have several open at the same time. 16GB RAM makes for a smooth experience, even with Photoshop, Outlook, and Firefox across several different monitors. Not even a hiccough. Substantially better than the laptop I was issued from work.

Retro Gaming - Runs everything from about 2010 and earlier (if it is compatible with Win10) like a champ with highest settings in most cases. Fallout 4 is AWESOME. GTA5 is....acceptable with the right settings. Streaming from STEAM or the XBOX works just fine, even on wifi. Much better with a wired connection, though.

Modern Gaming - Hit or miss. This has an older integrated graphics chip, so you're going to have to really drop a lot of quality settings to get just okay performance. You could always hook up an external GPU and it'd run circles around most other mini-PCs out there. This is NOT a modern gaming PC.

Emulators - RUNS ALMOST EVERYTHING. Came across a few PS2 games that were sluggish, but custom settings at 1X resolution made them playable at around 30FPS. PSP, PSX, GC, etc....No problems at all. Pair this with a decent wireless control and you've got all your favorite console games ready to play. Everything from the cartridge days works flawlessly. Batocera 33 is fantastic. Launchbox also does a decent job.

Hardware - Yes, it's older hardware...But for this price and this form factor, it's worth it. There's nothing I've tried that I wasn't able to do...modern games being the exception. For our use as a living-room PC, it is perfect. It's quiet, sturdy, and runs everything we want. Streaming from our media server is quick and there's no stutter even when playing 4K video. There are plenty of ports, and we've added a second hard drive for storage.

Overall, I'm super stoked to have this. It's a full PC the size of a Wii. Knowing what I was getting into when I purchased it certainly helped. I went in with the expectations of older hardware, no high-end GPU, and pretty basic tasks...Minecraft and Roblox for my son, and internet apps...Found out I could do so much more and ended up putting it in the living room for the family to use instead. Toss in extra RAM, add that second hard drive, and I have the best console gaming experience ever. Great machine!

title: Contains 6% isopropyl alcohol
text:
All of the top-selling screen cleaners advertise not having alcohol in them. This product contains isopropyl alcohol. The marketing says it was developed for eyeglasses, not LCD monitors.

Many manufacturers and Web sites advise not to use alcohol to clean LCD monitors and monitors that have an anti-glare coating. You can use alcohol on glass and glossy monitors. The manual for my Dell monitor says to clean it with a cloth and water. Another Dell monitor manual says you can use alcohol for spot treatment if water does not work, but it should be cleaned with water after that. The Apple MacBook cleaning instructions say to only use water when cleaning the screen. The Apple instructions for iMac screens are similar to Dell’s, where they say to only use water, but you can use 70% isopropyl alcohol for spot-treatment of hard-to-remove smudges.

The main monitor I needed to clean was a glass TV monitor, so this product worked fine for that. I also used it on multiple anti-glare LCD monitors and my eyeglasses, since the marketing for this says it contains 6% alcohol, which is a concentration so low that it likely has no negative impact. This percentage should be disclosed on the bottle itself so people who have not seen the marketing materials can evaluate whether it is safe to use. The liquid smells more like mint than alcohol, like a mouthwash smell.

They should provide more instructions on the bottle. You should get the dust off first using a cloth or maybe canned air. Using a liquid cleaner like this is for dirt that cannot be brushed away. These cleaners should be used with a microfiber cloth designed for glass. The main glass monitor cleaners are distilled water, which can be mixed with either white vinegar or 70% isopropyl alcohol. You can make your own screen cleaner pretty easily. "Nano Magic" and "nanotechnology" is nonsense marketing.

title: I am really liking this headset, surprised by the quality of sound, noise cancelling, and comfort
text:
In my work I need long periods of quiet. I’ve done what I can to deal with a lack of quiet these last two years, between my wife working at home and the neighborhood seeing far more people at home. I’ve tried a few things, but in many ways had to sacrifice and learn to deal with the sound. For several months I was working from midnight till 3 or 4 am to get some of my work done. So I started to think about going back to headphones. I’ve previously owned a set of a well known, expensive brand that was good - well, great sound, but they were big and got to be far too hot on my head, especially over time. So I ended up getting rid of those. I still wear a set of those that sit on the outside of my ears for sound - which is outstanding - but they don’t always cover enough noise as they were designed to allow the athletes who wear them to actually hear sound around them. So....

I was thinking what I might do again. I had the chance to get these Ankbit Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, but went in knowing they too might be too hot on my head after awhile. I figured I’d at least get some work done in a few hours each day.... but would they be enough?

I should also mention, I have a lifelong issue with my ears that causes me to feel the pressure (think airplanes and storms) in such a way it can bother my head. The other reason I got rid of those expensive well know headphones was that they sat so securely on my head, the pressure was too much for my head. I again, could only wear them for so long before I had to take them off.

So, these Ankbit Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones?
So far I really like them - a lot!
I’ve been wearing them every day for at least a few hours and getting work done. It has taken a bit of time to adjust, but what I am experiencing has been helpful and I am glad to have them.

The box they come in includes the headset, a bag, and needed cords.

The cords are easy to use, but I would say, it would be nice if the cord for charging were longer. I mean, this thing is SHORT! Where I could normally set an item off to the side with the cord reaching, I now have to set these headsets directly in front of the plug, meaning plugging in other things is difficult. So that would be one improved this set could use.

The bag is great. It is black, nice material, and holds the headset well. Glad to have it.

The Ankbit Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones themselves are surprisingly great. I don’t know why it surprises me, other than I had that expensive pair in the past - which was outstanding - and I like these as much - in some ways, more (think ear discomfort and overheating).

1. The set is comfortable with the ear covers nice and soft on my ears. They are enough to sit well, hold in the sound (my wife has not complained about any sound bleed), and work as far as noise canceling. ** I'll come back to this in a minute. But I find the Ankbit Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones to be very comfortable. If I had one “complaint” it’s that they are slightly large. I have a large head on which I wear large hats. However, even I find the top of this to be a bit larger than my head - which tells me someone with a smaller head than mine might have an issue with the size of these. They do fit, and the ears sit directly on my ears, but I can tell it’s just on my ears. It is comfortable, but something I take note of.

2. There is no (noticeable) pressure build up. Where my previous set caused such pressure that I’d have to take them off at least twice an hour, I’ve never had to take these off and have worn them up to 3 hours at a time - and could go longer.

3. ** The noise reduction works. We tested this the first day - including matching to another work style head set I got to also try and block the noise - the kind used on construction sites and the like - and this Ankbit Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones worked as well or perhaps better than that set. While that set has no music or sound to it and this does, both blocked my wife’s talking and yelling within 2 - 3 feet of me to the point that I could barely hear her. This Ankbit Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones offers the music as a way to add to the options - and I use an app to help if need be, with sounds such as white noise and thunderstorms. But in general, I prefer to be able to have no noise at all at times. With both the app sounds and no sound at all, I am able to block out MOST noise. I do add the app when my wife is working in the kitchen, which is behind my back where I’m working now she’s home. And the app takes care of the rest of the sound. But without it, I have great sound reduction and elimination.

You can also turn this feature off and have “transparency” which allows you to hear background noise, incase you need to listen for the kids or a phone. It still. blocks the sound, gives you good internal sound with music, but you can hear outside sound better. It is like my other, outside the ear set when in this mode, so I do not use it - I have those for that type of sound. But it is available.

4. The sound itself is excellent. I have listened to music and movies playing on these and both are outstanding. I truly love the sound and find it is full, rich, and well done. It’s a pleasant experience.

5. The buttons for on/off, volume up/down, and transparency are at the side of the ear phone on the right side and 1. EASY to the point of frustration that I keep hitting them - usually turning it off - when trying to remove the headset, and needing to learn how to not hit them and 2. easy to use overall. The four buttons are easy to adjust - I’m still getting use to which is which and not second guessing. The on/off is easy, but I’m really impressed with the volume up/down, which is in nice levels of degrees - not too much either way - and gives a great sound.

I also discovered - the hard way - when you close the computer it’ll go off, but open and it’s back up and running. There are so many little things like that. I don’t know, maybe they are far more common than I know - I have not been a headset user for some time - but these are details that impress.

Overall I really like this Ankbit Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones for my work and the quiet it provides, but for the sound I get when I’m listening to sounds to help me work, or even better, the music and movies that help keep me going throughout the day. I’m impressed and if this set lasts for a few years... it’ll be an outstanding find!

title: Zip ties are on my list of essentials
text: When you have a home where you must fix most things on your own, there are a few things that make at least an emergency "fix" to hold until you can get more appropriate items for a permanent fix.  On my list is definitely bungee cords - they are GREAT - and can hold some things for a while.  Zip ties are similar but not as "forgiving" like a bungee cord that can hold, but flex a bit.  As an example of using these zip ties, I have a chain link fence that I have used to "plant" a line of poles to hold string lights high enough that they are out of the way but still provide good lighting at night.  The poles I used bungee cords to lash them to the fence as rain softens the ground and can make the poles lean so the bungee cords hold them more or less in place with a little give.  Now, on the outside of my chain link fence I took rolls of faux ivy and zip tied the plastic grid under the ivy to the fence.  I now have a fence that from the street looks like a hedge even if up close it's obviously fake, but it provides my yard with a bit of privacy and the zip ties were necessary to hold the ivy in place top to bottom and across the length of the fence.  These are excellent, sturdy zip ties that I'm glad to have in my emergency fix it box!

title: Held this one up to my other very small projector
text: I have another small projector that is the size and shape of a CD player - like a CD Walkman, if that makes sense - and I like it so much that other projectors usually fall a bit short of the mark.  Not this one!  It is a little bit bigger, but not by much and the quality of the projector itself is quite good - very sturdy - but this is the only other small projector (other than my CD looking one) that comes with a tripod.  That is, for me, a big deal.  I mean, I live in an old house and half the place is slightly off-kilter!  By that I mean, if I had a projector sitting on a table, it would probably need some cardboard or whatever jammed under one side so the picture showed up on the wall completely level!  With the tripod I can make small adjustments to the projector and be happy with the projected picture.  The image quality is excellent as well from close - I have a pull up screen that is around 40" that's made for a projector.  The videos are amazing on that screen, so the question is how the projector does large, onto a white wall in the house.  The picture isn't quite as crisp at 100", but it is very good.  I have a really amazing bluetooth stereo that syncs up to this projector and really adds to the video experience.  That is not to say the internal speaker isn't good, but considering, I'd rather use an external bluetooth stereo.  Because I do have another small projector that has the same/similar restrictions on proprietary apps like Netflix, I had already purchased a Roku stick so that I could access my Hulu and other apps which worked well on this projector too. title: Solid basic UPS likely best used with doodads other than a PC
text:
I have 10 UPS spread around my home for various bits of essential kit (my needs are a bit beyond the norm), and this little guy has found a home with our modem being it's sole responsibility. Given the extremely modest power draw of the modem, this lasts 30+ minutes. 600VA / 360W won't go far for most PCs. It could do for a Mac Mini or similar PC with laptop based internals or a laptop (which tend to not need a UPS with their internal batteries serving that purpose), but I didn't try this. I didn't due to my 9 other units and the fact that this unit doesn't clearly state it's output waveform (pure sine wave, simulated sine wave, stepped wave, etc...). Absent that I'd recommend this be used with various low power appliances like modems, routers, inkjet printers (not sure why they'd need to be available in a power outage), DVR, etc... I'd recommend a POE switch, but those can chew through 600VA fast.

The price is still sound given those uses, but I'd only recommend buying this for non-PC uses given the limited power and uncertain AC output on battery.

title: meh product
text:
Firstly, I have to point out that half of the attachments are pointless or don't attach as you'd expect them to. For example, the straw attachment is so wide that its pointless to use by itself but none of the other attachments can be added to it to narrow the flow and increase the pressure. Considering this is supposed to replace compressed air cans which have high-pressure, narrow straws, this is incredibly silly. The few attachments that DO narrow down the flow also have extra holes on them. While I assume this is to avoid pressure burning out the motor, it makes it so that the intended output is weaker and you also now have 2 extra holes blasting air forward, so doesn't work very well for fine-detail dusting.

Secondly, I have to disagree with those claiming that this has more pressure than compressed air cans. The real difference is more that, while the pressure is lower, this device can maintain that level rather than losing it quickly like a can does. Unfortunately, this pressure is not as good and will still leave a layer of dust that will have to be wiped off in some cases. This was not really an issue with compressed air cans, except in the most extreme cases of neglect.

Thirdly, as many have pointed out, this thing DOES get warm really fast. It didn't get to a point where it seemed like it would damage components, but its worth noting that this is a valid complaint. The intake vent is also frustratingly easy to accidentally block and sucks up dust and debris like crazy.

Overall, I don't know if I'd really recommend this. Its cheaper than other electric dusters, but the payoff may be poor attachment design.

title: NOT A 1:1 REPLACEMENT FOR COMPRESSED AIR CANS
text:
I bought this since I have a good amount of old electronics that needed cleaning, thinking that i didnt really need to bother with compressed air cans anymore.

That is not the case. The amount of air it moves is quite impressive, and its pretty loud, but thats what is expected from a handheld air pump.

If you need to just generally blast heavy buildup in a PC, this will do a mediocre job, the problem is, the nozzles they include with this version are not designed for that kind of use. They only include a slightly tapered nozzle, which doesnt allow you to get the pressure and precision you need to clean as well as a can of compressed air, even if you blast the thing using the high-power setting. It will get rid of most of the dust, but it wont be able to get anything in any crevices, and it wont be able to remove nearly as much as carefully going over things with a can of compressed air.

If only they included a nozzle that tapers down to a tiny straw, I would love this thing. Dont buy this thinking its a complete replacement for compressed air cans.

title: No local control or UI or ONIF
text:
This is a cloud camera - doesn't support ONIF for recording to an NVR and doesn't have a local web ui to configure it. You must use the VicoHome app - for all settings. This means if the app is no longer maintained or developed, or no longer compatible with the latest Android/iOS - you have e-waste.

The app is kludgy - when compared to something like Ring. It's not fast, nor does it have a scrub line to pan through events. There's a monthly plan option - but you don't know how much it is until you sign up for the trial.

I like that it's solar, and helps cover parts of the property that I can't otherwise reach.

The mount system for the camera is nice - you mount the bracket first, then slide the camera on the bracket.

I HATE that they went with black wire from panel to camera. How many people have black siding in your neighborhood? None? How many have white? most? Why would you put a black wire - it's so hard to be discrete. I'm going spray mine with that stuff people spray for windows to make it look like snow. I don't feel like spray painting the whole thing.

My other complaint about the cable is that it's micro-usb NOT USB-C... so when you are up high on a ladder - you are playing Schrodinger's cable. A micro USB cable is both upside down and right side up until you go to insert it. Then it's upside down. USB-C works all the time.

title: No Web UI/Local control
text:
This is a mostly cloud camera, as the name implies. They DO support ONIF, but that must be configured using the app.

For anyone used to Ring or similar cameras with scrub lines and detection - this is not that. It works, but the app is sort of kludgy. I'm always apprehensive of a device that has no local control. If the vendor stops developing the app or it gets pulled from the app store, you have e-waste.

The motion tracking is OK - it's a bit slow. I leave it on so that any would-be trespasser might think there's a human watching them on the other side. I have mine up on my white siding. When the camera follows motion, at night, the white will reflect and it causes the camera's light to turn off. This is a nuisance that can be fixed by leaving your lights on outside at night.

The App itself is called CloudEdge - it's not fast or anything of the sort. Local storage works OK - but takes a while to load a video. IF you get alerted to an event - you are best to just wait a few minutes for the camera to record it and then watch. If you try to watch while it's recording - it'll likely timeout.

I love that the cable is white - blends better with my siding. I wish the USB cable was removable so that i can just use a longer cable.

The app doesn't' have pinch to zoom to zoom in on the video. So you have to save a snapshot and then zoom it. Seems like a bad workflow.

The connection to the plug doesn't seem waterproof - no gasket or anything - so I'm weary on longevity.

title: Very pleased with this TCL 32" television!
text:
I needed another TV. This time for the bedroom I had just renovated. Shopped around and purchased this unit. When I cut the cable a few years ago, I purchased a ROKU box and I've been very pleased with. Every now and again I experience network glitches, but that's to be expected and the glitches are few and far between.
So, when I discovered these TCL units on Amazon, my curiosity was peaked. I researched and read the reviews. Decided to buy the 32" unit. Was delivered in two days.
Setup was very easy. Hardest part was trying to find where I had recorded my WiFi hub password. With the password in hand and entered into the system, we were off. Programming (software updates) took a few minutes, but went quite quickly.
The picture quality is awesome! I am very pleased with this television. Sound is great and overall quality of the unit is great. Once I discovered how to disable the LED standby light, which is very easy by the way, I am a happy camper.
Oh, it should be mentioned that I did have to move my WiFi hub a few feet. You see I placed this TV at the farthest corner of my home so the signal was a little weak and I experienced the occasional "Buffering" message. Now that my hub has been re-positioned, allowing for a more direct signal, we are good to go.
Bottom line? I would definitely recommend one of these new TCL units. Matter of fact I am currently contemplating purchasing a 43" unit to replace my old 36" Philips unit. Only thing stopping me is that the Philips is still orking so darn good.

title: PistonBuds Pro earbuds are really nice. I like them more than Pixel Buds Pro.
text:
Update: Thoughts 2 months later. I returned my first pair of Piston Buds Pro within 1 week because they offered a $10 discount making them $49.99 instead of $59.99 I do wish I tried the regular Pixel Buds, they look more comfortable than Pixel Buds Pro. I possibly could have tolerated Pixel Buds Pro, but they were so heavy they would fall out doing strenuous activity and cost so much without offer quality sound.

Update: I did deduct 1 star for making me open Bluetooth on the device it connected to last to connect to my other device. I switch between my phone and laptop frequently. I can just select connect on the device I desire if the previously connected device is out of range or I toggle Bluetooth off. I did notice there was a lag delay between video and sound when using these ear buds to preview a video recording of myself for class, I didn't notice any lag with YouTube.

Original reivew:
For reference I previously purchased 'Wireless Earbuds made in China' E10 for $20 after coupon (left, white, smallest case), Air Pods Pro $175 (2nd left, white), Pixel Buds Pro $200 (2nd right, ), Bose SoundSport $109 (right, black, wired). Then this item, 1MORE PistonBuds Pro $50 (Black) in pictures side by side with AirPods Pro case. All tested using a Pixel 6 utilizing YouTube to replay the same song for each device.

PistonBuds review: After a week I really like the 1More PistonBuds Pro ear buds. They were initially $60 with a $10 off coupon, making them ¼ the cost of Pixel Buds Pro. They are much lighter and not as bulky as the Pixel Buds Pro making the design work much better for my ears. Comfort is key, and the Pixel Buds Pro were returned because they were uncomfortable and had inferior sound quality for the price. Bose SoundSport buds still have the best comfort and best overall sound quality. As for sound I will admit Pixel Buds have more bass than the PistonBuds Pro. However the quality of PistonBuds Pro is over all better than Pixel Buds but they aren't as crisp as my wired Bose buds especially in highs, most noticeable in classical music, but PistonBuds do have better bass than my old Bose. The noise cancelling is mediocre but does work, I'm not a fan of PistonBuds transparency mode, I hear like a wind rustling sound with it on, and I'm indoors. Pixel Buds and AirPods don't make this noise during transparency mode, but also cost a lot more. A nice feature is being able to toggle between ANC/transparency/off, pixel buds pro only let you select which 2 you want to toggle between with touch controls. Pixel Buds Pro do have the best touch controls, working consistently and easily. These PistonBuds Pro have more features than ways to access them through touch controls, but the 1MORE app does allow you to change what the double and triple taps do. The touch control options are play/pause, volume down(L)/up(R), previous(L)/next track(R), or voice control options. But you can only assign 2 of the 4 features. Noise cancelling/transparency/off is cycled by a long press. Luckily the mic is responsive and Google assistant is always listening, so "Hey Google" gives me voice control without assigning it. The $20 E10's had more functions assigned but rarely worked. I do wish these PistonBuds had a single tap option for features. Either ear bud works independently for phone calls. The E10's I tried only had a microphone in the R apparently. The PIstonBuds matte case feels good, but it is very light and the hinge is probably weak, I like the texture overall but the case is vastly inferior to AirPods who hands down have the best case. AirPods have completely rounded edge with a metal hinge. PistonBuds took the sharp edge off but didn't make it completely smooth but it does fit in my pocket well. It's a much better case than the E10's, E10 have the smallest of any case but it is the weakest in structure. PistonBuds have a sensor that detect when it's removed from your ear. The PistonBuds and E10's included a charge cable, unlike Google or Apple but no wireless charging capabilities like the Google and Apple have.

Following review posted on Pixel Buds and E10's prior to finding PistonBuds.

I really couldn't get over the pairing issue E10's caused. I went on the hunt again and found the 1More Piston Buds Pro. I was very skeptical because they are almost like the Pixel Buds Pro design, however being much less weight they are seated comfortably and securely. I'm not sure I'd trust them running, but they were $50 after a $10 off coupon. I haven't tested them fully but so far this is an amazing find for the price with actual active noise cancelling. Pairing via bluetooth works ok, both apple and google have better switching between devices. Pixel Buds I just clicked connect on a different device it would automatically disconnect from the old device and connect to the new. With Piston Buds I have to open bluetooth settings on my old device and disconnect before the new device will connect. E10's ($20) buds have to be repaired with device. I have only tested between my laptop (HP Victus) and cellphone (Pixel 6).

For $20 can't beat the E10's. Pairing, specifically changing between devices sucks on the E10 as the other sets switched simply. Also you can't just use 1 earbud in and save battery in the other, even if 1 is in the case it's also playing music. Apple, Google, and 1MORE all have sensors that detect when it's removed from the ear so it can conserve battery.

I received Google Pixel Buds for my birthday this month. I will say they had excellent touch controls and Google assistant was always on point. I'd imagine best wireless battery life too. Probably the best noise cancelling I've ever had. Even better than my, albeit older, Bose Quiet Comfort 25 over the ear wired headphones. Just can't stand how quickly these come out of my ears, the fit is like the tip of an adult thumb to the first knuckle shoved vertically in your ear. Also noted as the best bass.

I bought my wife AirPods Pro for her birthday earlier this year. AirPods are definitely more comfortable than these. Apple added an extra cushion tip that fits into your ear canal for a much more secure fit that also improves sound. Airpods aren't perfect, and will still fall out running or jumping for kids... I'd rather drop these for the price.

Bose SoundSport have the BEST fit of any ear buds I've ever worn. So tight, I've actually pulled the cord loose from my phone instead of out of my ear. But not hard, just the rubber piece fitting my ear perfectly. Bose also have the best overall sound, but they are wired and are lacking deep bass. I will admit pixel buds have the most bass of any of these 4.

Bottom line: The PistonBuds have better overall sound than Pixel Buds Pro not as good as the Bose SoundSport. Yet they do have more bass than my (very old) Bose SoundSport headphones. Small charging case for wireless, easily put in a pocket. Touch controls work but are limited to only a few options. Mediocre noise cancelling. Mic worked good, Google assistant heard me clear as did my test call. Included a charge cable. Cheaper case, not as compact as E10's, only slightly larger than AirPods Pro. I did not test pairing with multiple devices yet... Initial pairing worked well.

title: Not Exactly Heavy Duty
text:
Despite being self-labeled as "Heavy Duty" the specs for this device suggest otherwise. While the aluminum chassis looks and feels nice enough it definitely is not as heavy duty as steel. The only reason that companies use aluminum as opposed to steel is because it is MUCH lighter and saves an enormous amount of money on shipping charges. Shipping charges add up quickly when you are shipping a product from China.

Like most Chinese electronics this device has no UL certification. Like most cheap surge protectors it also comes with no long-term warranty or insurance for equipment protection. It also is only capable of handling 15A, which is definitely not in the heavy duty category. No circuit breaker protection is available, either. The MOVs used for surge protection only handle a paltry 300 joules. That is not going to stop a lightening strike or even a heavy duty surge from static electricity. Any serious power surge would fry this device and most likely any electronics that it is supposed to protect.

So, this is basically just a multiple outlet power strip with a minimal amount of protection. Definitely not worth the asking price, even though it is fairly inexpensive. The switches look nice but they are cheaply made and poorly assembled. This device is definitely built more for looks than for heavy duty use.

title: It's cheap. It's simple. It works.
text:
I took on a project where I recycled one of my PCs and turned it into a firewall/router for my home network. The only thing I was lacking for the project was a second gigabit Ethernet adapter. I've actually used quite a bit of TP-Link's networking gear in recent years, so I figured that I might as well give this inexpensive PCIE gigabit Ethernet card a shot.

Long story short, the card works like a champ. It was easily detected by the firewall software that I used for the install, which is based on the BSD operating system. Since it easily autodetects in BSD I would assume that it works equally well with Linux. I did not bother testing it on a Windows installation, so you should check the manufacturer's specs to make sure that it works with whatever version of that operating system you happen to be using before buying.

Autodetection of the card worked without a hitch and the card is now operating on my gigabit LAN at full duplex with no problems whatsoever. It's simple. It's cheap. It works. That is about the best I can say for any product.

title: DONT BUY. If I could give 0 stars, I would.
text:
The first one I ordered stopped working within a week, so I had it replaced. The second one I received worked fine enough for a while, but I noticed that my Bluetooth mouse and keyboard kept saying 'battery almost dead', so I changed the batteries but it continued to say this. I was convinced the issue was with the mouse and keyboard. I WAS WRONG.

Months later (and way beyond the window of return), I now know the issue was with the USB hub this entire time. I bought a different one just to test it out and WOWZAH what a big difference. For the price of $2-3 added dollars or even just a different brand, you can get an incredibly improved quality product.

If you don't believe me, try plugging each individual USB into your computer directly and compare the speed/function to it once it's plugged into the hub. For example, the connection stability to my Bluetooth devices and my ring light brightness are measurably better.

Beyond just product performance, the quality of the connection is terrible. If anything touches or my table shakes even in the slightest way, the cord connecting the hub to my computer's USB port will disconnect and reconnect-- you will hear this through the notification chimes. The connection is super unstable. In addition to this being annoying, why is it bad? Because you can damage your internal hard drive through the short-circuiting of the product.

As someone who spends a lot of time researching the value of products before purchasing, I am really disappointed. I feel that the other ratings are misleading, but likely just because they don't know better--- like I didn't know for months. Oh well!

Remember, I had TWO of these, so it's not like I just received a defective one.

title: A lot of value for the money
text:
I was looking for an affordable camera system to keep an eye on my two pups, and these Wyze cameras exceeded my expectations. Having them for about a year now, they’re still going strong. I use mine indoors exclusively, so I cannot comment on outside use, but for the money these cameras do exactly what I need them to do. My favorite feature is the ability to operate them from the app on my phone, which makes it very easy to change modes or make other adjustments. Whether streaming or recording, I haven’t run into any problems. From your phone, you can adjust night vision and the sensitivity of your detection settings, even going so far as to create a detection zone, where you’re only notified of a detection within a given area of the camera’s sight, rather than detecting everything the camera can see.

The firmware is regularly updated, and setup is a breeze. Once you’re set up for the first time, it’s as simple as plugging it in wherever you see fit. If you have multiple cameras, they’re all on your app.

While detection is always improving, your detection notifications will go off a lot if your camera can see objects that move a lot (like a branch in the wind, for example). While the camera detects people and pets, it also detects general motion. You can adjust the sensitivity, but it won’t completely resolve the issue. Since I use mine indoors, I don’t have this issue. But if you’re planning to utilize these for outside use, it could become a problem.

title: Good projector that has it all.
text:
When I decided to upgrade my old projector I didn’t realize how difficult it would be to find a model that had all of the features that I wanted for under $200.
The V50 has all of the features I was looking for, but unfortunately is not as nice as some of the other projectors I tried that had fewer features.

First the good. This projector has everything. It has a great, sharp, picture at full 1080 native. This projector is very bright, brighter than most. It has Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 2 HDMI connectors, USB, and even VGA. (Does anyone still use VGA?) Sound quality is clear although it doesn’t seem as loud as others. (I had this at 50-60% while my old one was at 30-40%) While most projectors have a microSD slot, this one has a full SD slot, so you can use SD or microSD with a simple SD card adapter. It also has a hole for a tripod mount. I had no problems using this with a 120” screen and there definitely was room to go larger while my old projector maxed out at this size. The remote worked better than my old projector.

Now the not so good: The lens cover is difficult to take off. You have to twist and pull to get it off. It seems like it was added on and not part of the original design like my old projector which never had a lens cover. The manual keystone adjustment is minimal. While the description says it can adjust ±15 it seems more like ±5 and the adjustment dial barely moves. It seems like something inside is blocking it from moving more. It has two HDMI connections, but since they’re recessed slightly a Fire Stick won’t fit directly and you have to use the dongle which luckily is included with the Fire Stick. I had no problems when using Bluetooth to a speaker, but I did notice a slight delay. Since I haven’t used Bluetooth with a projector before I don’t know if this is specific to this projector or all projectors when using Bluetooth.

Overall the V50 is a great projector that checks all the boxes. I thought the V52 was a better projector, but the V52 doesn’t have Bluetooth or a tripod mount which the V50 does have.

title: Great projector
text:
When I decided to upgrade my old projector I didn’t realize how difficult it would be to find a model that had all of the features that I wanted.

The V52 is a great projector and probably the best I tested in this class, but what killed it for me is the lack of Bluetooth support and no tripod mount. Instead of a tripod mount it has four screw holes that I’m assuming is for a mounting plate for a ceiling mount, which doesn’t do much for me as I want to use it as a backyard projector mounted on a tripod with Bluetooth speakers near the screen.
The V52 has a very sharp clear full 1080p image and is noticeably brighter than similar models. While competitors have only manual vertical keystone correction, the V52 has electronic keystone correction for both vertical and horizontal adjustment to ±50 degrees. The image can also be electronically rotated in one degree increments. It also has several auto settings that can automatically set keystone and rotation which make set up quicker and easier. It supports WiFi for wireless screen sharing from Android and iOS devices. It has a 3 watt speaker that actually provides quite good sound. The fan is a bit noisy, but not much more than comparable models. As far as connections it has USB, HDMI, AV (via included cable), audio out, and a TF (microSD) card slot. It does not have VGA (does anyone still use this?). It has a 3-prong power cord and a user-replicable fuse. I tested this with a Firestick 4K and had no problem using it. If you need a projector for a ceiling mount or table mount and don’t need a tripod mount or Bluetooth audio, this is definitely a great projector.
PS. If you need a projector with Bluetooth and a tripod mount, the V50 has both, but is not as good.

title: $699, Wow!
text:
Let me start out with a couple of caveats that have been very disappointing on the Apps. 2 apps that I like are NOT available for Google Tv. Xfinity Stream and Roku Channel . I can live without ROKU channel but planning to out this TV in a bedroom away from the router box in the LR is a non starter if it can't stream my cable channels. Why??? So now I have to buy and plug in a roku stick to get xfinity. I'm not happy about that.
Now back to our original review...
After waiting for a Roku version of this TV for over a year, our wait was finally rewarded with a decidedly disappointing R655 release.
- At that point we considered switching brands to a smaller OLED. But, after reading OLED reviews regarding burn-in prevention technology that still does NOT work in 2022!...we ended up back here for a TCL R646. In the end, it's all about the picture and the budget.
- The newer R655 appears to be the Roku version of this TV with minimal upgrades and notable downgrades. It appears that the R655 took this same panel, swapped the metal bezel for plastic, added Roku on top of it and somehow ended up with a vastly inferior picture! It defies logic.
So with the astounding sale price, we finally decided to buy and we chose the R646 despite it being a GoogleTV.
Even professional reviewers, presumably being OS agnostic are recommending going backwards to the R646 over the R655.
- When I realized that the main upgrades to the R655 were just Roku on top, 144hz VRR and AMD blah blah blah, I decided I will survive playing my PS4/5/6 games fine at 120hz.
- TV was well packaged and undamaged.
I ran some tests from you tube to see if there were tone or lighting variations. This unit is amazing. Even better than our R617. Head and shoulders above the 4 year old 5-series it replaces. We watched PREY again on it. Very satisfying visuals, and very decent sound.
- One thing I despise about it is the volume control . It seems unpredictable. It goes up or down 1 notch , and another notch, then 5 notches, then 5 or 10 notches. I prefer a linear control to a geometric progression.
- The built-in mic on the TV can be manually switched off. Thank goodness.
- Contrary to what I had read a couple of years ago this GoogleTv does NOT have a built-in camera. Thank goodness again.
- If you don't have internet, the Google Tv acts like an Xbox. It's nothing but a paper weight until you register it online. It will not fully boot without it.
- Not a fan of the remote. They tried to emulate the Roku remote with jump buttons for common apps, volume and mute on the right side which is fine.
But they use the concentric circle navigation button for rev/play/ffd instead of dedicated buttons. That's a problem.
I often hit rew/ffd when trying to hit pause/play in the center of the ring .
- The app tiles include a TV tile but, it seems to go to the last input you used. That might be tunable??
There's no app tile for HDMI1, etc like we have on the roku and fire tv. Inconvenient.
Trying to explain to the fam that you have to go into the settings to switch HDMI inputs is no fun.
You can name the inputs, like the other platforms.
- Surprisingly many reviewers ding the Roku TV for lack of fine picture control. Unless I've missed it, I'm not impressed with the controls on the GoogleTV either. They seem pretty basic.
- Closed-Caption, in fact, on the Roku has very fine tuning for foreground and background Opacity, etc.
I have not found any tuning at all for the GoogleTV except Font size. I like being able to see what's BEHIND the CC bar, especially if it's sports stats and what-not. So that's a bit frustrating.
- The Google TV has TWO usb ports, so, if we add a Roku+ 4K stick, there is still a USB port for OTA Live TV buffering (I believe that's a TCL exclusive)! Though having to retain 3 remotes is not a bonus.
- We planned to add a Roku stick to avoid the Google TV AD machine.
We found there is an option under the User ID profile to enable “Apps Only Mode”.
It still leaves your app tiles tiny and subservient to a huge AD from Google at the TOP, and you can mute the AD from settings it seems.
But at least all of the other distractions are gone.
Apps Only, does disable the Search feature and Google assistant. But their search did not target specific apps installed like the Roku does. I doubt we'll miss Assistant. Much prefer the Roku interface, but we'll try this for a while.
- One R655 bug you just can't fix with an OS patch is, TCL/Roku downgraded the speakers in the new R655 to only 10 watts!!
These 15 Watters are almost adequate. So TCL or ROKU have decided to basically Force you to buy one of their laggy sound bars for the R655. That was the straw that broke my dedication to the ROKU lineup after 5 iterations. (Note: The 75" version of the Google TV even has 20 watt speakers, just like the older Roku models).
- The only other semi-benefit of the R655 is the center TV stand. We typically purchase a fitueyes or other brand of Center stand for all of our tvs that has at least 8 height settings (instead of trying to find some type of oddly shaped bookshelf or huge entertainment table to place those crazy-wide R646 TCL bird legs on).
- We had already bought an extra center stand on sale, months before the R655 was introduced with its new center stand. (Of course, TCL kind of mucked that up as well giving you only 2 height adjustments.) So, at least now we have a good use for the stand we already have from Amazon.
- Upon finally getting the right price on the R646 and ready to pull the trigger, I was dissapointed to find that (in Oct '22, well before Christmas) Amazon's delivery options were 10 days away!
Unfortunately, even the local buy store had a 4 day pickup window! So we still had to wait a bit. It did actually arrive in 3 days.
- In addition, I had decided to purchase an extended warranty on this item. I am disappointed with Amazon's choices of ext warranty providers over the years, so we made the choice to buy from a local buy store where we can go in, check the condition of the pkg, pick it up and bring it home. The box had no dents or tears.
- The local warranty was much better. We were able to get a warranty for the next 5 years, which includes repairs at home.
- Fortunately, the local buy store matched Amazon's price within hours so we didn't even have to consider price!
- I have to admit, based on reviews, I Might have been dissapointed by this Google tv a year ago. They must have worked out most of the bugs since then. Now it's pretty stable and the new Roku line is the buggy one!
- I still despise the ad-driven Google interface.
I can only refer to it as a distraction from whatever you are trying to do. I have nothing good to say about the Google tv platform, sorry. Some menus go 5 or 6 levels deep. Things that I thought would be under TV settings are instead under User ID.
It seems every new version, the Ads just get bigger and bigger! They even make the icons of your favorite apps so small that you have to search the screen for them. Apps are front and center and the focus of Roku TV.
But Not on Google TV, it's ADs.
Plus, they change the appearance and location of everything as often as they can to keep you searching the screen for your apps, trying to focus you on their ADs. Roku interface is much much much friendlier.
Our next upgrade won't be until the 85" 8K micro-pixel true-black LCD model gets within our budget in a few years. So we wanted a good long warranty.
I used to use a 65" TCL R617 when I was traveling. It had a great picture and amazing brightness! This R646 provides everything that unit had and More of it! I am still searching for actual words to described the even-better-than-spectacular picture that the R646 provides.
Enjoy!!

title: I'm Impressed
text:
I think for the price, TCL cut reasonable corners. Somehow, 32-inch TVs now are "small TVs" and as such, are more appropriate for bedrooms. This is where I set up my TCL smart TV, and it goes perfectly. I have no complaints about the image quality. Sound quality from the built-in speakers won't blow you away, but it is perfectly fine for a bedroom. The sensitivity of the built-in TV tuner isn't anything to write home about, but it is far from the worst I've seen. There is no wired networking, but 1080p video streams over Wi-Fi just fine; you only really need wired networking to stream 4K, which this particular TV model doesn't support. I appreciate that TCL went with Roku for their Smart TV platform rather than trying to reinvent the wheel with their own thing. And other than a red TCL theme, the Roku experience is pretty stock too.

PROS
* Good picture and sound quality for its size and price.
* Near stock Roku software experience.
* Bloatware is removable. Or in many cases, you can even prevent installation of unneeded software in the first place.
* Easy to find and easy to understand signal meter when watching antenna TV.

CONS
* Wobbly legs even when fully screwed in.
* Roku remote is pretty limiting for watching antenna TV. There is no way to direct dial a channel number. You also can't dial RF numbers to manually pick up channels not picked up during the channel scan, so your only option is to run a rescan and hope none of the previously found channels is taken away.
* Roku remote has four shortcuts that can't be reassigned to apps you actually use, and you can't even disable these shortcuts. If you are watching live TV and you press one of those four shortcut buttons by accident, you'll be taken away from the channel you are watching without any confirmation.

I don't know how this TV will stand in the test of time, but so far I am impressed and would not hesitate to recommend the 32-inch 1080p TCL smart TV.

My idle temps now are low to mid 90s. One of my cores is showing 87 degrees! *TIP: Don't make the mistake of mounting the fan blowing air on the heatsink. You want it taking air away from it. Mount with the fan grill facing outward. I initially had the fan mounted the other way and was getting higher idling temps. Once I flipped it around, it was instantly cooler. I mounted the heatsink fan next to the rear exhaust fan.

I haven't tested temps with it during peak performance but I have no doubt it will perform better than the stock cooler, just by the huge amount of difference already.

The thing is a monster but fits in ATX case. Mounting it was really easy. Had it installed in less than 10 mins. I wished I'd had spent money on this sooner. Comes with a really nice magnetic screwdriver too :) Also, make sure all you case fans are working properly and there are no restrictions to the air flow as best you can (bulk cabling / obstacles). It makes a difference.

I will update at a later time when I start pushing the system harder, but untill then I believe it has been worth the money thus far.

title: Great little TV.
text:
I saw prior to ordering that this TV is noted for being somewhat fragile. Sure enough, despite handling it with great care, upon power up it was quite apparent that the screen was badly shattered. Front glass was intact. Damage was only visible on power up where the screen's backlighting shone thru the damaged area. Immediately contacted Amazon and got the replacement unit less that 24 hrs later.

The second unit arrived intact, and has been quite impressive. Great picture, and better sound than we expected for such a small TV. We already have a Roku stick on one of our TVs, but this TV with Roku integrated into it is far faster in Roku menus and program selection. We use it on the patio for baseball games and occasional TV watching, where it has been a big hit. Was pleasantly surprised to find our entire Spectrum Cable channel line-up was available as an app on the Roku menu, meaning we can watch TV over wifi, without a cable connection.

Only negative might be if you aren't or don't want to be a Roku customer. Signing into Roku or becoming a new Roku customer is pretty a much mandatory first step before using the TV. You do not have to register a credit card to do this, though this will speed up any later purchases.

title: Interesting little PC but misses the mark in several areas.
text: I purchased this product for a specific use case. I want a replacement for the underpowered RPi4 that could not handle the hardware processing I was using. I had high hopes that this little PC may accomplish the need. Unfortunately, there are several major issues upon receiving it. First, the Windows 11 inside the device is just a clone-copy from a working device (it is loaded with spyware and other nefarious programs). It is also not an active license. Thank goodness my home network is robust enough and blocked this hardware quickly. Second, the screen is configured for portrait mode (extremely difficult to make it go to landscape). I chose to wipe the device and install Ubuntu 20.04 on it instead. According to the images it is compatible. I would say it is 25% compatible, it installs. It has a lot of errors. Once again the screen rotation is an issue. Next, as others have said the power is a major issue. I understand using 12V but usea coaxial power plug like other 12V devices not a USB-C connector if you do not want to use standard USB-PD. Finally, this unit gets hot. It also throttles the processor due to heat. This makes it very difficult to use. Would like to have had some case options to add external fan, VESA mount, etc. I will continue to play with this as I believe it is a good form factor, just poorly designed. ***Absolutely zero support from the Chinese company that makes this product, zero documentation available, did find drivers but unknown if any are valid.***

text:
The battery lasts forever & the case acts as a power bank. So if you charge the buds in the case & get to 100% there is additional battery life in the charging case. I could not be happier with this purchase, these things are fantastic. title: it works OK - but hard to use
text:
I bought this primarily for cleaning areas at the back of my desk and dresser where dust accumulates. Unfortunately, I found that the negatives outnumbered the positives. Also, it's default mode is for use as a blower (which I really don't need); some minor disassembly is required to convert it to a vacuum cleaner and you will be on your own trying to figure out how to re-attach the very stiff hose to the back end for use as a vacuum. And, as another reviewer noted, disregard the instructions to plug in the power cord first. Plug it in only after you have every thing set up and ready to go.

Positives:
fairly compact
good blower power
bag is easy to get to and clean/exchange

Negatives:
1. noisy - I mean really noisy
2. short power cord - you will probably need an extension cord to use this
3. attachments fit extremely tight to the hose - you'll need to twist and put some oomph into it
4. very stiff hose - any movement of the hose and the machine will be flopping around on the floor
5. the hose is so stiff, it is almost impossible to store it in the included storage bag
6. baffling instructions on how to convert this from a blower to a vacuum cleaner - you're on your own to figure it out. Hint: don't unscrew the large ring that holds the assembly to the power unit. Pinch the filter with your thumb and forefinger and pull it out. Remove the small plastic gizmo in the center of the adapter and then you'll see where to attach the hose.
7. for such a noisy machine, the vacuum power is pretty weak. Much of the dust is simply picked up on the brush bristles and then you need to clean them when you're done.

title: Could be great if it delivered at release what it advertises
text:
Unfortunately, some of the biggest features that T-Rex 2 has advertised over its previous models is the custom training plans and the ability to import .gpx files for navigating routes are not available until late July. Which led me to return the item as so many tech companies over sell and under deliver on their products.

For what did work, the function was surprisingly good; very good in-fact! The T-REX 2 has responsive buttons to compliment an equally responsive touch screen coupled with a fluid well designed OS. A stand out feature was the accuracy of the sleep tracking which seemed to surpass my fitbit charge 5.

Aesthetically, I liked the rugged look of the watch with one exception on the bottom lug bar is an embossed white lettering "T-REX" which looks cheap and the watch band looks to be proprietary. I was unable to remove the band to confirms as the band is held by triangle screw heads on either side (I didn't have a driver to remove them).

Once the late July update hits, I would have no reservation recommending this watch based upon my experience and it's low price point. The functions of this watch sit somewhere between a Garmin Instinct 2 and a Fenix 7. The big deviation from a Fenix 7 is the T-REX 2 will only have breadcrumb routes to follow vs a full fledge map. Construction of this watch seems to be very well built, but I still believe long term that a Garmin product will outlast an Amazfit product. Finally, there is the concern of privacy as I believe Amazfit is a Chinese company that is also headquartered in China. Since I do not work at a sensitive location I really could care less who is monitoring my watch (time will tell if that is naive of me). Considering the price-point of these Amazfit devices it leads me to consider if a revenue model exist to profit from a users' data; then again maybe Garmin just charges a significant premium for their devices. Regardless, my choice is spending more for a Garmin as it delivers what is advertised from delivery and Garmin has a track record of lasting for many many years.
