title: A fantastic replacement for compressed air
text:
If you're like me, you've been looking for something to replaced compressed air cans for cleaning your computer. They're costly over time and short lived. This is what you're looking for.

Pros
- More power than a compressed air can
- Doesn't run out of air and will save you money in the long run
- Multiple nozzles for a variety of uses beyond computers

Cons
- Air/device heats up after a few minutes of use. While a desktop computer won't take that long to clean, this may be a concern if you're using it for other surfaces or devices.
- The nozzles do not click/slide into place. You push them onto the slot until they are snug. Nothing has shot off, but this does make me a little uneasy when aiming it at my computer's innards.

As for the noise, it's fine. It's quieter than a vacuum. I have sensitive ears and regularly *need* to wear earplugs at concerts and found this to be at an acceptable volume level. It's a motor that you plug in. It's not going to be silent.

All in all a fantastic product and something I should have bought a long time ago. Should they come out with a new version that improves on the two cons mentioned above (or even just the nozzles), it'd be a five star product for me.

text:
I bought this because the features listed were better than the smaller more portable projector I bought a few weeks ago. I bought them to compare as the more portable one is not as bright as I would like and the shadows can be pretty muddy. It's great for cartoons, but other media it's pretty lacking.

Now this device is slightly brighter, only just even though it's listed as being much brighter. The shadows are not as muddy, however the color and picture quality are seriously lacking on this thing. You have minimal picture adjustments and every setting and custom setting do not look good on this thing. I am returning this and keeping the more portable unit as it's way more convenient even if the picture isn't stellar. I'm actually kind of shocked how off the color and contrast is on this thing.

The sound is really awful. It does have options to use external speakers, but sometimes I don't want to bother with that. The small portable unit I bought actually has pretty decent sound for the price. The audio coming out of this projector is terrible. That is, if you can even get it to work half the time. Sometimes I was getting no sound at all.

Mounting - it has a 4 point mount bottom which doesn't work well for my tripod. The small unit I bought has a traditional tripod screw in the bottom center. With this I had to get a TV tray and laptop stand to get the picture where I wanted. Much bulkier and harder to place where I want it, especially in the bedroom where there is limited space.

All in all I'm pretty underwhelmed with it, and getting this has made me more impressed with the portable unit I already have.

If you don't mind pretty crappy picture quality and kind of awkward mounting for this thing, go for it. If you're looking for something more convenient with an picture closer to a TV I would keep shopping for something else.

I installed this on a Mazda CX-5, and overall it is doing the job. It does have some flaws and quality issues that should be pointed out.

First, as others have pointed out, the frame needs to be trimmed out to allow the wire to wrap around by the license plate. This is a silly oversight - there is NO WAY to route the wire that doesn't travel under this frame somehow, and if you ignore trimming the frame and just screw this down, you can pinch the video cable so badly that it would be damaged.

Second, at least in my case, the video output is skewed - it's almost as if the camera lens isn't straight in the camera. It's not bad enough to be unusable, but it's not squared the way one would expect - one side is skewed.

Finally, the wiring could be more considerate. The video cable included to run to the front of the vehicle has a full-side connector on each side, which is very challenging to push through the boot on most hatchback vehicles - it would be nice if on one side they included a smaller connector that was easier to push through.

Other than those issues, it does work, and the price is right.

title: Horizontal iPad Case
text:
I was looking for a new case for my wife’s Apple iPad 8th Generation because her current case, though protective, would not allow the iPad to stand up horizontally because the grooves that held the iPad were too short, and the iPad would slide out when in use. I couldn’t find a case that would stand up correctly. I did find cases that would stand horizontally, but they had a different configuration. This case was one of the options that I thought would work. However, it had a kids’ themed base, but that didn’t matter. We were hoping it would stand steady when we used it. Instead of grooves that the iPad would fit into, it had legs that opened in the back for a horizontal use, mainly at a desk, or on a table.

I got it last week, via Amazon, and I didn’t know what to expect: you can’t really tell quality from a picture. To my delight, the case was well made, and solid, with a dense red silicon rubber backing, and legs that easily opened toward the rear to support the iPad horizontally on your desk. Printed assembly instructions were included. To fit your iPad in the case, you remove the blue frame from the top, then place your iPad into the frame, and mount the iPad, now in the frame, into the case bottom. That’s it. At first, I wasn’t sure how the frame was removed, but it was simple. Just bend the red silicon rubber from the short side, and then lift the frame up and out. And, I wasn’t surprised to see how stable the iPad was on the desk in this case. And it was even stable resting on a bed. However, I was a little disappointed that the case did not come with a protective cover. But it worked well for our purpose. Also, a factor I consider when buying rubberized products is their odor. I'm sensitive to that stuff. Fortunately, the case did not have an odor.

title: Excellent Midrange Chromebook
text:
I've been a Chromebook user for 7 years. My old one hit its end of life, so I ordered this model a couple of months ago and have been using it daily.

Highlights:

- Excellent battery life. The best battery life I've personally experienced on a laptop. Can go a couple of days on a charge.
- It runs cool. No fans, so no fan noise.
- Nice big smooth Gorilla Glass track pad. Very nice. Premium feel.
- Aluminum top cover with chamfered edges. The rest of the body is plastic but solidly built.
- 8-Core ARM CPU with a 26K Octane Score, almost twice as fast as my previous Chromebook which already was sufficiently fast.
- 8GB Memory. Many other Chromebooks in this range have 4GB.
- The device will receive Chrome updates until June 2029. 7 years. Nice.
- Wi-Fi 6 wireless
- 2 USB-C ports, 1 USB 3.0 port.
- USB-C Charging
- Thin. Under 3 pounds
- Very good keyboard feel. Backlit keys.

Other features:

- The screen is Full HD, IPS. Nice, but could be brighter. No problem at all for indoor use. Not really bright enough for outdoor (I tested it,) although the matte screen is helpful there.
- Headphone jack is there if you need one.
- The Chromebook comes with basic travel sleeve. Nice perk.
- The 720p Webcam is nothing spectacular but will get you through meetings
- Storage is a 64GB eMMC, not an SSD, but it seems fast and I have no issue with it.

Not necessarily negatives but worth mentioning:

- No HDMI slot. I don't really need HDMI anymore because Chromebooks can wirelessly cast the screen to my Chromecast. Or it can cast YouTube to my Roku. Beyond that there's always a USB-C to HDMI cable I could purchase if needed.
- No SD card slot. Would be nice to expand storage if needed in the future, but I suppose a USB flash drive could be used instead.

Could be better:

- Speakers - I guess I was spoiled by my Toshiba Chromebook 2 with fairly robust laptop speakers, because these Acer speakers, while up-firing, lack any bass and with music can be tinny sounding at times. They do have good stereo separation though. For voice, they're good and clear. But for music I will be bluetoothing to my external speaker or wireless headphones most of the time.

Summary:

Overall an excellent mid-range Chromebook! Highly recommended.

Update - November 2022: As I see other reviews have noted, occasionally the laptop will not connect to wi-fi when you first turn it on. Rebooting it resolves the problem and luckily Chromebooks reboot very quickly. (The issue does not occur when waking the laptop from sleep.)

Update - March 2023: The wi-fi connection issue has not occurred in a month or so, so it seems like they fixed it with a software update!

title: Useful and compact - UPDATED: no power after 5 months
text:
It's always a nuisance to unplug power, hub, mic, ethernet and external display even on the newest M1 MBPs. It's a laptop and it should be portable. One connection port... that is the dream... I have another USB-C dock that I tried for a few weeks that I really liked, but it got a little too warm and its fan was too loud for continuous use. This one looked like a better option.

This is a very compact hub when compared to other full size docks. However, it's larger than simple USB-C hubs. There are enough ports to cover most all daily use cases.

It comes in a flimsy paper box with a concise foldout instruction for installing its driver (that you'll likely not need) and... that's it. From the packaging, I would not have guessed it'd cost as much as it does.

The main different in this device that other less expensive options offer is to have ethernet, a USB-C data port and two HDMI ports (one 4K@60Hz and second 4K@30Hz). I can't express how useful the USB-C data hub is. And, at this price point, 4K@60Hz is expected to just work.

Setting up is fairly straight forward as there are no drivers that to install, but it does include one (built-in... shows up in desktop as an external drive). For Mac OS I didn't need to install anything for the displays to work. I double checked that I am running at 60 Hz in HDMI1.

However, I could not get the Ethernet configurations to appear in System Preferences. I had to contact tech support.

The strange thing is that, even though the hardwired network LAN port was not appearing as configurable, the laptop is clearly online. So the port does work. After tech support replied (within half a day), at first, it appeared to be a generic reply, but it did contain a link to an article that actually had the step-by-step configurations. In short, I manually added a USB 10-100-1000 LAN configuration and "Applied" and it all worked after a quick restart.

Finally, temperature, does this hub get too warm? It gets warm and it does not have an internal fan as far as I can tell. I measured it to run continuously at around 115˚F on a cool day.

I wish it had a longer USB cord or that it was detachable, because I found it to be a bit too awkward right next to my MBP. Using a USB-C high-bandwidth extension, I have have this hub sitting on my desk at a comfortable distance from the laptop and close enough for me to reach to add a microSD card without having to stand up.

UPDATE:
It has not been a full 5 months since I've been using this hub/dock and it is not completely unresponsive. I contact support, who were willing to, via ZenDesk ticket, send me instructions to do usual power cycling and other troubleshooting, but the device is, as I said, unresponsive.

At this point, since it's an Amazon order, we can only do the manufacturer RMA process for a repair under warranty. This means I have to pay to ship the unit to Fremont, CA and wait for a repair/replacement.

This has been an ok dock that I used almost every day. For something priced at this tier, I'd expect it to last at least a couple of years.

Quite unfortunate... I would not recommend it...

title: In this case, you DO get what you pay for
text:
I give up. How do you find a decent-sounding pair of earbuds that will last at least two years? I've bought DOZENS. If they're expensive and sound great, one earbud inevitably fails. Fast. If they're inexpensive, the sound quality is so poor you don't want to use the earbuds. I thought I'd try these out to see if I could replace my expensive bluetooth earbuds whose battery just died. These have such a tinny sounding treble that I can't understand what speakers are saying (movies, music). The bass is decent and the volume gets higher than my bluetooth sets' volumes, but the sound quality is so muddy that I know I'd use these only in emergencies.

The sound also doesn't have a natural stage. The left earbud gets far more of the sound. If you increase the volume to hear out of the right earbud, the left earpiece distorts.

What a shame. I thought at this price, I'd have a backup pair of earbuds while I research a day-to-day version. But I would rather listen to nothing than struggle through trying to understand what's being said through these. Another knock against these inexpensive buds is poor fit. They keep falling out of my ears. You get only one pair of ear inserts with these, so if they don't fit your ears, you're out of luck. On the bright side, the ear inserts these buds come with pop off easily so you can try putting on other inserts--which is what I did with my now dead BT headset's comfort inserts.

Overall, I don't recommend these earbuds. The most important feature of headphones is sound quality. If the sound is so poor as to make you uncomfortable or make words unintelligible, nothing else matters about the headphones.

title: Outstanding Wireless Sound Quality With Great Noise Reduction
text:
This is a great-sounding full sized headset with excellent bass. Of four Bluetooth headsets that I tested recently (including the Ankbit E600 which I also really like), this one with sound cancelling is my new favorite. Right from the start, the packaging for these is excellent, on a par with what I’ve come to expect from Apple and leaving a great first impression. The goodness just continues from there. Pairing with the Bluetooth transmitter I bought for my receiver was seamless, and I was listening to a movie in seconds. The earcups are large and create such a good seal on my head that there’s actually a bit of low-pressure suction that required a bit of repositioning and getting used to. However, once in place the audio experience is absolutely outstanding — the “Deep Bass” delivers as advertised for a truly immersive listening experience. The control buttons are in an accessible position that don’t get bumped when putting these on, and lettering on the controls is small but legible. The active noise cancelling (ANC) is great, with an additional setting that will reduce environmental noise but still let you hear if someone speaks to you. My single complaint is that these headphones do not provide an equalizer, though the balance between bass and treble is excellent and the bass provides a deep, rich sound without being overpowering. These don’t have quite the range of my Ankbit E600 headset, dropping the signal when I step outdoors and put two walls between them and my computer. However, inside my single story house I’ve got pretty good coverage throughout.

The bottom line: Recommended. Even if you pay a bit more compared to other brands, you’ll be glad you did every time you use them.

title: Installing backup camera
text:
My car didn't come with a backup camera and after reading an article on how a dad ran over his kid, I decided it is really a must and did some research on installing one myself.

There's a youtube video by Cars & Driver on installing a backup camera, but every car is a little different, so before buying everything, I would advise to check out your car and envision how you would put everything together. I spent $100 total make it happen:

Morris Products 10772 Quick Splice Connector, Red, 22-18 Wire Range
- It worked well! The difficult part is making sure the wire is in the right places before clamping down with a plier. Once all the way down, the wire is really tight in there. I used this to splice the power from one of the reverse light on the trunk.

E-PRANCE New Car Door Clip Panel Audio Video Dashboard Dismantle Kits Installer Pry Tool
- Could not have removed the stupid trunk lid liner without this tool and also a small flat head screw driver. The trunk lid liner is held on by 8 black plastic round clip and to remove them without breaking the plastic round clips, you need to discover where to push in with the flat head screw driver by probing under the clip. The location is found when you can stick the flat head deeper than everywhere else. The two sides are usually vertical or horizontal and once found, just shove in the screw driver and one of the very narrow but flat prong to pop it out!

INNOVA 3300 Hands-free Digital Multimeter (10 MegOhm)
- Had to use this to find where to get the power source for the LCD Screen. I did not like this for the car because the prong is not narrow enough to stick into really tight spot.

Esky® EC170-09 Waterproof High Sensitive Color CMOS Black Aluminum Alloy Universal Car License Plate Frame Mount Rear View Backup Camera
- The camera is really nice and the frame is nice too. There is are built in indicator lines for distances that's not removable. Fish eye camera lense is also really nice. My only issue is that there doesn't seem to be a way to stop the camera from freely rotating other than the wire sticking out stops it. The length of the wire is also a small issue; it was ok for my car as it's the right length to go through the plastic of the license plate lighting fixture. But I can see it an issue if it needed to be longer.

4.3 Inch LCD TFT Rearview Monitor screen for Car Backup Camera
- I wish the wires coming out of the LCD Screen was much longer, but it wasn't. The picture is very accurate in its portrayal, so it's not a problem.

2.4g Wireless Color Video Transmitter and Receiver for the Vehicle Backup Camera/front Car Camera
- Works very well for short distance of a normal car. The transmitter heats up very fast though, and I worry it may break down with the amount of heat it produces. ... I'm scared of if and when it breaks as I don't like the idea of going back in to fix it.

**** Installation on 2015 Volvo S60 ****

1) 20 minutes just trying to get the trunk lid liner off. The black clips were really hard to remove, but once I figured it out, it was just a process of getting to the side of the clips and pushing in the right way. There is also the trunk latch plastic cup thing that pulls right off. A trunk holder thing that has two plastic clips that needed a good push from the back side that I didn't do appropriately (and broke the clip). A trunk release handle that is attached to a steel cable that needed some finessing to remove.

2) 10 minutes on unscrewing the license plate lighting fixture. I needed some special Torx screw driver and it was almost not the right size. Eventually, it came out easily when the screws were all out.

3) 30 minutes to connecting the *RIGHT* 2.4 ghz transmitter to the license plate camera and stuff it in the space inside the trunk. What's nice is the transmitter has the plugs to power the camera and to receive the 1 yellow RCA feed. So, I had to thread the transmitter cable into the trunk through the license plate lighting fixture. Then, to power the transmitter, I found the red/black wire for the reverse light on the left side of the trunk lid. My wife had to come to put car in reverse for me to verify the right cables to use. I used the splice things to splice the cables together, very fast!

4) For the front, I stuck the LCD screen to the dash, ran the cable on the side, and connected the power lines together with a cigarette lighter car adapter. I utilized an old cigarette car adapter that I wasn't using anymore, cut the wires, stripped, and lashed it all together.

Now, I have a backup camera for just about $100!

** EDIT 19 June 2014 **

How to fix static / flickering picture 5 seconds after going into reverse:

After I installed everything, I thought it was all working wonderfully. After the weekend, when I actually went to drive the car, I discovered the rearview camera would go from clear to fuzzy and flickering within 5 seconds. With some research, I discovered that this is due to the reverse light is not powered by full 12 VDC after the car is in reverse for a few seconds. The fix for this is to install a relay ASIN B000PHLQJW:

http://www.amazon.com/Parts-Express-Waterproof-Relay-Bracket/dp/B000PHLQJW/

The connection for the relay is as follows:

Red (Power) from the cigarette lighter connected to 30
Black (Ground) from cigarette lighter connected to 85
Reverse Power (Red) from reverse light connected to 86
Camera Power (Red) from backup camera connected to 87
Camera Ground (Black) from backup camera connected to 85

After I did this, the camera stopped flickering and everything is working as intended ~ so far anyways.

title: Power without the price
text:
I chose JBL over all the other brands and bluetooth speakers that I was looking at, including the HomePod Mini from Apple and was rewarded with a speaker that I am more than pleased to have.

I was looking for a Bluetooth speaker for the office that could be charged by USB-C, provide a better experience than my phone speakers, and have the sound be really soft so that others walking by my work office wouldn't hear, and when they would enter my office, we can carry a conversation without me having to turn off my speaker. The JBL provides that experience, coupled with the iPhone to get granular volume control. Now, I can have an ambience that suits my workflow. All I have to do is fire up Apple Music, Spotify, Podcast, or my favorite radio station.

Exciting part is that when I am playing my music on the phone and the JBL isn't turned on, the moment that I do turn the speaker on, my iPhone switches the music to the speaker. It works flawlessly. As it is supposed to do!

The quality of sound is representative of the JBL brand. I was concerned about the size of the speaker, but JBL did really well with providing a speaker that is competitive with all the other Bluetooth speakers - making it a no-brainer to get this one.

JBL brand is important to me. My GF had a JBL speaker that she plugged into her computer in the early 2000's (wires to each speaker, power cord, and another wire to the computer - what a mess) and I enjoyed listening to music belting out from those speakers. She is a music enthusiast and because of her experience with JBL, that is the brand that she prefers. For Christmas two years ago, I got her JBL Flip 5 to replace the older wired speakers and she absolutely loves it and I love the sound coming from it, also!

How does this compare with the Flip 5? I think the Flip 5 has more bass and obviously will fill a larger room with sound. It's great for outdoors when you have a lot of activity, noise, kids screaming, etc. The Flip 5 would have worked for my office at work, but the JBL Go 3 is actually better as it is smaller, I don't need to have the music pumped up (although it can be loud!), and I can place it anywhere in the office, or put it in my coat pocket and bring it home for the weekend. It is more versatile.

The HomePod Mini was a preferred speaker as I love the extended features. I thought long and hard about getting one for the office (I have two at home) but I just couldn't see putting an Apple speaker in a work officer environment.

I looked at all the other brands on Amazon. In the end, it was the JBL brand, the quality that I could expect (and that came true), the price (very reasonable) and the size. I am more than thrilled with my purchase. It works seamlessly with my iPhone.

title: Day 1 - excellent router so far. Will update.
text:
Upgraded from the Archer C3150 V1 (which was an upgrade from another TP Link router before that). Excellent upgrade. Set it up yesterday in about 3 min. I am an IT Professional for a living, so yes, my opinion on what's "simple" might not be the same as others. But that said, I imagine the interface was so simple anyone could set it up in less than 10 min. It walks you through everything. My 3 min included custom settings and port forwards, virtual servers, VPN, the works lol. Simple setup is great for beginners but if you're looking for more advanced features like these just click advanced and go to town.

My old C3150 did a solid job for 4 years, but recently started having issues. The 5Ghz would almost never work, and the router needed rebooted once a day ish. I don't hold this against TP Link tho, because I have had Netgear, Asus, Lynksys, TP Link, you name it, I've worked with it either at home or at work, trust me, they ALL go bad eventually. From my experience, TP Link has the smoothest firmware, the longest life (4-8 years for me so far), and most reliable connection. The main reason I started with TP Link at home 12 years ago was because it was the only brand that gave me the FULL speed that my ISP was sending me. I pay for 1 Gig, and on a TP Link, I get 1 Gig.

Anyways, signal around the house is significantly stronger with this than with my old Archer C3150. Ranch style house, router is on far end (worst spot ever, but best I could do). Old router would only get the 2.4 G to other side of house, with about 10Mbps on my phone. This one blasts all three bands strongly all the way out the other end of the house lol. 400Mbps on my phone standing right by the router (Samsung Note 20, non-ultra), and 150Mbps when I'm aaaaall the way on the other end of the house in the bedroom with the door shut. 100Mbps out the garage and on the sidewalk. House is ranch just under 2000 square feet. So distance/wall wise it's about the same as a 3500 sq ft 3 level house. This thing will do just fine in any average house. My basement is not counted in that sq ft and still gets perfect signal.

Good thing about this router is is works with TP Link mesh ad ons, so if I ever decide I need an extender I can get one later. Pretty sure I won't tho.

All in all, great start to a hopefully long 5 or 6 years with this router. Again, I only got it yesterday. If anything changes I promise to update this review right away.

title: Not for listening to crisp music. Perfect for phone calls.
text: These are not something an audiophile is going to be picking up to really appreciate their music. The use case is entirely when you want to be able to hear external sound but still completely hear music/calls as well. Think running on public roads, talking while driving, or listening to music in a collaborative group environment. The bone conduction concept is really a thing as you can hear the sound get better once they are against the side of your head. That said about the best you can hope for is a slightly muddied sound devoid of highs and bass really just ends up tickling the skin around where it sits. That's just the result of sending the sound into your head this way instead of the normal one. Where these really shine is when you need to be on a call but hear your surrounding environment. You can clearly hear the person on the other end and the mic works well enough that they hear you just fine too. Once you've tempered your expectations about sound quality these are a decent product. Very light to the point you could forget you were wearing them. If you want them while exercising and need to hear possible approaching cars the good news is they stay in place no matter how much you move. The main body is a basic plastic with the transducers being covered with a firm rubber and the same material covering the band around back. Controls are basic but easy to locate and use with raised buttons well spaced behind your right ear. I like them for specific situations but consider what you're looking for as they're not just another pair of headphones.

title: Very, very basic
text:
This is as basic a laptop as you're going to find, so if that's what you're looking for, this might be ideal. The HD is only 32gb and there's just 2gb of Ram. So essentially, you're really not going to be able to download tons of stuff onto here, including a large iTunes library, if you have one. The screen is small, comparable to a Chromebook, but the quality is surprisingly sharp and bright. I've streamed Netflix and Amazon Video with zero issues, so that's a major plus. This comes with Windows 8.1, but you should check for updates right away, because there will be some. Since it does have a full operating system, you can use Microsoft Office with this, which makes this a great laptop for a student. It's very thin and lightweight and it's actually a pretty attractive laptop. There are no additional drives on this, so that's something to consider and the battery life is not the greatest, though that's comparable to almost all entry-level laptops. I have 2 Samsung Chromebooks and personally I prefer those to this. I'm fine with a Windows based system, but this laptop lacks so much that I just prefer to use the Chromebook for daily tasks. I will probably give this to my daughter soon, as she enjoys playing games, and also, in our Elementary School, kids are required to do certain work typed out on a computer.

Lenovo is a great brand, and I prefer it over HP and Dell (the worst) so I'm hopeful this laptop will last a few years with no issues. For the price, it really can't be beat for a Windows laptop and would also make a nice gift for a student.

title: Best for little kids. Standard tablet features, with added parental controls.
text:
This is a very cute Android tablet in a super-flexible case with child-sized handles. I'd say it's a good tablet for a five-to-seven year old.

The blue, silicone case may not make this completely unbreakable, but pretty close. Dropped on a hardwood floor or cement, the case (with the tablet securely inside it) simply bounces a bit. No breakage. (The tablet also comes with a five-year warranty.)

The tablet comes with instructions for the many ways parents can monitor and control how much children can use the tablet. For example, it's password-protected. Also, you can set it so your child can use it just a certain number of hours per day. As parents, we appreciate that.

You'll need to be familiar with typical Android features and settings. Also, the on/off button is at the upper right corner, on top, and raised but not a separate color. (It took my husband and me at least half an hour to figure that out. lol )

The only modification we made immediately was to cover the camera in the center of the cute face on the holder. (Fortunately, that lens is where a nose would be. Covering it - for privacy - was easy and didn't look at all weird afterward.) There's a second lens on the reverse side of the tablet, and you may want to cover that, too.

Other than that, you may want to change some of the app settings, such as YouTube and Netflix, but that's pretty standard on any tablet.

With access to all the usual Google apps, including Google Play and educational games, this can be a good, safe way to introduce a young child to tablets, computers, and the digital world in general.

And besides, it's really cute. Every time I look at it, I smile.

The camera behaved as though it was going to connect, but it just spun and never connected to the app, so again, I'm stuck with another insecure app for each separate camera that I'm testing. Ugh.

Anyway, these cameras require you to grant them (at least during the setup) full access to your phone and home network. The latest camera I tested even requires you to give it full access to notifications on your phone as well.

All that aside, the app interface is slow to connect to the camera, so if you get an alert on motion and want to look at it live, whatever you want to look at will be long gone by the time the app connects to the camera. It literally took 30 seconds to connect to the app each time I wanted to use live view. Not very realistic for that aspect of a surveillance camera setup. I also assumed, because it has two antenna on the sides, that the wireless signal would be great, but it's actually worse than other cameras I've tested that have no external antennas. Weird.

Overall, I'm not very impressed with this camera.

title: Great Quality and Easily Installed
text:
This review only applies to the solar security camera sold by Hose US. This is my fifth security camera from various makers. All of the features listed in the ad work properly as expected. Camera easily pairs with the application and seems to have very good Wi-Fi reception.

Beyond those features, I was immediately impressed by the robustness of the camera compared to previous ones; it doesn’t feel like a toy like the others. This camera also has better insulation from water than the others I bought. There is a good seal around the USB connector used to interface the solar panel which is very important. The solar panel itself seems like good quality. The ease of installation is well thought out. Instead of the body of the camera having to be installed directly, there are brackets for both the camera and solar panel. The brackets make it much safer and easier to install when you’re high up on a ladder. Just install the bracket first then the camera is secured by both a terminated slot and a machine screw; very easy and secure. The solar panel’s mount is also well thought out with the ability to easily point the panel in the desired direction and angle. There is at least 10 feet of good quality cable to go from the panel to the camera providing a lot of installation flexibility

So far, very impressive. The picture shows both the camera and solar panel up around 20 feet. I am thoroughly satisfied with my purchase.

The constant alerts continued. Being hearing impaired, I use an Apple Watch with haptic alerts so I can be alerted of things most people would hear. I chatted with Wyze several times trying to troubleshoot the camera. They had me reboot it several times, delete and reinstall the app. Nothing worked. The last agent I chatted with said it was probably a firmware issue, that should be fixed when a new app update was released and I should just wait for that to happen. WTH? I was close to the end of my return window, so I ended up returning the camera. Although the chat agents tried to be helpful, I was never offered a replacement camera, which leads me to believe this is a known issue and other camera of the same model will do the same thing.
Back to the drawing board.

title: Impressive performance and speed with included AC Adapter
text:
I have a PC (Acer) that has a 3.1 Gen 2 USB & and a C connector conveniently located on the front for easy access. The problem is...they never stay connected to anything plugged in. The only thing I could get to work was a Sandisk USB reader for a Micro SD card. The C connector never worked. I never understood why but just continued using the 2 USB 3.0 connectors on the back.

I was wanting to plug in more devices to those connectors instead of swapping them regularly, so I purchased this amazing device. I specifically wanted a powered hub because I knew I wanted to use 2 external HDD's and 1 external SSD and knew they didn't produce enough power to drive them. When I selected this on Amazon, it said it "found" 2 bundles with this device. Thinking maybe I could get a better deal while also adding a C hub, I looked at them. They are not the same because the "bundles" offered have no AC adapter so neither is powered. Don't be tricked into getting something that won't work for you. I'm sure Amazon isn't doing that on purpose. I fault the seller. The model number for both devices is identical, but one comes with the AC adapter (what I wanted and needed) and one doesn't.

Questions and reviews for this product are confusing since some say it DOES come with the AC adapter while others argue it does NOT. They're both right. Make sure you're ordering what you want. There's no reason to have this hub without the AC adapter. It might connect to your devices, but not anywhere near their rated speeds. On gaming, it would cause the dreaded latency. I'm not a gamer but my system is set up like I am because of the business software I need.

After reading many reviews of various products, I wondered if the front 3.1 Gen 2 connectors weren't working due to lack of power. When I received this hub, I excitedly plugged it into the front USB 3.1 Gen 2 and everything is working lightning fast! There isn't a connectivity issue and all drives are running at their top rated speeds! Two of those drives are for USB 3.1 Gen 2 and even came with the cables but they've never performed anywhere close to what they should being plugged into USB 3.0 outlets. I even connected my new iPhone 13 Pro Max and it stayed connected and even fast charged it! Not to overstate things, but this is lifechanging!

I was concerned about the AC adapter not fully plugging in to the hub. Pics and vids clearly show it sticking out some. While many might not think it really matters, here's why it's extremely important for it to engage fully in.

1) The power it produces is plenty enough to cause issues if anything comes into contact with it. That could lead to damage to anything plugged in and to what it's plugged in to (ie your computer), and also there’s a potential for fire.

2) Power cords produce EM interference which can affect electronics including Bluetooth and Wi-Fi signals. That's why the cables are double and triple shielded to prevent that from occurring. That 1/8" that's sticking out isn't shielded at all! I even saw a review saying they couldn't use it because of the interference. That's why.

I had asked a question about that and the seller responded that they'd fixed it even though it really was ok for them to stick out, also saying there might be a few old ones left in the warehouse so if I did get one of those, they'd exchange it. Fortunately, mine was one of the fixed ones.

I believe Amazon should force the seller to replace for free all the AC adapters that aren't safe. Hopefully the right people will read this and solve this liability issue before equipment starts getting damaged or fires are caused (electricity + combustible materials = fire).

As others have stated, each plug can be switched on/off. They've brilliantly put it on the side so it's not accidentally pressed. Besides, turning it on requires only a touch, but turning it off requires holding it for two full seconds, eliminating what could be a costly mistake (data can be lost or damaged if you don't properly eject it). There's been no heat from it, and I put it through its paces. It's attractive, small and has two rubber-type strips on the bottom that keep it from sliding around. I highly recommend this hub by Rosonway and am now ordering their C hub (with the AC adapter, of course).

title: Heavy Duty And A Flexible Socket Arrangement
text:
This five foot extension cord uses 14AWG cable with strong stress reliefs on both ends. It has six 120V outlets and three basic USB outlets - two type-A and one type-C for providing power. The USB power is limited to 2.4A on each socket with a combined amperage limit of 3.4A when more than one USB socket is in use.

What is particularly useful is the way the AC power outlets are arranged to accommodate the many adaptor shapes and sizes allowing access to all six of the sockets. The power strip can accomodate almost any combination of 120VAC plug and adaptor shapes. Two indicator lights confirm the the circuit is grounded and protected.

This extension cord/power strip is for indoor, dry area use only. A long list of restrictions includes prohibiting operation in possibly damp areas and use to power medical equipment. Most puzzling, the BN-LINK Surge Protector safety instructions have printed in bold, all caps: "THIS IS NOT A SURGE PROTECTOR", in spite of listing it as a surge protector in the advertising and on the front page of the user instructions.

That aside, I am finding this extension cord/power strip very useful around the house, due to its plug configuration and heavy duty construction.

As I was a complete beginner I found this telescope to my liking. It came in a nice shoulder bag, and I was able to pretty easily figure out how to assemble it and begin use.

No, the viewfinder didn't seem to line up perfectly, and no, the phone attachment was a little clumsy to use, but for sub $100 I now have a telescope that I can actually use, and that I didn't have to invest too much in.

title: Compact
text:
It is more compact than I expected it to be. That's a good thing.

There is nothing wrong with it; no defects or problems. But I should have paid closer attention to the specs. I have a MacBook Pro 2021, which is not officially supported. If you have a Mac, even if it is officially supported, you may be disappointed by the video limitations. If you are running MacOS, you cannot have more than two independent monitors via this product. That is, you can extend over only two screens, while a PC can extend over three screens. Mirroring is no problem, but who wants to do that?

I won't mention the VGA. No one uses that anymore. So you effectively have the two HDMI outputs. On Macs, you can either have UHD from a single monitor, or two monitors running HD resolution. That's sort of like VGA. These days, it's important to be able to support multiple UHD monitors.

So, while this is a quality docking station, its capabilities are limited.

title: Great little tv for the price!
text: Ordered the 32” 1080p ROKU smart tv on Tue. evening and it arrived today (Sun.). Set up was pretty easy, although my son did come over and lend a hand as neither my husband nor I are that technologically savvy, and we still had it set up and running in less than an hour. In addition to ROKU, we also have it connected to Dish, and with three HDMI ports there is even room to connect our fire stick, so plenty of options for entertainment. A sound bar can also be connected but it really is not needed with this tv. I see myself cutting the cord in the near future. The picture quality is great and the sound is also for a tv this size. I set it at 18 (less than a quarter of the way up) and it was plenty loud enough to hear. The only con for me so far is the ROKU remote does not have a numeric keypad so you have to scroll through the channels until you find the one you want, but I was aware of this when I purchased the tv. Oh, and FYI, you DO NOT have to pay ANYTHING to set up an account with ROKU! It is absolutely free to set this up. There is plenty of free content but you will need a card number if you wish to purchase any of the paid content. If you do not wish to enter your credit card info all you need to do is scroll through to the bottom of the page without inputting that info and click where it says “skip this”. You will still have access to all of their free services. I hesitated buying this as there seemed to be a number of instances where the product was received with cracked or shattered screens but I decided to take a chance and am very glad I did. It was packed very well, with a protective cover over the screen and styrofoam casing around the tv, all packed snug in it’s box and with no damage to the packaging or contents when it arrived. Would highly recommend this tv at this time and will update if any issues arise.

title: Awesome Smart Watch
text:
For the money, this is an awesome smart watch that has some of the same popular features as that “fruit” brand.
The watch was packaged securely in a box and included a User Manual and a “How to Connect with the smart watch” brochure.

My watch was received with 46% battery life and did not need to be charged immediately, but I noticed that the charge cord is magnetic and attaches easily to the back of the watch.

I read the instructions and powered on the watch. I downloaded the app and proceeded to pair, referred to as “bind” in the manual. The smart watch paired effortlessly with my iPhone 13. Other than pairing or unpairing, the user manual doesn’t cover much else, but I found the watch use to be intuitive. I do think a more detailed user manual would be helpful to explain navigating and swipe direction of the screens.

The watch has many functions and I was pleasantly surprised that the watch provided a “Siri connection” and performed flawlessly. I compared the blood pressure and oxygen sensors to my individual monitors to check accuracy. Surprisingly, the watch is pretty accurate.

As I mentioned earlier, I started using the watch with 46% battery life and wore the watch for approximately 25 hours before I received a low battery alert.

This is a great buy and so much so, that within hours of using my watch, I ordered another one for my husband.

The touch screen is responsive, and the colors are vivid. We had no issues with connecting Bluetooth devices, surfing the internet, email, and all non-gaming applications. We did experience latency and speed issues when trying to load games such as Pokémon Go. The device will play games, however, the experience will be too choppy to enjoy on more resource-intensive games like Pokémon.

We will use this tablet primarily for internet, streaming movies and as an E-reader. The tablet is slower than we need for certain games but a nice tablet for day to day use. Four stars.

title: Sticks out a little bit and not flush to my wall
text:
So the product is great - the amount of outlets it gives you as well of the position of them, you can tell someone really spent some time developing / taking into consideration what consumers need. The reversed orientation on some of the plugs was a really nice idea for those extra large wall warts.

The plug itself is well built, sturdy and feels of good quality. It's nice that they also included a screw to bolt it to the outlet. I'm admittedly slightly surprised that the back of the charger does not use both wall outlets. What it does is uses one, but places a plastic stabilizer into the other. I have images in my head of the movie A Christmas Story where they show tons of items connected to the same outlet, but I guess in this case it is ok to do so.

Lastly, as I said mine unfortunately does not sit flush to my wall, this is not a fault of the product, but of how my outlet is in my wall. My outlet sticks out ever so slightly past the wall and face plate. Because of this, when removing the plate and putting this on instead, I have about 2-3mm of gap between the charger and my wall. It would have been nice if this was flush, but it is what it is. Oh yea, and lastly when I took off my face plate, I found out that my outlet is cracked in half, figures. Whelp, I'll be replacing the outlet for sure before committing to using the charger long term.

Overall though for the design, the outlet orientations and just the overall quality and feel, it's a great product for the price.

title: It's not perfect, but I believe it's the best out there.
text:
I had a Ghostcover on my 2017 MBP for over 4 years. It got cloudy slowly over time, but it never warped or got stiff. Typing was a breeze and it kept my keyboard working WAY longer than most 2017 models because dust/dirt couldn't get into the mechanisms. I got a new MBP this year and chose the tinted cover this time around. It looks great on the keyboard and fits perfectly; however, it's not as good of an experience.

Because the newer macs have taller keys, the ghostcover has to bend a lot more to depress the keys. This is a much poorer typing experience than with my old macbook. It feels gummy and it's so easy to mistype. There isn't really anything wrong with the keyboard cover itself, it's more just the way the new macs are designed.

I use a mechanical keyboard 90% of the time, and you're really not supposed to use keyboard/camera covers with these new macs anyways. I only keep the cover on when I'm working at my desk and the computer is open. I try my best to remove the cover anytime I shut the laptop, but the couple of times I've forgotten the screen has been fine. I don't use it at all when I'm on the go and relying on the Macbook keyboard for typing.

Overall I still think it's the best keyboard cover you can get for Macs and it's already kept a lot of dust and cat hair out of my lovely new machine. If you plan to keep this on 24/7 though you're going to be disappointed.

title: AVOID if you're a Mac user with USB-Cs!
text:
I bought this to eliminate the echo my previous USB webcam caused because it didn't have speakers, only a mic and camera. What a mess! I only discovered after troubleshooting that the manufacturer doesn't recommend using this with a USB extender, which anyone on a newer Mac laptop with USB-C ports is relegated to by default.

While the camera and speakers work, the mic constantly cuts in and out, and freezes Finder every time I try to play around in System Preferences. I've tried this with two different USB-C adapters, in all four of my laptop's ports, thinking it might have been that but it's not. (One was an Apple make, one was by QGeeM for reference.) Went back to my previous $45 webcam, and I'll have to be more vigilant about muting right after I'm done speaking so I don't send feedback from my speakers back on through.

TL;DR save your money and buy something cheaper and more reliable.

title: Great picture quality for the price, loud and clear (single) speaker, quick and easy to setup
text:
[[VIDEOID:eb2ee0ce934f5fd0d2c278dce60c361d]] For the price, this projector is fantastic! We use it for playing games on Nintendo Switch, streaming content from an Amazon Fire Stick, streaming content from an iPad (requires an adapter) and from a laptop.

The speaker (not speakers) is loud and clear and works great on its own, but it's only ONE speaker, not TWO as needed for stereo sound. It's a good thing that the speaker is loud and clear because the fan produces a very audible and annoying hum; like coarse white noise.

Video quality, clarity, color reproduction and brightness are good overall. But the claim of 15,000 lumens is doubtful as it can't easily be proven what the actual output is. As a comparison test, I borrowed a projector from work, an Epson Powerlite 1781W (~3x the cost of WEWATCH and rated at 3,200 lumens) displayed the same content from the same source and you can see that the WEWATCH is not nearly as bright, colors not nearly as vibrant, but video quality is about the same.

The controls on the top of the projector allow you to access the projector's settings, but it's not very intuitive so keeping the remote handy will save you a lot of time. The remote itself works well, but the range is limited to direct line of sight to either black sensor on the front or back of the projector. You can't really deviate too far from aiming directly at the black dots (IR receiver) or the remote will do nothing. In the projector's menu there are many settings to adjust color temperature, zoom, shape, volume, etc. ; but one thing I have noticed is that when reducing the screen zoom to below 100% (to fit a projector screen for example), the settings menu still displays at full 100% size even when whatever you're displaying is say 70%. It just makes it difficult to view the full menu options when a portion of the output is cutoff outside the viewable area.

Compatibility wise, it has worked with everything I've used to send output to the projector. Using the Amazon Fire Stick and its far-reaching remote has been the easiest to manage content, but you still need the projector remote to control the volume. Using an Apple Airplay device (iPad, iPhone, etc) with an adapter to HDMI was the only time I had to fiddle with connections. Occasionally, the projector would stop displaying the video but continue to play the audio. To fix this, I just needed to stop/start playing and reconnect cables.

I had the older version of these for 3 years, the S8. I had to get new ones, because after daily use they finally stopped charging and working.
I bought these in hopes they'd be as reliable as the previous ones, sadly, not so. These frequently don't charge in their case, leaving me with dead earbuds when I'm expecting full batteries. The contacts from earbud to case are clean and cleaned frequently. Currently one stops charging while I write this because my typing causes the slightest bounce.
Another dislike is the extra tasks the the one button on the ear does. The old ones, tapping the earbud would pause or play music or pick up a call. These have two taps for this or that and most times it ends up max volume-ing me in my ear when I wanted to pause it.
Highly unimpressed and sad that the upgrade is trash.

UPDATE: The manufacturer reached out after my review. I retold my complaints and was sent a new set which was a very appreciated gesture. It turns out my original S9 were a lemon. Their charging issue was resolved in my new set. I am happy with the battery life now and reliability.

title: Very functional security camera!
text:
[[VIDEOID:2f341d63e0df9b17cccc695aec3f130e]] Very functional security camera!
I bought two of these little solar security cameras for my home and so far they are a good investment. I live in an old dwelling with limited access to power outlets so these little solar cams are just what I needed to help keep an eye on my home. They can be set to record 24 hour loops or you can set them to only record events detected by the camera. I have had one of my Katt Cams mounted out in the weather for about two months and so far it has performed well. It is still waterproof and hasn't even fogged up once. The night vision works pretty good and the clarity is fine for identifying specific vehicles; however, I don't think the camera's pictures are fine enough to make out a license plate number. These cameras have both a microphone and a speaker for 2-way audio and unlike most budget security cameras, these have decent speakers that don't distort the operator's voice.
These cameras charge effortlessly and the battery will hold a charge while functioning for a few days without being connected to power.
These cameras have many functions such as motion sensors that can be set to record activity. You can go into settings on each camera and set a custom detection sensitivity, so it isn't wasting memory on record every moth that flys by. These cameras can support 128gb SD card, but I found a 64gb card is fine for my needs. It took a bit of time and patience to pair the camera with the router, but once I followed the directions exactly and took the steps slowly, I was able to get everything to sync.

title: SLEEVE Your Worries Behind, This Is A Great Buy
text:
Bottom Line Up Front: This is a solid laptop bag. I ordered it because I want something small to carry my Microsoft Surface, kindle, and maybe a notebook and some pens to class. This bag provides me exactly that ability, no more, no less. If you want a small bag that can fit a minimalist amount of items, this is a great option! I cannot say enough good things about this bag if you are looking for an inexpensive way to stay organized and minimalist. I have divided my review into 3 parts: Durability, Usefulness, and Aesthetics.

Durability (5/5): The material of this bag is of good quality. The zippers are not cheaply made, the handles are firm and well attached. The clasps and shoulder strap are even made of good material (typically the shoulder strap is where companies save money in their design). The padding on the inside of the bag is also good quality. Due to it being more of a minimalist bag, the padding is not ultra-thick and protective. I would not buy this bag as a defense against computer drops (although I am pretty confident it would be enough padding to protect your computer if it were to fall). I am very impressed with this bag's durability.

Usefulness (5/5): This rating will vary based off what you are looking for out of the bag. If you want a computer bag that can fit all of your school books, a bunch of different cables and accessories then you'll definitely want something bigger. Personally, that isn't what I was looking for. As I said earlier, I just wanted an organized way I could transport a few items without having to lug around a backpack or a huge bag. This bag is exactly what I needed.

Aesthetic (5/5): If you like how this bag looks in the product description you will like this bag. The only thing I do need to point out in this aspect is the bag doesn't maintain its shape too well when bulky items are in it. Aka, it does not really have any stiff material on it to force it to remain with sharp edges and keep it from wrinkling. That said, if you are only putting a laptop, some pens, maybe a charging cord in it then it will still maintain its look. I also enjoy its flexibility when wearing it across my shoulder, as it actually wraps a bit around where it is resting against your side which keeps it from bouncing up and down as you walk.

All in all, this is a great bag! I will be using it as my primary bag for a long time. If you are a little worried about if it will be a quality bag for such a cheap price, have no fear! You will not be disappointed with this purchase.

title: Very misleading images -- looks like a white elephant
text:
This is for the SAMSUNG 32" Odyssey Neo G8. I should have looked at the Samsung website rather than rely on the misleading images on the Amazon website. This monitor is said to black and white but in reality, it is almost entirely white; the Amazon website does not show this.

Of the twelve images presently shown there is only one angle shot showing a bit white on the rear of the monitor stand; the actual back of the monitor is not shown. The back is entirely white; a shiny white that is ugly and cheap looking. Worse, the back is also is quite large because this is a 32" *curved* monitor so this flawed color scheme is as prominent as a white elephant. No wonder it was on sale.

I have not actually fully unpacked the monitor, so I have no idea how well it works (the spec's seem very good) but I can't past the physical look of the monitor. Amazingly there is apparently no other color scheme. It is unfortunate that such a seemingly well designed product is only offered in such an unsightly color scheme.

What was Samsung thinking? Of course, this begs the question, were they thinking? Apparently not.

title: Best value all-in-one USB-C hub
text:
I use this hub daily in my home office setup, and I am extremely satisfied. It is an incredible value at this price. My current connections include: 4K display, external keyboard, external mouse, USB audio interface.

This hub has allowed me to significantly simplify my setup so that only one usb-c port on my Macbook is being used. Also, the color matches the dark gray finish on my laptop perfectly, and the hub feels like metal.

Minor issues: It only supports a maximum of 30Hz at 4K over HDMI. I have a 60Hz display and would have preferred to use the full 60Hz. It runs pretty hot with all my devices connected, but that's not an issue for me in general. Also, when my Macbook Pro charger is plugged into it, but the hub is not plugged into my computer, it occasionally makes a very high pitched noise. This stops when I remove the charger usb-c from the hub. Note that this sound is not heard when the hub is plugged into the laptop.

While I would probably rate it at 4 stars due to the minor issues cited above, at this price point, it is a full 5 stars. You could buy several as backup or for travel and still be cheaper than a similar product from Apple.

Highly recommend!

title: One major flaw...
text:
For a small docking station / port extender this is a decent solution. It has more USB ports than many devices in this price range, but not coming with a power supply is a major drawback. I went back and checked the listing, and it does say all that comes with it is a single usb-c to usb-c cable, so it's on me not noticing. There are competitive products in roughly the same price range that come with their own power adapter, however. The idea of using the laptop power brick seems to be a common thing with these units, but a micro-sd port doesn't really seem to justify the jump to this price point, as there are less expensive units that provide dual monitor support and no power supply as well.

The port selection is pretty good, but I would have liked perhaps one more usb-a port on the back (there's physical room for it I think) to accommodate a hub or webcam hanging off the back.

I don't have 3 monitors for use with this, but it drives two 34" LG monitors perfectly. No issues with any of the peripherals or my one hub attached. It works perfectly with the Lenovo power brick that came with the laptop, and all USB ports can be driven properly. The gig port works well and Purely plug and play, with no usability issues. All-in-all not a bad solution, but there might be less expensive options with precisely the same features.

title: Best monitor on the market, but has QC issues.
text:
First off I'd like to say this monitor is absolutely gorgeous, but has QC issues. 10/10 playing submersive games like Valheim, WoW, and Red Dead 2. Red Dead 2 is the cream of all games that I have played on it. Situational awareness is enhanced 10x by the screen being so wide. You see so much more than what you will with a standard 16:9 monitor. I have a 3090 founders running this monitor with a 5085x AMD processor. It's unbelievable and describing it doesn't do it justice. The blacks and colors of the monitor side by side to my other monitors show just how far color accuracy and brightness have come in the last decade. I can't stress how beautiful this monitor is and how much of an advantage it is having the extra view area on the sides. Images do not seem distorted either. Even movies look great on it with the curve. However....

I can't get the BIOS to update. I have gone through Samsung customer support and they weren't able to remedy the issue over the phone. They said they'd send a technician out to fix the problem, but after 4 weeks of waiting I was told they don't have the parts. Then they said they'd replace with a new one. They couldn't find one. So now they want me to go through a very painful return procedure. I should have just gone through amazon's, but amazon didn't do anything wrong so why put it on them?

in this day and age I don't understand why you have to make us use USB thumb drives to update the monitor bios. Especially when it's hidden behind a massive monitor like this in a hard to reach area. Why are there not USB connections on the side for things like this? Failing that you've got a USB connector to the monitor already. Why not use the USB hub to allow you to send the bios update? Just add a button to turn on a BIOS drive internal to the monitor and allow you to drag and drop the bios to the folder. EZPZ. Instead we have to format our USB to a specific allocation unit size and then stick it in the correct USB port hidden behind the monitor in a hard to reach place. Considering how often updates are coming out for this monitor as the technology advances this should be an ez process instead a pain in the you know what!

I have some issues that the BIOS is supposed to fix hopefully:
1) Monitor power cycles randomly when under load.
2) Pixels enlarge on certain content. I don't know a good way to describe this other than it seems every pixel gets a border around it on the screen. I've noticed this happen when I'm on certain web pages or developing in visual studio with certain files open.
3) HDR looks dim when looking at the windows desktop. This may be a windows thing, but why is this painful?
4) Shadowplay requires me to pay for a codec to play my replays because of the resolution. 2500 dollar monitor and 1700 3090 and neither of you thought to make a free codec for it's users to use?

Even with all the issues above I'm still returning this one and buying another one. Hopefully the new one will not have these issues. It really is the best monitor on the market right now. I just hope the new one works as advertised and I pray for no dead pixels as I've seen others complain about. The one I have is flawless.

title: Ultra-light Laptop. Good Small, Inexpensive Laptop
text:
As might be expected from a $200 laptop, this Lenovo is not the biggest, baddest, slickest kid on the block. I warn you in advance, I have a MacBook and a Mac Mini, as well as a Samsung laptop and a Toshiba, plus a Mini iPad, an iPad 3 and an Amazon Kindle Fire HD, so I have a pretty good base to compare this laptop with.

This is much more like the HP Netbook I used to have than it is to any of my other devices. Of course, I gave the Netbook away when I went to Best Buy to buy a real laptop. And at the last second, I cancelled the laptop and bought the just released Apple iPad (the first one) and fell in love with Apple all over again.

So, Lenovo is really a poor man's netbook. The keyboard, like the rest of the device. Is functional, but has way to little click and spring back for my satisfaction. Not sure how durable the keys are, as on other laptops either the white coloring of the letters fades too quickly or the keys break off. Lenovo keys may surprise, but the feel of them does not inspire.

Capacity for storage on the device is pretty much a deal breaker for me. Although I could get used to the cloud, so I won't criticize that too harshly. The cloud seems to be the future.

I do like the USB 3,0 connection as an addition to the USB 2.0 port, and the card reader.

Another welcome feature that is practically mandatory with any Microsoft Windows driven device is the trial MacAfee anti-virus.

Thus, when budget is a concern, as in when you have two or three kids and want to give them something really nice that the can use to surf the web, and when you want something thin and light, this Lenovo S21e is, in all fairness, a good deal.

title: Great audio, very comfortable, battery life could be better
text:
This is one of the most comfortable set of headphones/headset I’ve ever worn. The sound quality is excellent. Comes with a USB adapter (not required if you have Bluetooth but becomes more full featured if you use it anyway), a desktop charger, USB-A to micro charge cable (also needed for firmware updates) and a soft/neoprene case for all but the desktop charger. Install the Poly software for complete feature set when used with a computer. It’s more or less connect and play, but there are other configurable options with the Poly software. I find the sound cancellation functionality to be quite good, and I’ve have few to no issues or problems. The headset will also connect to two devices at a time - think laptop and cell phone. It works great with Teams (it will auto answer incoming calls when you put the headset on!) as well as Cisco IP Communicator (a software-based telephone). The headset can be worn with the mic on either side of your head. I like to pace when I talk - this keeps a solid connection at a ridiculous distance for a Bluetooth device.

My one and only issue is the battery life - if you use this regularly throughout the day for calls and not in standby, you will need to charge it at least once during the workday. This isn’t such a big deal if your in the office or have a permanent space at home where you can use the desktop charger stand, but if you don’t, plugging it in isn’t ideal - at least not for me. If were magnetic like with the stand... I’m so close to giving this 4 stars or higher, but the battery life (at least with moderate use) is holding me back. Having said that, it’s never dropped its connection or had any technical issues at all, so I’m torn. Overall I’m very pleased with and use it regularly, but for the price point I expect better battery life. I’d still recommend this as it’s a well known quality brand, just adjust your expectations on the battery life.

title: Not Impressed
text: First, let me tell you I am a Samsung fanboy. I have the 85" q90b neo tv, several galaxy phones, watchs, and their 2020 laptop. Samsung has a LOT of my money. So when I heard they made the first 4k@240hz monitor ever, I jumped on it. I bought the g8 neo for about $850 on Black Friday. While I guess that's a "good" price, it still too much for what you get. First, since you will likely use your monitor for things other than just games, the curve is odd and distorts any image. In games it is... okay, but for normal internet browsing or productivity work, it is bad. Your brain is expecting straight lines, but the curve makes the dead-on part straight and the sides very curved. Looks like the view from cheap scuba diving goggles. Regardless of the marketing, it is NOT an improvement over a flat screen, it's just different. Second, the monitor's colors are bad. It looks like it has a grey film over the screen that does not get better with any adjustment. Third, mine constantly blanks-out like you are changing sources. Every time you open the internet or an app, it blanks-out. Often, it also has large rectangular boxes that rapidly appear and disappear. It does this randomly. One day it works fine, the next day it freaks-out. I tried different cables of different lengths, in different Displayports, on my RTX 4090 (the best GPU you can buy right now). Nothing made it work correctly. Dumbing the resolution to 1080@120hz helped, but then there were random screen jitters. Are there fixes... maybe. Did I get a bad one... maybe. But for this price I expect an item to work, right out of the box, without issues. I just went to my local MicroCenter to buy a 32" LG for half the price. While only 2k@240hz, it worked right out of the box, it is flat, and the colors are sharp. And MicroCenter just happen to have the 49' g9 on display and guess what... it had a grey film look and when I wiggled the mouse to get out of the demo program it was using... it blanked-out like it was changing sources. Hopefully the technology will improve because the concept is great, but these just are not ready for as is.

title: Help in a transitioning world
text:
With the proliferation of USB-C ports on personal computers and mobile phones, accessing them with older peripherals, like mice and memory cards and even monitors becomes challenging. I have more Chromebooks than I should, and most of them have USB-C inputs. When I want to plug in a keyboard or a monitor or a flash drive, I quickly run out of ports IF they even have an older USB port to begin with. And one of my Chromebooks only has USB-C ports to begin with.

For this reason, this Aceele multiport adapter makes perfect sense. It allows me to plug several devices at a time into one of those USB-C ports and increase my connectivity. You can read the specs for this device in the product description, but it allows me to quickly plug my Chromebook into an external monitor thru the HDMI port, or a flash drive for adding files to my laptop - really helpful when the file is too big to email to myself. Especially helpful is that the multiport adapter even includes another USB-C port so I'm not really sacrificing one of those ports on my Chromebook.

This adapter is very slim and light weight - smaller than about a third of a pack of cards . The cord connecting it to my laptop is about seven inches long. The body of the adapter is plastic, not metal, so use care where you store this. It is a nice, inexpensive way to expand your Mac or Chromebook or even your mobile phone.

title: Overkill but in a good way - headroom is always nice to have
text:
This item arrived with a small user’s guide (magnifying glass required of course) but no USB cable. This is the third high speed charger I’ve looked at lately and none has included cables. I’m guessing that’s because USB cables that support higher wattages are pricier - sometimes much pricier - than everyday cables. I wouldn’t bother with this charger if you don’t use USB cables rated at least 100W as a lesser cable will just throttle the flow of the extra power the charger can produce.

I can’t test the advertised 140W ceiling of this Rocoran charger because I don’t have fast enough hardware. I do have a battery bank that accepts input as high as 100W and I have a USB C cable rated at 100W to connect between the Rocoren charger and the battery bank. Nowadays 100W is considered pretty darned good, but it’s not good enough to max this charger out. But when you charge multiple devices at the same time, that extra capacity really speeds things up.

I connected my 100W rated cable between the charger and the battery bank and unsurprisingly saw that the juice was flowing at around 100W. I didn't want to let all the extra power go to waste so I plugged a relatively wimpy (45W capacity) cable between the second USB C port on the charger and my phone. My older Moto phone promptly announced that TurboPower was connected and began charging (exact power draw unknown). The battery bank draw did drop from 100W to about 63W when I connected the phone but still, no complaints. Many of today’s high speed chargers will max out at 45W when charging only a single device.

Did I mention that this little critter easily replaces the power bricks that come with many USB C powered laptops? It fully charges the battery from zero to 100% on my Lenovo Chromebook while it’s running UToob videos on autoplay.

After running for about 40 minutes the charger was very warm to the touch but not unexpectedly or unreasonably so. This is a nice, tidy charger that performs as advertised. If you’re using an older charger/adapter that was included with your phone or tablet you are going to love this ridiculously fast charger. Just keep in mind that you may find yourself wanting to replace your older USB C cables with higher wattage ones.

title: Good deal for a throwaway monitor
text:
I used to live in a cool, quiet house in a valley but had to move into a hot and noisy apartment in the city, with no A/C. The temps inside get up to 88 F on a hot day with a 90 F high! As room temp is considered to be 68-72 F, I was worried about my high end Lenovo ThinkVision monitor ($300) and HP color laser printer ($400) being fried or corroded in the heat and humidity of this wretched climate. So I placed both in my air-conditioned self storage unit while I look for better living conditions.

To replace them, I decided to buy this $85 Acer monitor and an $85 HP inkjet printer (which costs less than a black toner cartridge for my color laser) and I could pretty much dump then when I move abroad to live (my main intentions). While the Acer is no match for the color saturation, overall screen quality, and bells and whistles of the Lenovo (which was pretty much hand-picked at Best Buy before I pulled the trigger on a good monitor), the Acer has surprised me for such a cheap monitor. It's sharp and color contrast is excellent. My main issue was the screen background being yellowish-green compared to my Lenovo or my Dell XPS, however it got whiter with time as the monitor burned in. In addition, I used the preset screen settings and found a couple that was able to whiten up the screen quite a bit, so that now, it's not bad at all.

For $85, I expected soft, blurry text with dull colors in which case I'd return the monitor but I have no complaints now: sharp, excellent color saturation and contrast, and decently white background. Just be aware it has ZERO USB ports, no USB charging port, no HDMI or DisplayPorts, and no audio out port - nor height and tilt adjustments - like my Lenovo. In addition, Acer deleted the audio out port that the earlier models had. Well, I guess you get what you pay for. It's probably worth it to spend 3-4X the cost of the Acer to get a good monitor like the Lenovo, but for my purposes, the Acer suits me fine. I might have to find room in my self storage to keep the monitor as it's too good to throw away!

One thing to note, the 2 legs need to be installed correctly (R for right side, L for left side. Match the arrows as well). Everything else was easy.

The display is amazing, with different options in the setup menu. The internal speakers are good (not tinny like most) for a 32 inch TV. The external devise is plug and play for the most part. No problem connecting my cable box and soundbar. *One thing to note regarding the "optical connection of a soundbar..... the remote control will NOT control the volume. You must connect via HDMI to use the remote for soundbar speaker control. If you have an Alexa device, you can control some features of the TV with it (very cool so far). It's easy to add and use apps. Connecting to my wireless connection was fast and easy (if you remember your wireless password). I'm running 100MB (Spectrum, which is very good in my neighborhood). I live alone, so besides my PC and cell phone, no other wifi is being used. There has been NO LAG watching live TV for the past 5 hours (while I'm working).

Cons:
*The remote's volume controls are on the side of the remote. I inadvertently change the volume when hitting other buttons.
*The soundbar optical connection does not support use of the remote to control it's volume. You need to use HDMI
*If your TV is on a high dresser, the TV needs to be at the edge of the dress for the remote to work. I'm building a 12" riser for the TV to sit on so I can move the TV away from the edge.

All in all, for $150, this TV is EXCELLENT so far and I don't regret buying it. I can now "cut the cable cord" and save $60 a month. My other TVs are Samsungs that were over $1,000 each, and I honestly can't see much of a difference between the video and speed (60MHZ with this model; no lag or pixelating).
