title: You get what you pay for!
text:
This device comes with instructions, but they are next to useless. It is supposed to be plug and play, I gets.

On the latest version of Windows 10 (this is what I have now when I got this camera, so I can't speak to prior versions), you have to adjust your "Privacy" settings to get this device to work, even though Windows see it. While that is not the fault of the camera, this point could have been included in the manual included in the box (there are two of these which say the exact same thing on the front cover but they are actually for different languages). I finally got on the phone with tech support, and they didn't even know this. I saw a comment on Amazon.com that mentioned this Privacy thing and that prompted me to dig into that setting. So I wasted a lot of time on something as simple as that. Tech support is supposed to call me back within 24 hours, which means I hear back on a Monday, since I called them on a Friday. Useless.

Second, and even more important, is that the video coming from this looks like crap. There is no way to control anything. The image is over exposed and noisy. The camera in my laptop works way, way better than this, so rather than using my desktop (which allows me to get the camera much higher up and hence gives me a better angle) and I going to go back to the laptop. Argh.

The mount they put on this webcam does not inspire confidence. It is a weird mount for a monitor, as you can't lock it down. It does stay put, though, but it makes you wonder if you are missing something. The tripod mount is simple to use as you just screw it on. The webcam can angle down once mounted. If the video image were better, then this webcam would be great. But it is not.

The mics on this seem to be ok. They were working from the get-go and Windows didn't block that. Hey, Microsoft - why don't you block audio too since you are blocking video by default? How stupid are you guys? And why didn't you pop up an alert to say that the new camera device I just installed is blocked by default? That would have saved me a ton of time. What are you people thinking over there? Ah, you're not! I see.

The only good thing in this story is that this is the only camera I could find on Amazon that would ship to me in a useful time frame due to Covid-19. Now, you can't find any webcams and they ones you do see are priced out of this world.

title: 1st monitor lasted 20 min but the replacement is fantastic.
text: I was excited to get this monitor and had very high expectations.  I set it up and it looked great as I started playing a game.  It lasted 20 minutes until there was a bright flash of light that appeared toward the middle of the screen and it wouldn't go away no matter what I tried.  I researched the issue and turns out it is a common QC problem with Samsung panels and requires a panel replacement in most cases.  I decided not to test my luck again so I packed it up and shipped it back for a refund. I was not going to try for a replacement but decided to give it one more chance since it was $800 during the week of Black Friday.  My 2nd monitor arrived flawless.  It took some getting used to the curve but I don't even notice it during gaming.  It is very noticeable though when browsing the web or doing anything other than gaming or watching movies.  Isn't too bad though.  The image quality with the bright HDR, deep blacks and stunning colors is where this monitor really shines.  A little bit of blooming is visible at times but it doesn't bother me.  I have had OLED TVs since 2018 and am very happy with the HDR and the black levels on this monitor.  I have it paired with an i9-13900k and RTX 4090 FE PC and they're a gaming match made in heaven.  It doesn't have official G-Sync support but you won't even know.  PC games run buttery smooth with zero screen tearing.  Even the PS5 looks exceptional on it and I'm replaying games I haven't touched in a while.  I am glad I decided to try this monitor again because it is fantastic. I use it mainly for playing AAA titles.  I personally wouldn't use it for competitive fps games as the curve may be a hinderance for those.  For competitive games I use a 1080p Acer Nitro XV252Q 390 Hz monitor.  Neo G7 checks off all of the boxes for anyone not wanting to go the OLED route and risking a burn in. The image quality of this display is so close to OLED that I don't feel like I compromised on anything and the colors look better than on my LG C1 OLED.  139 ppi make everything, inluding the text nice and crisp.  If you can live with the curve and the hefty price tag I highly recommend that you give the Neo G7 a try for PC or next gen console gaming.  I see myself enjoying this monitor for a long time without buyer's remorse no matter what new screens come out next year.

Sound: eh, it's okay. I'm not getting that warm butterfly effect from these. Definitely not at this price. My WH-1000XM5 over ear headphones at $400, now that's an amazing sound. However, for a nice walk or run they're okay. They're just okay mom.

Fit: I'm super confused as to how they're supposed to fit in my ear. I'm not sure if there was a tut in their app. They don't feel like they're fitting in my ear correctly. I'll review the app and screenshots if I find any.

App: I'm not thrilled that I had to connect via their app. However, I haven't tried disconnecting them either. The one thing I couldn't stand from their app is the Talk setting. Price: To me, these plugs don't warrant the price. I think they're overly priced for what they are. Sony had wired in ear plugs back in the early 90s I think it was and those were 20x better than these. I believe they cost me around $29 I still have them somewhere in a box too.

title: Old school quality and functionality
text:
Firstly, this router has a physical button to turn on or off the LEDs on the device. Can I say how much I LOVE this feature? Our homes are glittering lightscapes of tiny, annoying lights where most can only be disabled by strategic placement of tape. This router arrives not only with politely sized green LEDs but the option to quickly and easily turn them off. +1 that it is a physical switch. This router also has a physical power button and physical buttons for WPS and Wifi. Overall, I get the feeling this product was not designed by the "ooh shiny" crowd but by the "we don't need superfluous nonsense, just make it WORK and work WELL" crowd.

We did not use the app to configure this unit. Because of a bad experience with our ISP-supplied equipment, we specifically purchased a router that would permit full configuration via the traditional web interface. This unit does not disappoint. It is definitely more techie-oriented, something we appreciated.

The ability to operate separate wifi bands was required, again because of the past experience with our ISP. As such, we do not have the wireless operating as one, rather it is broken out into separate networks according to purpose. Thanks to this router, we have our Ring devices on a 2.4 GHz guest network and we can load-balance our personal devices across two 5 GHz private networks. So far, bandwidth, throughput, and stability are excellent but we've only had this connected a very short time. This review will be revisited if necessary and after additional features are tested.

All in all, this router has been an excellent purchase.

title: Love this monitor for both work and gaming!
text:
I purchased this as Used-Acceptable from Amazon, but it turned out it was a completely new monitor and still covered under Samsung's warranty until next year. It was relatively easy to setup. You'll need two people to lift the monitor.
I used the Ergotron HX monitor mount, which I'd highly recommend for this monitor (makes accessing the back so much easier when you can just tilt it all the way up).
I love using this monitor for both gaming and work. For work, I like to use the full-screen and I can have so many coding windows open at one time. It's amazing. For gaming, it took me a bit to get used to things moving in my peripheral. I was actually getting motion sickness, but the more I used it the better it got. I've tried out the monitor on Horizon: Zero Dawn, Elder Scrolls Online, World of Warcraft, Raft, Project Zomboid (very nice for seeing zombies sneaking up), Diablo 3, and other games. So far most games I've tried work with the aspect ratio, and it feels very immersive to game with this.

If you aren't sure about the aspect ratio, you can just play in Windowed mode and adjust the aspect ratio as you need. Samsung has a free app that lets you customize different areas of the screen you can snap applications to.

Also, the monitor works for up to three external outputs (2 HDMI and 1 DP). I have my work laptop, my gaming laptop, and my Nintendo Switch plugged into the monitor. If I want to use two of the outputs at the same time, the Picture in Picture mode works really well. You cannot split your screen (as if you had two monitors) for the same output.

Finally, if you connect a Mac to this monitor, you'll need to go into System -> PC/AV Mode -> and change your port to AV. That'll fix the monitor turning pink for Macs.

Some things you should know that I didn't see in other reviews.
1. Mine arrived with a stripped screw holding the camera to the frame, I was able to salvage it. It's cheaply made, which considering the price point is ok, but quality control is obviously spotty which explains the wide range of reviews.
2. The camera is sensitive to infrared light which makes it see well in the dark but will make colors seem unnatural in the daylight.
3. Contrary to someone else's review, the correct aspect ratio for this camera is 4:3. (old tvs were 4:3) If you connect it to a 16:9 (modern HD TVs are 16:9) monitor you will either have a stretched image or black bars on the sides.
4. I'm not sure how they measure it, but as far as I can tell it's not 170 degree viewing angle. By my measurements, it's closer to 100. Nonetheless that is adequate for me to see that I don't hit anyone near the outside of my car when backing up.
5. Where the video and power cables come together there's a bump in the cable. For bench testing I left it on for awhile. I noticed the bump got quite hot, 118 fahrenheit by my measurement. It didn't seem like it was going to catch on fire, but energy translating to heat is inefficient. It really makes me wonder what's in that part of the cable.
6. Depending on how you run the cables it's possible to get interference in the picture.
7. If you are using this as a rearview camera, the wide angle will make things seem much farther away than they actually are.
8. At night this camera is quite visually noisy, but probably better than most of the other cameras in this price range and it's adequate to see if you are about to run something over.

I haven't had the camera long enough to know about long term durability. Despite it's faults, the camera is adequate for what I need it for, which would be making sure I don't hit anyone backing up and also giving me a fairly good wide view of the road behind me while driving. The 71 mustang mach 1 has a slit of a rear view window so this camera helps me get a much better idea of what's behind me and has already helped me not run over the neighbor and her dog who were in my blind spot coming out of the driveway. As far as I can tell, this is the best of the cheap backup cameras.

title: Should be a bit better for the price.
text:
While the video quality on the g900 is good, there's a couple things I feel could make this better. My MAIN issue? I seemingly can't manually lock recorded video. I can select, play and delete it, but I can't seem to lock it so it doesn't get overwritten. Viewing a video tutorial of a lower model Wolfbox that can do it, this one SHOULD be able to but I haven't found a way and the manual doesn't help.

The second is the rear camera. While it is recommended to mount outside the car, this comes with a major potential issue: wet visibility. Water just clings to this as soon as I hit a wet highway and being dark outside just leaves me with bright, blurry splotches. Being this becomes your new rearview, and recommended external mounting, it should really either have a hydrophobic coating over the lens or a hydrophobic lens cover. Trying to see behind you can be dangerous in wet weather.

With no wifi (or Bluetooth) as I've seen in other brand models, you'll have to remove the SD card to save anything externally (which right now seems like the only way to manually save video). I don't have a SD card reader so I had to remove my card from my previous phone to save a file, then remove it to reinsert into the dashcam.

Note: Because of the very wide camera viewing angle, things will be MUCH closer than they appear on the screen. It will take some time to get used to.

title: Watch the online video and get a perfect fit for your new Garmin watch
text:
I ordered this screen protector on a whim because there weren't any reviews yet, but I've got to say that it is FANTASTIC.

Opening the box, there are 6 screen protectors, an info card, a squeegee, and a spray bottle of solution. Going onto their website and watching the installation video is an absolute must because they do not provide written instructions, and I would not have guessed to apply it how they recommend.

To apply the screen protector, you clean everything off first as usual, but then spray the front and back with the solution before applying (mind you, this is not an adhesive). You then place the protector onto your clean watch face, and the solution allows you to move the screen protector around a bit to perfectly center it. GENIUS. You then squeegee out the excess solution, wait for it to dry a bit, then press all the sides down that are on the curved edges.

I'll admit, at first the screen protector didn't look great because there was still some solution under the protecter, but once I got it all out and it dried overnight, it looks spotless. Further, it is the perfect size for the screen and goes right up to the bezel, and thanks to the solution that lets you move it around, it is perfectly centered.

I have used glass screen protectors for my phone for the last few years so I was unsure of how I would like the flexible screen protector, but it looks great and is much better quality than the old flexible screen protectors I used to use.

It doesn't add any extra glare and has minimal smudging. It does slightly reduce the crispness of the screen in certain angles, but it is on par with flexible screen protectors and its not like the garmin watch has impressive screen resolution anyway.

The best part about it: YOU CANNOT TELL THERE IS A SCREEN PROTECTOR ON THE WATCH AT ALL!

Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend this screen protector if you have the Garmin Vivoactive 3 Music.

title: NOT Bluetooth 5.1
text:
Despite saying it's 5.1 all over the listing, all over the packaging: the driver only supports LMP 9. The Bluetooth SIG's assigned number for LMP versions specify that 9 is for Bluetooth Core Specification 5.0, and that 10 is for Bluetooth Core Specification 5.1.

The device uses a RTL8761B, which appears to be a partner-only model. As of writing, the latest driver (March 2021) is only LMP 9.

Perhaps the *hardware* itself might be certified to meet 5.1 standards, but if you can't use it as such, that pretty much sums up as false advertising to me.

Edited to correct chip part number. Jan 6 22

title: Sharp & bright from edge to edge. Quite impressive.
text:
The image quality is excellent and no doubt 1080p. On-screen display states refresh rate is 60 hertz. I have an older 720P projector that only upscaled to 1080P. I was able to tell the difference in quality right away. This is a well designed projector, including the app you can use with it.

My use of this will be outdoors, at night, once I get an appropriate screen. I did test and provide pics of this in use indoors, with image projected onto a light beige wall with some daylight coming into the room from windows. I was quite surprised at how great it looked.

With projector 10' from wall and sitting on a counter 34" high, the projected image (16:9 aspect ratio) was 104" diagonally. Using the “zoom” feature, I was able to reduce the size down to 53" diagonally.

- Menu control is by remote (requires 2, AAA batteries) and on the projector itself.
- Menu navigation and choices are so intuitive, there is almost no reason to need the instruction manual, which happens to be thorough and well written.
- The are more adjustments with this than budget projectors, such as color temp and balances, sharpness, aspect ratios, extra zoom features and more.
- Tabletop use leaves you with the typical threaded foot for elevation. A 1/4-20 mount is also included on the bottom for use with a stand or ceiling mount.
- Via the easy to use app (on a newer and fast Android phone in my case) I was able to stream (mirror) movies from my phone. Some of my GoPro movies at 4k caused a little stuttering, but everything lower than that was not an issue.
- I did play 4k movies from my laptop via HDMI cable. No buffering and projected image was just outstanding in color and sharpness.
- I’m not a fan of the built in speaker in terms of loudness, and I don’t think other reviewers would agree. I think the limitation is that if a speaker is designed to be too loud, it is going to vibrate the projector housing and effect the image. It was loud enough to overcome the cooling fan, but not by much in my case. My future use of this will include an external speaker.
- Fan noise bothered me a bit - could be heard within 8' of it.
- This comes with a really nice storage/carry case, with enough internal and external pockets to hold more cables than most will ever need.
- Power and HDMI cables are both 6' long.
- Focus was not overly finicky and getting keystone adjustment dialed in not hard. I like that the lens cover is part of the housing - slide open/shut. It will turn off if you slide the door closed, but directions state to first power this down via remote or onboard power button.

All in all, I am very happy with the image quality. The speaker is a non-issue for me as I intend to use an external speaker anyways. I’m really impressed.

title: 5 stars not enough.  Should win an award.
text:
[[VIDEOID:48c60e0a8a6ca4e5ea0f9ea21d380ebc]] I don’t recall ever being so impressed with a compact personal speaker this size. This little speaker is amazing and well worth the $50 price tag. I have 2 other JBL speakers (Flip 6 and Charge 4). While those big brothers to this are great, this Go 3 is made to really be portable (and waterproof), and that it is.

Main specs: Bluetooth version 5.1; Dynamic frequency response range (Hz) 110 Hz - 20 kHz; Maximum music playing time (hrs) 5; charging time (hrs) 2.5. On my scale, this weighs in at 7.3 ounces.

No issues when pairing with my android phone. Strap loop is super strong. Overall construction is really great - this is built to take some abuse. As you can see in my video, the little punchy bass this puts out will vibrate this thing away on you if laid down. And it will sound awesome while it runs off.

The bass: By far, the best I’ve heard in a speaker this size, and better than others 4x larger. You can more than mildly feel it, but it of course will be nothing like its bigger brothers. For what it is, it is amazing though. Keep in mind this is meant to be a personal speaker, and not a party one. However, playing on my kitchen counter, I can clearly hear it as I move about the house.

From a full charge, and at near full volume while out on a waverunner and also while mowing my lawn on a tractor, I have a good 2 hours on the charge and it hasn’t died yet. I think their 5 hour battery life is realistic, but of course not at super high volumes.

I’ve owned, played with at stores, and/or reviewed here a number of bluetooth speakers. In its class and price point, this one is going to be near impossible to beat. It is extremely difficult to make a speaker this small to sound this good, especially with its legit IP67 waterproof construction. Good job JBL.

title: Works Great!
text:
Ordered this because I tend to lose my cell phone, keys and remote in my home. Once I found my keys in the refrigerator! Seriously, how did that even happen?? lol I attached one to my keys, and one to my cell phone wrist strap base, and will probably put one on the remote.

They work great! My place isn't huge, so the range is just fine for me. They work in all the rooms of my place. The beep is pretty loud, and I have no issue hearing it. Kind of reminds me of the fire alarm beep.

Best part is, there's a button on the base for each separate color, so it doesn't beep all of them at once! If you're searching for your keys (the blue), you press the blue button and only that one goes off, and so on for the other colors as well.

As far as battery life, I couldn't really tell you because I've only been using it for a couple of weeks and they're still fine. But, they're similar type of batteries like you use on car key fobs, and those last a pretty long time, even though we use the all the time. You might use this battery even less times than that {unless you lose your stuff all the time. lol), so I'm thinking these may last even longer.

The key finder boxes are small and are super light, so it doesn't add a lot of weight to whatever you put them on. Very lightweight. You can also use the 2 sided adhesive piece to put it on the back of your phone, or tv remote.

If there were any negatives at all (and this is a me problem, not a product problem), is that like I mentioned, the alarm sounds a lot like the tone of the fire alarms in my home and my dogs hate it. Every time any of the fire alarms go off, they start barking and howling. They don't start right away though, it takes about 10 seconds before they start, so I just try to find my lost item quickly, so I can shut off the alarm. lol It has a switch to turn it off right on the little box.

The base looks really nice as well, kind of looks like some kind of phone cradle charger, so definitely not an eyesore.

Anyway, I'm glad I picked this up. Works perfectly, good range in my opinion, great battery life so far, looks nice, no complaints.

title: Good product for this price point but can not record 24/7 on solar
text:
This is a truly wireless security camera with some neat features, but the battery isn't sufficient to make it through the night if you want to record 24/7. Worse, once the battery runs out, it "bricks" the unit, not only does it remain "off" when the sun returns, it won't even charge. So when you manually turn it back on (requires you to be physically present at the camera) the battery will be close to 0%, regardless of how long it's been in the direct sun. The only effective option on solar is to operate it in motion-detection only mode, which, unfortunately, means it will not record every event one is interested in, because not every event will trigger the motion detection. For example, I wanted to watch what the camera captured when we had an earthquake, and there was no record of the event. Even on the highest sensitivity setting, sometimes the unit will record an event just as it's ending. I have the camera pointed away from the house and I've had several recordings of vehicles just as they are exiting the field of view.

While operating in motion detection only mode, the solar panel has no problem keeping the battery charged, even under cloudy skies. It would be nice if the camera could at least record 24/7 until the battery gets low, and THEN switch to motion only, however the camera currently doesn't have the option.

The unit does not come with an SD card to record video, however it doesn't require a large or expensive one to operate. I put a 64GB card in my unit and after several days, it has only used a few GB. I think 64G is more than enough storage to record for months.

The night vision and extremely bright white LEDs that the user can configure are really good.

The unit can push notifications when motion is detected, but unfortunately, it does not push an image or short video to go with it. It also can sound an alarm from the unit, but it is comically too quiet to be any use. The microphone on the unit is good, maybe too good, I wish there was a way to adjust the sensitivity (my other cameras have such functionality). The speaker on the unit is underpowered. Just like the alarm is quiet, so is the volume when trying to communicate through the unit. A neat feature one can toggle in the app is the ability to distort one's voice. For example, a female can toggle to sound like megatron when speaking through the unit. The icons for the distortion effects are very small and not descriptive of what they are doing, but with a little experimentation one can figure it out.

This is a good camera for this price point and being solar powered and being truly wireless provides a lot of flexibility. The wifi range isn't impressive (about 30 feet) and there is no way to add an external antenna, but it's enough range for most applications. If one needs more distance than that, a wifi extender or mesh network may be required.

title: Small, Neat-Looking, Works Well For Me Without the Firmware Upgrade
text:
I ordered this to replace an airplay adapter that occasionally loses contact with the phone and freezes my Airplay. It is quite a bit more expensive than my other one, and the ad promised much more stability. Unfortunately it does not live up to its promise.

It looks pretty nice, like a miniature computer mouse, with clean lines and a very retro metal-flake finish. It takes a USB-C input, and they include both USB-A to USB-C and USB-C to USB-C cables - nice touch. The instruction booklet is nicely illustrated and very complete. Setup was pretty easy - you just plug it in, connect the Bluetooth on your phone to the adapter, and you're in business.

It arrives with a firmware upgrade procedure, but there is a note in the Amazon page that says to try it out without updating. It has worked very well in my car without the update, so I'm leaving well enough alone.

title: Excellent Surge Protector Outlet
text:
I'm working my way through all my work areas, cleaning them up and simplifying all the plugs and outlets, and this outlet extender is a big help. It's very well designed, with the outlets spaced enough to handle all sort of plugs and adapters. They have even reversed the top outlet on the top of the sides so it will accommodate two 90 degree plugs on each side.

Of course there are two USP-A and 1 USB-C charging outlets on the front, which does away with the need for a couple of adapters. The USP-C charging port is only 3A, not a PD or Quick Charge, which is fine for my application. If you need PD, you will have to use an adapter rather than the built-in outlets.

Construction is excellent. The whole device feels solid and sturdy, with an LED to indicate that the unit is getting power. It covers all of a dual-outlet fixture, turning two outlets into eight - eleven if you count the USB chargers. The surge protection will safeguard the small fortune I have invested in rechargeable power tool batteries and chargers.

A small but very nice feature is the long outlet plug that you can use to secure the unit to the wall. Without it you have to be careful to hold the extender in place when you unplug anything to keep from pulling the whole unit out. Thoughtful little touches like that go a long way.

title: Nice Outlet Extender
text:
I wanted to clean up all the wires in a corner of our kitchen, and this is exactly what I need. It is relatively attractive, low profile, and very well laid-out. I have several rechargeable kitchen gadgets, so the USB charging ports are great to have. The surge protection is an added bonus, since I will leave a blender and coffee maker plugged in to it all the time.

The arrangement of the outlets is the biggest advantage for me. The "always plugged in" items are out of the way, and the center-front outlet is easily accessible for the coffee grinder, vacuum sealer, or anything else I want to use and put away. The USB charging ports are also front-and-center for convenience.

They provide a long outlet screw that I initially was not going to bother with. When I pulled the whole unit out unplugging the coffee grinder for the first time, I got the point and used it. It turns out that the retaining screw is a very nice feature after all.

All in all, very highly recommended.

text:
WHY do phone makers put the charging port on the bottom of the phone where it get in the way, forcing you to harshly bend the charging cable? That constant flexing and twisting is what kills charging cords so quickly. But these little right-angle doodads do a great job, taking the stress off the charging port and the cable.

title: Good USB-C multi-port adapter
text:
I have tested this adapter in several scenarios and I have had good success with it.

Build quality is great, with all metal construction and a sturdy permanently attached USB-C cable.

USB-C power pass-thru is great for charging your device while utilizing the ports on this adapter. I have connected this to my Galaxy Note 10+ and my Galaxy Tab S7+ for use in DEX mode, and when I connect a power adapter and USB-C cable to the USB-C input, it will charge the device that is connected. I have also used this connected to a Chromecast with Google TV to utilize the network port instead of wireless, and that works fine (use the HDMI connector on the Chromecast, not the HDMI port on this adapter)

I have also used this with a Lenovo C730 laptop for network and for additional video out and it works fine. It does not charge the C730, but that laptop does not support charging via USB-C.

The video out did not work when connected to the USB-C port on an Asus X570-I motherboard with Ryzen 3 3200G processor, when other USB-C video adapters haver worked. Other functions of the adapter work as expected.

Overall, this is a versatile adapter that works as expected in all portable use cases that I tested. The Asus X570-I motherboard test was an outlier situation that I would not normally use this adapter for anyway.

title: Very nice and light weight.
text:
Having spent the last month working on 21.5" i-macs (2009,2010,2012,2015) which weight over 23 pounds each I was very happy to receive this monitor to use as a second monitor for my 2010 MacBook pro 13". The monitor is very lightweight, just 5 pounds .5 ounces (without cables) and not massive looking on my desk.

Since my old 2010 MacBook pro does not have HDMI I am using a display port to HDMI converter cable. Using this cable to hook up to an HDMI cable I am able to use the monitor at 1280x720 and 60.00 Hz VSync. My old computer (with the converter cable) is unable to display 1920x1080 without some artifacts, but it does work. This is no fault of the monitor. Other than that issue with my old computer I am having no technical issues with the monitor. Very happy with my purchase.

Looking forward to seeing how this monitor displays with my upcoming AMD Ryzen build...

Highly recommended, lightweight, and a great price.

EDIT: Enabled the NVidia graphics card on the 2010 MacBook pro running Linux 20.1 Cinnamon and now the monitor is displaying 1920x1080 flawlessly. :-)

text:

After reading reviews and websites on options, I decided on the Scythe Mugen 5 Rev.B over more expensive options like the Noctua U12A or Dark Rock 4. Super happy with the Scythe! It's much much quieter then the Wraith, with which I had to fiddle with fan curve settings to get an acceptable noise level. The Mugen is quiet out of the box, even on load running Cinebench or playing games like Overwatch.

The mounting was much easier and less of a hassle then dealing with the clip system on the Wraith, and the fan was super easy to clip on. Temps during gaming are probably 10 deg cooler, which is a nice perk as well. Highly recommend over more expensive options out there.

title: Great All Around Product - Quality and Design
text:
Lots of things to like about this tablet.

+ Comes with a cover in the package. With a toddler at home, it will drop and the cover has already saved the tablet a couple of times. The cover works as a stand and can also be used for carrying it. Top design.
+ Screen quality is great! Looks great and is very responsive to touch controls.
+ Charging times are fast and battery life is pretty decent. Have not drained the batter all the way, but my observation is that it can run for a couple of days on one charge (with moderate use).
+ Another neat design tweak is to not have an opening for the SD card on the outside cover. I load up videos and once I inserted it and put the cover back on, I'm comfortable that my toddler will not fiddle with the card or remove/damage it.

One improvement suggestion:
Update the quality of graphics in the content of the KIDOs app. The animation quality is a little on the older/outdated side. It's not a problem with so many streaming options available but the app will be more attractive with all the other features if the videos can be improved.

Overall very happy with the product!

title: Easy installation and setup
text:
This product fits my needs well because I wanted a camera in a location that doesn’t have a power outlet close by. The camera seems like it will hold up to the elements well. Every port is covered and the battery compartment is protected by a gasket. The solar panel has a generous cord length and charges the camera’s built-in 3.7V 7,800 mAh battery pack via a USB-C connection.

You must use the UBox app to configure and access this camera. A link to it is provided in the user manual via QR code. Note: when you launch the app the logo says “UBIA” not Ankway, and the app is authored by Hongbo Wang. I like that the app gives a clear indication if the battery is being charged and has an option to turn off the camera’s LED. Not surprisingly, the camera doesn’t appear to support RTSP so you’re locked into using the UBox app for recording and playback.

The camera supports class 4 or greater MicroSD cards formatted in FAT32. I installed a Samsung EVO card which was instantly recognized for local recording.

I found there to be a slight delay when using the PTZ controls and the movement wasn’t precise. If you’re not needing to adjust the camera often it’s not a big deal.

Picture quality is great during the day and at night. You can choose the spotlight or IR LEDs for nighttime illumination. Detection sensitivity offers three selections (low, medium, high) and relies on passive IR.

With its external WiFi antennas, this device gets a good signal (-63 dBm) compared to a device equidistant from my access point that has internal antennas and gets -73 dBm.

title: Fantastic charger, great for travel and for desks!
text:
This is an excellent charger, capable of 65W of total power output. I use it at my desk to charge my phone, power a wireless charger, and for misc. charging using the USB-A port.

The power distribution on this charger is excellent, meaning that with three ports used (USB-C1, USB-C2, and USB-A1), I can charge my phone at full speed, power the wireless charger with the maximum wattage it can handle, and simultaneously charge other items at 15W.

A lot of chargers in the market don't split the power this way and waste wattage, this one doesn't.

I think this would also make a great addition to travel as you can plug it in with the 6ft cable, and have your charging ports easily accessible.

The build quality is excellent and the charger works exactly as advertised, and after almost a month of constant use, I can say with confidence that it will hold up to daily use with ease!

title: A long HDMI cable with a quality feel and that works
text:
I may have gotten lucky ordering this in 10 feet, since I do not see it available in that size anymore. But it came as advertised so I am a happy camper. The other sizes are likely to reflect similarly in use.

It arrived in a simple branded box with no indication of size. The cable itself is braided and the ends are metal. There was protective pastic around the 8K logo of each end you can take off and caps to protect the actual plugs. It also came with a free velcro cable tie which I appreciated. I liked that the cable ends are not too bulky. Some HDMI cables have fat plugs but these are nice and thin.

Plugging the cable in to my PC and monitor it worked without issue. Instant high definition picture of my desktop. I have not tested it with an 4K or 8K device but I like to future proof my purchases as much as possible, so having a cable I know I can use long into the future is a nice extra.

Overall a good cable with a quality feel. I'd buy another if needed.

title: Does everything as advertised and has decent quality image too!
text:
I'm constantly searching for new web cams to improve my streaming setup, so this one seemed different enough that it was worth trying out. So far, I am not disappointed!

It came in a small, branded box and was well packaged. Inside is the camera (cable is not removable), privacy cover, remote, and instruction manual. The camera was very easy to setup, just plug and use. The cable length is not very long, only a few feet, so for some you may need an extension because you cannot just swap out the cable entirely.

The camera comes with the ability to attach it to a tripod, but the folding mount for monitor mounting is very well constructed. It comes with a third "panel" that folds out to sit flat against the back on the monitor. This helps secure it from a other point. Most other web cams just use pressure to hold against the back of the monitor, this extra folding panel ensures it doesn't slip. A nice feature, I think.

Once mounted the camera can swivel left and right AND up and down, giving you a wide range of possible positions you can set it in. The swivel isn't too loose either, so you can set it in the position you want and not worry about it being pulled back to an off position.

The privacy cover is interesting. Personally, I prefer ones that are built into the product but the freedom to move this one around is different and kind of nice. I am just afraid I will lose it. When not in use you can just move it to the back of the camera where it magnetically attaches there too.

There is an LED status light on the front of the camera that tells you if the microphone is muted or not. Pretty happy that it includes this. The camera face is also touch sensitive and when you tap it, it will turn on the ring light! Three settings are available for the light. I would describe them as "dim, bright, and blinding". Find which works best for you but for me I'll likely keep to the “dim” setting and use secondary lighting.

The camera quality is pretty good. It appears to output true 1080p at up to 60 fps. The software I use reads it as such, and provides other options like 30 fps, and even 720p and below if desired. I do feel like the image itself is a bit washed out in color, but that is something that can easily be adjusted via software and the instruction manual even includes a section to explain how. I did not test the microphone as I use a headset.

The included remote is where this webcam takes things to the next level. It allows you to turn on or off the camera, mute or unmute, zoom, mirror / flip, and brighten or darken the image. Its really cool to see all these features accessible like this. When you zoom in with the web cam, the digital zoom doesn't cause the image to pixelize, and then you can use the arrow buttons to move the image around to focus on what you want to show! This camera really wants to ensure you get the exact framing of yourself or your surroundings that you want.

I think this is an excellent webcam. Although a bit pricey compared to some cheaper webcams, it has good image quality and a ton of features that most other webcams in this price point do not offer. It’s worth the upgrade.

title: I'm Going Back to Buttons
text:
They sound good for podcasts and seal well for less outside noise and better bass. The batteries last for hours and the charging station is fantastic for how many charges it supplies before it needs charging.

But, the sensing is too sensitive, or the active area is not placed well, because these will pause, skip tracks, etc. when I am simply adjusting the fit from the sides. This will happen even when I remove them from the charger. They activate and my podcast starts playing just from my touching taking them out of the charger. They then will do various functions as I put them in.

Strange too that when I tap them correctly to correct an unwanted pause, etc., they often don't respond, or the bluetooth delay gives the impression it didn't respond. Since pause makes no acknowledgement beep, one can't tell if it detected the tap. If someone listens to music, they can more easily tell if it pauses, or plays. Spoken word is different, since it is not continuous.

I'm going back to buttons.

title: Not recommended for use with USB extender
text:
Running on a Mac. I have not reached out to support yet, but I might have to. I downloaded the Poly Lens app and applied the latest firmware before testing.
- Sound quality when streaming music was iffy. Sound was good, but the stream had a crackle (for lack of a better word) or signal drop. It was as if there was some kind of conflict on the Bluetooth. I moved over to a PC and it worked great. But on the Mac, not good. I'm using Spotify to stream, both desktop app and browser, and it's just not good with the combination of this device and a Mac. This device and a PC is fine in my limited tested,
- Speaking of Bluetooth, why do I need to use the included Bluetooth adapter? If the headset is Bluetooth, and the Mac has Bluetooth built in, why can't I discover the headset without the adapter, especially since the headset is plugged into the USB on the Mac to get its power anyway?
- Since plugging the headset in, audio seems to be unstable in MS Teams and Zoom. For example, I used a Jabra 930 prior to testing this. Today, I decided to use the Jabra for a Zoom call. I could hear the chimes when people connected, but I couldn't hear voices of people speaking. After disconnecting, unplugging the Bluetooth connector for this headset (which, remember, wasn't being used for the call) and re-connected, the call went off without a hitch.
- The one call I was in yesterday on Teams was fine. I too don't care for the placement of the Mute button, but I don't mind the indicator telling me I'm on Mute. Mute reminder is software controlled through the Poly Lens app, so I believe you can turn that off.

So still testing, but my initial impression is not that great with the Mac. Seeing that I got this for work, and my work machine is a Mac...I've got more testing/troubleshooting to do.

*** EDIT
Changing to 4 stars now that I realize the dropping signal was due to a USB extender. Sound quality is good streaming and in meetings as long as I'm plugged directly into the Mac. I can still use the extender to plug the base in and charge, but the bluetooth adapter still has to be plugged into the Mac. Still taking one star off because I have to use THEIR bluetooth adapter. This makes no sense.

title: The fan is LOUD, picture quality is only OK, mounting angle adjustability is poor
text:
I was excited by this projector having a 1080p native resolution and priced at a reasonable price but was ultimately disappointed and will continue to use an older, lower-resolution project for my home-use.

With all projectors, you're at the mercy of the "throw" angle of the projector. From ~20ft away, this projector cast an image that was approximately 7'-0" by 12'-0" which surprising fit my space perfectly. I was disappointed to find that the image at this distance was not the clearest. You could focus it at the middle of the picture but the corners would be a bit blurry. Also the fan that cools the bulb was distractingly loud. My projector setup is just in my living room so I don't play volume at movie theater volumes that might drown it out. This is very annoying for casual use.

Quite possibly my biggest complaint is that there is almost no mounting angle adjustability. There is a single "foot" at the front (near the lense) that can unscrew to prop the front of the projector up ~0.75" max but that's it. My projector would be mounted on a shelf above head level so I need to be able to prop the back of the projector up a bit which is unfortunately impossible without carefully stacking things to put the projector on. That's doable but it feels like design oversight to not include that in the projector itself.

All-in-all, this projector does project a visible image and it is reasonably priced, it just has enough frustrations that it was not able to overtake my existing lower-resolution projector as my daily-use projector.

title: Good sound, very portable, minor flaws
text:
Being a Gen Xer I grew up on vinyl, so we recently tried out another record player we found on amazon but it was so cheap and poorly made it sounded like it was being played through a tin can and even a pristine new album skipped constantly. Back it went. I assumed they would all be that bad but then I saw this one and the video review which lets you hear how it sounds. It intrigued me enough to go for it, and I am glad we did, although when it arrived it was smaller and lighter than we imagined so I had doubts. It literally looks like a toy, not a real record player. But we gave it a go and lo and behold, it sounds pretty good. Obviously not as full and rich as a real turntable with receiver and speakers but this fills in nicely and it is tiny, so it's easy to make a space for it and move it around.

Two drawbacks for me. First, no headphone jack. I don't use wireless headphones or Bluetooth so I am hoping I can find a splitter to use the speaker output jacks but we shall see.

Second, you cannot close the lid with an LP on the turntable, because the whole thing is so small. If you have a 45 on there you can, but I play mostly LPs and anyone used to record players knows you sometimes want to close the lid to keep dust out or keep your album ready for the next time. Not a big deal, just a small oversight.

But honestly, if you have a vinyl collection and miss having a record player handy, this will do. And so far even my ancient, dusty albums which appear scratched have played very well. Zero skips on the ones in good shape, unlike that last terrible player, and only a few skips on my weathered old albums. It's a bonus to have a radio, wish it also had a cassette deck! Oh the joys of the mix tape, kids. I'll make sure the next one has it all. ;)

title: The Good - The Bad - and The Ugly
text:
The Good;
Hold your tablet comfortably with one hand. Securely with no effort. Slide your hand in, adjust the strap, rotate the holder to any position. It is absolutely comfortable. Long use, no problem. Sitting, standing, walking, sitting in a car. It really is versatile. The stand works great. Adjustable in increments all the way along its length. Locate the handle along one side, you can set it on a table and watch it in landscape mode or lengthwise.

The Bad;
It is permanent !!!! 😡
This is a permanent fixture onto your tablet. All that wonderful slim sexy stuff it has, is gone. This thing is huge. Mobility is gone. No longer will your tablet fit nicely into your backpack. No longer will that beautiful protective, expensive case fit. No way to protect the screen in travel. No cover, no protection, not easily packed or traveled, it will never fit flat again.

The Ugly;
This thing is ugly. The tablet is sleek and sexy, add the handle, it's just ugly.
Sadly, all the wonderful stuff this handle does is heavily outweighed by the negatives it brings. 😢 If this could be unattached and reattached it would be wonderful, but it's not. I have now removed it. Protecting the tablet and being able to transport it are just far more important than comfortably holding it. Even removing it was horrible. It was difficult to remove. title: Great price but the colors are way off.
text: I liked the idea of the privacy door on this camera and I had a very old Microsoft Lifechat camera that seemed to flicker and not auto-focus right compared to other video participants in my meetings.  The price was right on this eMeet C960 Webcam so I gave it a try.  I was shocked at how bad the color rendering was with the camera.  Using Zoom with a bright green greenscreen and a navy blue shirt, I became a floating head in the rendered screen.  The color vibrance and differences between the colors were not captured by the C960 webcam.  I looked dingy but the camera otherwise focused just fine.  If you plan to use this camera with a greenscreen, this is not the camera for you.  See my attached photo which shows a direct comparison between what my old Microsoft Lifechat camera captured vs. the eMeet C960 Webcam for the color of my greenscreen.  The vibrant green that the Lifechat camera captured was accurate.  The grey dingy green that the C960 captured was inaccurate and resulted in other colors also being similar enough to it that either the greenscreen was not detected or everything except my face was considered the background color.  This is an ok camera (not great) for no green backgrounds but not at all ideal for greenscreen situations.

title: Good solution for keeping touchscreens smudge free
text:
I use a touchscreen laptop daily, but often don't notice how smudged the screen becomes until I step away and the light hits at the perfect angle to show each and every smudge!

Some experts recommend spraying this sort of solution onto a suitable cloth (like microfiber) and then using the dampened cloth to clean the screen. I understand this is to help prevent the solution from penetrating the screen and causing damage.

I, however, typically just spray a modest amount of the solution on the screen and then use a microfiber cleaner to wipe off the solution and the smudges. I have a spray container that nests in a case covered in microfiber. So I can transfer the solution in these bottles to the smaller spray bottle and always have everything needed to keep my screens clean handy.

So far I haven't experienced any problems in cleaning my screens in this fashion. I'll leave to everyone else the method they wish to use, but this method has served me well. And with this volume of cleaning solution I'll be able to keep my screens smudge free for months to come. This solution is supposed to be safe for all types of electronic screens. My experience thus far seems to bear that out.

title: Great Cooler even Better Price
text:
I got this for my Ryzen 7 2700x, since I built this system a couple years ago I have been using the stock wraith prism which was annoyingly loud (I mean loud like an aircraft taking off when the fan spun up). I don't overclock beyond what Ryzen does on its own as I prefer a super stable system so I really didnt track my temps, but I can tell you when I would play games I know it would get warm as I could hear the wraith start screaming.

So I got this and it was a quick and easy install, basically take the wraith off, clean the old thermal paste off, remove 4 screws and the plastic brackets for the wraith, put down 4 spacers, place 2 metal brackets, 4 new screws , new thermal paste (comes with thermal paste but I used my MX-4), place cooler, tighten screws (it even comes with a really decent screwdriver if you dont have a long shaft one), install fan, and boom you're done, total time maybe 30 minutes. I used the supplied fan, and then I set it up as push pull and used another 120mm fan I had (they give you enough hardware to mount another fan)

Now my system runs nice and cool, and even my other case fans don't seem to have to run full speed to keep everything cool. and the quietness is taking some getting used to.

Bottom Line, its a great cooler and it is a very good value, I can even use all 4 ram slots without issues as it doesnt cover the 1st 2 slots. its quiet and does a good job. So if you're looking for a good cooling solution and don't want or need RGB puke (Im not into RGB) its a solid buy for you.

title: Mininum Requirements
text:
I am using this tablet since a couple of weeks. I find these cheap off-brand tablets a mixed bag. On one side they provide a lot of computer for the price, on the other side they scrape on the lower end of what most want on performance.
I like them because I can use them for things I wouldn't put an expensive tablet through, or as a backup. They work great to have recipes on hand in the kitchen without being worried about spills or greasy fingers. I use one when I work on cars for manuals, ODB2 diagnostics, and listening to music. I have one in my emergency backpack packet with map material, emergency information, and scanned documents, in case I we have to leave the house in a hurry leaving everything behind. That's great and works for me, but I can't deny that these are slow. WiFi connections are inconsistent and slow, battery time isn't that great, and more demanding apps suffer from performance issues. A well kept second hand device from a known brand will most of the time outperform these budget devices. So while the prices are tempting, keep in mind that there is still a profit margin for everybody involved. Meaning that the actual product is even cheaper than the price tag reflects. Need a device for mails, docs, home automation, watching movies, this one will do. But even a simple video conference is too much. I hope this helps to make a decision.

text:
I called TCL within two hours of delivery. I HATE THE REMOTE. I am not the only one. It has a volume control on the side which you easily hit by accident (if right-handed), and there are 4 quick buttons at the bottom that are always live for netflix, hulu, roku and espn. These will ALWAYS take you somewhere even when you do not have accounts. You cannot reprogram them. You cannot disable them. If you google reprogramming you will find a lot of annoyed people who actually remove the button and fill it in to stop it from being so annoying. This is particularly annoying when other roku-tv-remotes have other choices (such as Amazon). TCL says that they have no other (eg. aftermarket universal) remote recommendations. They did however help me to set up the page I want to see when the tv first comes on (it doesn't have to be the home page that is cluttered with all the stuff you don't have).
Mechanically, the tv seems great. The picture is very sharp and clear -- better than the Vizio tv it replaces although both had the same resolution. That tv was 8 years old and just kep getting dumber and dumber (no you tube, no skype) and then eventually all the hdmi ports stopped working. So I am happy with the tv, and thrilled with the price, but the remote is a deal-breaker for me.

title: Beautiful Feature-Packed Monitor
text:
For the price this is a great monitor IF you want it for gaming and IF you are OK gaming at 1080p.

IMPORTANT: Since this is an AMD Freesync monitor, you should really only buy this if you have a Freesync compatible graphics card (otherwise you're paying extra for functionality you won't use). That said, if you have one this should sync up with no issue (my RX 480 immediately recognized it as compatible).

A nice bonus is that this monitor has a 75Hz refresh rate instead of the standard 60, which results in smoother gameplay if your card is capable of 75 FPS at 1080p. The 4 ms refresh rate is nice (but also expected at this price point). While this not being 120Hz is a bit of disappointment (120 Hz at 1080p is a current sweet spot for gaming machines), at this price its understandable, especially given the inclusion of Freesync.

The monitor itself is very striking, with almost no bezels and a thin profile. I personally love the look (there is even a fun textured circle pattern on the base), but its important to note if you use an monitor mounted webcam or similar. Since there are practically no bezels that sort of solution won't work as well on this monitor.

The monitor itself is an IPS monitor, which means great viewing angles and good color accuracy. With my Spyder5Pro I measured 97% RGB, 70% NTSC, and 75% AdobeRGB. These are good values for gaming and everyday use, but not sufficient for professional photography, videography, or similar. The monitor also shipped with washed out colors - calibration made a noticeable improvement to the display.

Overall I'm very, very happy with this monitor. It includes all the right features at the right price, with nothing extra (i.e. no speakers, which is a plus here in my mind as it cuts down on the price and keeps the display thinner). Beyond that, its stylish, fairly lightweight, and a breeze to setup with Freesync.

My only complaint so far is the color accuracy out of the box - its still very pretty, but there being such a noticeable improvement from calibration is a bit disappointing ... I would have liked it better calibrated out of the box, without the need for professional calibration tools.

text:
I have had Acer computers in the past and they've been real workhorses that needed to be replaced due to obsolescence, not any failure of the computer itself. I expect this Chromebook will be the same. Sturdy, well made, and solid without being heavy at all.

Pros:
1. It does not get hot like my laptop when I have it resting on my legs and mess around on it for an extended period of time. This may be common with Chromebooks but I don't know as this is the first one I've owned.
2. The battery life seems to be great. I've used it for several hours, playing videos and music that I would expect to run down the battery, but it is still holding on. I have had it for just over 5 weeks and I haven't had to charge it yet. I wish my (another brand) tablet held a charge like this. It's not getting heavy use, but even leaving it idle for a long period of time doesn't seem to drain the battery. Gotta love that!

Neutral:
1. The built in speakers could be better. They're absolutely fine for a laptop or Chromebook, but I had hoped for better sound. They are CLEAR and you can hear dialogue with no issues, but I just kind of hoped for a richer sound. Not really a negative as this isn't really the type of product that would be expected to have amazing sound.
2. I miss a touchscreen. This is NOT a touchscreen, and doesn't need to be. I just happen to love them, and miss it on this one. That's a personal preference, so I can't really call it a negative. My husband is primarily using this Chromebook, and I'm using the touchscreen one (same brand). He's happy without the touchscreen, but I miss it so much.

Con:
1. Is this really a con? Since this is my first Chromebook, I guess I didn't understand the limitations. I had hoped/expected to run some of my games on this (a Star Wars game in particular). It's available on Google Play, but doesn't run on the Chrome OS platform. My mistake for not looking into this a little bit before obtaining the Chromebook, and I don't think this is really a con as much as it is a warning that if there is something you REALLY want to play/use this Chromebook for, make sure you can before you purchase.

Overall, this Chromebook is amazing and does 99% of everything I had hoped. I'm very happy with it, and wouldn't hesitate to give one as a gift, or buy another one when I ultimately need to replace this one.

One final note: Before you buy ANY Chromebook, be sure to check with Google to see how long that model will be updated. Once the updates end, you have to plan on replacing. This particular Chromebook is set to be updated until JUNE 2029. You have PLENTY of time to enjoy it, and no worries that it will be obsolete within a few years.

title: Pretty Incredible for the Price
text: One hundred and twenty Gigabytes isn't very much these days, but this thing only cost me like $10 on sale a few weeks ago. It's not the fastest SSD, and it doesn't have a DRAM cache, and the manufacturer's warranty isn't that long and would probably be difficult use, but for the price of a cheap USB flash drive, getting an actual SSD is pretty impressive.  I put this in a $10 SATA enclosure, and for around $20, I've got a 120GB USB 3.0 SSD, pretty nice. Yes, you can get a 128GB USB flash drive for less, but USB flash drives have incredibly slow write speeds, with poor endurance, while this one does not. Also, when used as the boot drive for a legacy PC (or Mac (though I haven't tried that), for ten bucks you'll get 6 - 10X better performance than you'd get with a hard drive, assuming you don't need to store that much data on it (or use the Cloud).

title: Say goodbye to PCI!
text:
Let's face it, most new motherboards are going with more PCI-E 1x slots and less standard PCI slots as time progresses. More often than not, the layout of modern mainboards almost always guarantees that your PCI slot will be blocked by something (I'm looking at you double wide graphics card!).

Almost as common of a dilemma is the chance of your integrated network adapter dying on you.

This particular gigabit adapter works a charm, although I recommend using the official TP-Link drivers from their website. I had a few bugs with the automatically installed Windows drivers and/or the Realtek drivers. Eventually I went to TP-Link's website and got the official drivers and now it works like a charm using Win7 x64!

text:
This tablet works all right for basic needs like browsing the internet and streaming shows. It's not as fast, and the picture is not quite as crisp, as other more expensive tablets, but it's perfectly acceptable for light usage, and the screen is a good size.

It was easy to set up and has the standard settings you'll find in any android tablet.

The one weird thing is how the buttons are set up for the power and volume. It seems like I have to hold it upside down for the buttons to make sense in portrait mode. This places the power button in the lower right, which just seems strange. If I hold it so the power button is in the upper left, then the volume buttons are reversed, with the higher one making the volume lower. It's not a huge deal, but there are certain intuitive aspects to using electronic devices, and this is certainly not intuitive to me.

title: Nice alarm with remote & mounts easily. Plastic cable ties attach it. Fourth purchase.
text:
USABILITY...
It is relatively loud (I would like one louder!) and easy to install. It is reasonably sensitive as most wind gusts won't trigger it but it does trigger when my other alarm goes off (have to turn this alarm on last). I use it on the bike in conjunction with another motion alarm and a disk brake lock/alarm. These will go on fencing.

I actually got these to put on fencing around my bikes (probably with Velcro) so people moving the fencing to get at my bikes will set off the alarms before getting to the bikes. The remote control ability is a blessing here.

MOUNTING...
I would have paid more if it could have been mounted to water bottle bosses which it then covered so as to not be readily removable, or otherwise locked/attached permanently to the bike frame or fence/building/whatever. Even stainless steel cable ties (maybe similar to auto hose clamps) would have been better. It uses batteries which would be almost impossible to change if permanently glued to the bike frame or structure.

title: Great choice
text:
I use a lot of flash drives for video, and my playback devices all require FAT32. I was able to reformat the drive to FAT32 with no problem. Files transferred fast (not to advertised speeds, but that is the fault of my computer, not the drive). Flash drives tend to be durable, as I've seen more than one (not mine) go through the washer and dryer.
As flash drives continue to drop in price, it just makes sense to load up on them to backup and store your data, and this sells for a reasonable price. I like that the red LED shows the drive activity so that you can verify visually that it is working and being recognized by the computer. All in all, this appears to be a solid choice.

title: A nice, basic tablet at a great price
text: This is a very generic, basic tablet that runs Android 11.0.  It has a decent but not super bright screen.  It is really a good tablet in one way: no "garbage apps" put in by the manufacturer. It is totally "Google".  Which is great if you use Google apps a lot, and I do.  The camera? Well, you get what you pay for.  The placement of the camera lens in the middle horizontally instead of vertically is both good and bad.  The best photos are taken wide.  But holding it the wide way is a bit harder.  It is in solid and sturdy plastic shell, feels good and put together well. Battery life is normal, depends on use, you'll get at least 5 hours.  It is not super speedy if you are used to a higher end tablet, phone, computer. But it is a great basic "starter" Android tablet for seniors and younger people without spending a ton of money.  You get what you pay for, but with this, you get a lot more!

title: Decent, discrete, good volume
text: This is a smaller sized sound bar. I think that for the price, it should have a bit better bass sound.  It is slim, though, has a nice simple look that blends in easily into the background.  The sound is okay. The bass is "just enough" when on "Movie" setting.  On the other two settings, there is only squeaky midrange and highs.  As for the midrange and highs, again, the settings only really make it sound good on "Movie" where the highs and lows are pumped up a bit.  It is versatile, many ways to connect. Easy to set up fast, remote is okay, simple design.  Overall, for the price, just about what you'd get, but there are other choices out there.

title: Very good sound, full bass and nice looks
text: Easy to set up and use.  Fast Bluetooth connection.  Lights around the front can be turned off for extra battery time, but they are nice and not too obnoxious.  The bass is full and loud.  The Equalizer has four modes, and only one is really useful for me, the "music" setting. The bass eq setting just seems to reduce the treble rather than increase bass.  The music setting balances it nicely,  it seems to be a "W" curve equalizer mode, high bass and treble and low mid-range.  That's what I prefer. The others, especially the "audiobook" eq setting, I won't ever use.  Tinny and just mediocre, takes no advantage of the really nice sound this puts out.  Weighs a decent weight, and that's good, that means the speakers are good and at 30W, it gives really decent loud volume sound,  minimal bit of distortion at the bass end when turned up full on loud songs, not noticeable unless you are really quiet and listening and reviewing.  The finish, textured black and solid, feels good and like it should last.  Overall, for the price, this is a very nice speaker.

text:
After a lot of reviewing specs, comparing prices, and considering customer reviews I decided on this system, and I am very happy that I did. In my opinion this is the best value for the money in terms of quality and value. The cameras are truly "plug and play". I purchased a separate 32" TV to use as a dedicated monitor on Amazon for $130.00. This is a better option then buying a system that comes with a monitor as those monitors are typically very small and if you want that size for viewing just download the app to your phone or tablet. I downloaded the app to my phone and can check in LIVE at anytime as well.

Customer service is great too. They are very concerned about providing good customer service and that is very important to me. I called the customer service number because had a couple of questions during setup that were addressed promptly. They were patient and very informative. Another reason I had to contact customer service was to inquire about additional cameras because I did not see any individual cameras for my system on Amazon. PLEAS NOTE: If you purchase the 4 camera system and decide to add additional cameras you will have to contact the customer service number to have them send you a link to purchase the additional cameras on Amazon.

The setup is very easy. I am not technical and I was able to get all 4 cameras online in seconds. One thing I would like to mention - once I got the 4 cameras setup I decided that I would like more coverage and wanted to add additional cameras. It is much easier and cheaper if you buy more than you need (i.e. 8 camera system) than to have to purchase more after the fact. Lesson learned, but not a big deal. Still the best system for the money.

I installed my cameras outside. Unless you have access to electrical outlets that are convenient to where you want to mount the cameras you will need to have someone that is familiar with light electrical work to install the cameras and wire them into you electrical source. This can be expensive or inexpensive - totally dependent on who you hire. At first I contacted a company that primarily installed security systems and got a quote of $800 for 4 cameras, I tried a few handyman sites and got quotes around $240 for 4 cameras, then I contacted TAKL.com and I was able to get the 4 cameras installed for $120! FYI - on their site this was considered a SMALL ELECTRICAL job.

title: Could be awesome, but it really depends on your specific laptop
text:
First, a number of other reviewers mentioned the stiffness in adjusting this. They are correct, and also correct that once you get it right, it feels extremely solid!

My problem is that I have a very old, very large, very heavy laptop. At any reasonable angle for me, it *slides off* the front of the stand. It "fits" fine, but the laptop is heavy enough that the front "hooks" (their terminology) don't grab the laptop securely enough.

In other words, the stand is as sturdy as you would like, it doesn't budge or rock or fall over, but the laptop itself just slides off the stand.

That makes it useless for me, but I could see this being extremely useful to most laptop owners who are interested in elevating their machines.

I am rating this a 4 (instead of a 5, even though it doesn't work for me), because the hooks in the front are generally simply too "shallow" in my opinion (though I do believe they will hold most laptops effectively). If they were curved upward a bit more, or simply "taller", they would accommodate all laptops up to 17".

I still recommend this for most users (I just wish I was one of them!).

EDIT: it occurred to me right after I hit submit that perhaps I could "build up" the "hooks" myself. I grabbed two large binder clips and was able to create a barrier that stopped my laptop from sliding off. A little kludgy, sure, but it now works exactly as I had hoped. Photo now included with the binder clips attached!

title: Easy, affordable option to add carplay
text:
We have an older car that didn't include carplay, and really wanted to look at finding a solution to add it. The other vehicles we have includes it, and it's become a lifesaver for both my wife and I while in the car for podcasts, music, calls, and texting. Instead of having to fork out close to this $250 price just for a new carplay system that would have to be installed, we were lucky enough to find this dash option. I didn't even realize these existed, which is a great option for those with older cars not wanting to pay for the expense of having one installed.

It comes in a generic box, with the actual screen found on the top in bubble wrap. Below that, you'll find find the cables for power (cigarette lighter), a cable to plug into the AUX port, assuming your car has one, a stand/mount, and the manual.

Setup is extremely easy. You put the actual display on the stand, and then mount it to your car dash. You plug in the power on the left side, and then to your cigarette lighter, and it comes to life. If you prefer to use a USB cable, you can plug in your phone directly into the screen (also on the left). After authorizing the device on your iPhone (sorry, I don't have an android device to test Android Auto), Carplay pulls up and works as expected. Touching the screen works as expected, and there really isn't a lag when swiping between screens.

This unit also features wireless carplay, which is awesome. I, however, have had a hit/miss experience with wireless carplay. To setup wireless, you select the wifi network which is broadcast from the device on your iPhone. It pairs up also via bluetooth, and then makes the connection. Generally, for me, it works, but there are the few times that it just wouldn't connect after starting the car. I can't tell you why exactly. I'd say 90% of the time it works without a hitch. You power up your car, the screen starts up, and within a minute or so, you're connected. The other times, it just didn't seem to connect. I'd show the wifi network and bluetooth connected on my iphone 13 pro, but carplay wouldn't appear.

If your car has bluetooth, this can connect to your car's bluetooth to allow for audio to come through the speakers via bluetooth, which is nice. Otherwise, you need to just plug in the included AUX cable into your car. Depending on your car, you may or may not have such a port.

Overall, I'm happy with this. I'll probably stick to using a USB cable versus wireless, but it is nice to have the option for wireless during the quick trip, if needed. Price wise, again, this isn't bad for what it is, especially.

title: Decent USB C powered soundbar
text:
[[VIDEOID:19ff5245499eed04b8aff29bcf53e689]] This review is for the Razer Leviathan V2 X.
I ordered this soundbar to replace an old 2.1 desktop computer speaker set to save space because my desk has limited real estate and I want to reduce the number of wires as well.

The Razer Leviathan only has 1 USB C cable to connect and definitely fit my space requirements. Keep in mind this soundbar is USB powered via the single USB C cable.

The build quality is definitely good and above average. The soundbar is encased in a hard plastic shell with a smooth matte finish. The front is covered in speaker fabric. Physically the Leviathan V2 X gives the impression of quality.

However, sound quality and price is where the biggest problem is. The sound just does not live up to my expectations for the price. The sound is how hollow and lacks depth. There is little to no bass. The bass that is there sounds boomy especially at high volume. Voices however are clear and midrange frequencies sound decent even at high volume.

If you consider that this soundbar uses only 1 cable for both power and audio signal then you might judge it against other USB powered speakers and the Leviathan would be considered above average. However, the price puts this soundbar into a different level of expectations.

The best use cases or scenarios for this sound bar is for listening to voice audio, and pop music. If you watch a lot of movies, play games, or listen to bass heavy music then you'll probably find the sound lacking. It'll do the job but you'll feel like something is missing in the sound.

Overall 3 stars. The Leviathan V2 X is good to above average for being solely USB powered soundbar, but it lacks value.
At $100 it competes with other products that have a better sound profile, but if you are absolutely only looking at a USB C soundbar, and you're prioritizing simplicity and compactness, then definitely consider this Leviathan V2 X.

title: Great budget earbuds
text:
At the time of writing this review, these earbuds were about $20. As such, they will be reviewed knowing that they only cost that much!
This is a no frills pair of wireless earbuds. You won’t get noise cancellation or won’t be able to change settings on the sound.
What do they do? They provide you wireless sound at an affordable price!
It comes with the Bluetooth earbuds, the case, ear tips, and a usb C charging cable.
The case feels like a $20 case. Glossy plastic. It works though. And you know what it provides that other high end buds don’t? A screen with the case’s battery percentage and a graphical battery indicator for each of the earbuds. That’s amazing for such an affordable pair of earbuds. Why don’t other brands do this, when this one can?
The earbuds themselves work well. They connected to my iPhone right away and provided sound. That’s all I need them to do. I’m not an audiophile. I just need sound to come out of them. I can listen to music and watch videos with them. And it works.
What I don’t really like are the touch controls. It’s very difficult to get any function out of the touch controls and I just don’t bother trying to use it. I just use my phone to control volume, play/pause, etc.
But for the price, they work just fine and the digital read out is a great plus.

text:
I'll go over the good and the bad

The good-
- Very wide range of magnification, 28-233x is exceptional at this price point. Usually max you'll see is around 150-175x
- Comes with a bag that fits absolutely everything
- Comes with a 5x finder scope
- Tripod itself is tall enough for teens and smaller adults, which is much more than others at this price point
- Optics themselves aren't bad either. I'd say this is above average when it comes to clarity, color reproduction and chromatic aberration.

The bad
- The tripod is extremely wobbly and sensitive to movement, made worse by the fact that you have a 233x magnification option. I think I would have paid a little extra for a better tripod, this is just basically a good camcorder tripod and not meant for something this powerful.
