title: amazing sounding headphones for this price range!
text:
I am not an audiophile, but I do buy a handful of under-$100 wireless headphones every year given that I spend most of my day writing and need music/podcasts to drown out the world around me. But I also record my own music and use wired Audio-Technica M-50’s for that, so I have a fairly good sense of ideal headphone sound quality, at least in the sub $500 range.

So, with that in mind, I am pleased to report that these Ankbit E500’s are quite excellent. I would say for pure sound quality they are the best I’ve ever head in the wireless under-$100 category, edging out even my Anker Soundcore Q20’s. The sound profile is relatively neutral, with precise non-boxy/non-thuddy bass and boasting an excellent (wide-ish) soundstage. I listened to a variety of music – live 68 Grateful Dead, experimental violinist Tony Conrad, my own low-fi indie rock, and Kylie Minogue’s hyper-polished pop album Disco – and everything sounded fantastic: good detail, good separation, and no weirdness with the EQ’ing.

As for the noise cancelling, I don’t generally use ANC, but I tried it on the Ankbit and it worked very well. The noise of my window fan was nearly blocked at about 5 feet with JUST the ANC on (ie: no music), and with the music playing, it gave a good sense of being in an enclosed listening space. I honestly don’t understand the point of “transparency mode” but I found that it amplified certain environmental sounds, making them sound louder than they do with all of the ANC off. I’m not sure if that’s the point, but I didn’t use it for long and could do without it.

Everything else was what you would expect from a quality pair of sub-$100 wireless cans – build quality was good, phone calling worked fine, and the pairing with Bluetooth was painless.

The only thing it lacked is the audio notification for pairing and battery status. So there is no accented computer voice saying “battery MEDIUM” or whatever when you power them on/off. Indeed, there seems to be no way to monitor the battery level, butI’ve been using them all week, charging only while I sleep, and they never ran out of juice.

So, TLDR, I would absolutely recommend these excellent sounding headphones for anyone looking in the under $100 range for quality music/podcast listening and phone-call making. I did receive them for free as a Vine review, but I would absolutely buy these again on my own.

title: Hugely dissappointing.
text:
[[VIDEOID:d26a63514b7c6b10b3ed98584e8cdf70]] Plantronics by Poly Voyager Focus 2 UC Wireless Headset with Microphone & Charge Stand - Active Noise Canceling (ANC) - Connect PC/Mac/Mobile via Bluetooth -Works w/Teams, Zoom & More-Amazon Exclusive

Well these wont be replacing my opencomms. Maybe my expectations were too high, but this was an incredibly frustrating experience. Starting with 5 separate sheets of documentation with microscopic letters none of which were a proper manual. Woefully inadequate all the way around. Says to download poly lens app. So went to the place you get apps and this does not exist. Yet. There is a plantronics hub app. Supposed to be able to update firmware, connect and tweak thru the app. No. App does not recognize headset. App is useless. Beyond useless because it actually makes you angry.

Once i was finally able to connect headset to phone it seemed to work fine and sounded decent for an on ear headset. So the phone app was a bust so i went to their website and downloaded their software. The stuff there was actually very clunky there are actually two places to do the same thing and only one works You only find this out by struggling through the first one that doesn't work. So as matter of course the first thing I do with an electronics item is update firmware and this was a problem. Software has a page where you select your headset and it brings up like a battery level the current firmware and then upgrade firmware option so you press the upgrade firmware button and it does nothing and says failed try again. It doesn't give you any information doesn't tell you what to do. So after about a dozen fails I did some searching and there was another place to do the firmware but you have to do the Bluetooth receiver first and then you have to plug in the headset with the cable to the computer to upgrade the firmware This was not clear and it was super frustrating. It does not give you instructions. So finally got firmware updated There are no notes on what you just did so you don't know what the updates included so that's great-- not. Was able to find the or I should say a manual under "focus 2 series" which brings up only a desktop landline model which isn't relevant to this particular headset so I don't know what they save by not actually providing a proper manual for this headset but that's just nonsense. $$$

Anyway once we got past that I have the Bluetooth dongle attached to the computer I'm able to have the headset connected to my computer I was able to do voice typing. Then i was able to listen to a music app and a video app simultaneously which was fantastic The sound is not bad it is not great but it is not bad. While you're connected to the computer switching to the phone is basically seamless if you use your phone dialer that's pretty nifty. However while connected to the computer the headset did disconnect from my phone on several occasions for no apparent reason. and I don't know what the reason is for that but my normal headset that I use on the regular doesn't have this problem but it also doesn't simultaneously connect to the computer and to the phone so I don't know if it's a phone issue if it's a headset issue if it's a combination of all those moving parts not going to fault it for that.

The other stuff's enough.

I don't think this headset is streamlined for mobile use I think it's really designed for someone who does zoom calls on a computer all day long I think for that use case it's great however the last nitpick and it's a big one is the noise cancellation is just utter garbage. First of all it's on ear headphones so you're going to get ambient noise because you don't have an air seal around your ear or within your ear it's resting on top of your ear and your ear is uneven so any air that can get through means noise can get through. They head set is incapable of compensating for that. so I had a TV on and I was listening to music and I could hear the TV bright as day I tried all the different noise cancellation settings and I honestly don't think it did much Maybe 5 to 10 decibel change I don't know I'm guessing at that number but it wasn't much I would say it basically accomplished nothing. If you need noise cancellation you need over ear encapsulation or inner ear buds to seal the ear canal. Then some extra mics to phase out the extraneous noise. These do not accomplish that.

I just cannot recommend these headphones. especially for the asking price. all these things should be seamless there should be no issues There should be a proper manual The noise cancellation should work there's just so many things that didn't make the grade. Horribly dissappointing.

title: Excellent price, comfortable, OK sound, Terrible mic
text:
I did not see these Kurdene S9 headphones until after I purchased the S8s. I would recommend these over the S8s. I purchased the S9s for just $9, they fit well in my ears, the sound is more than adequate for my daily use. As I've lost/broken my fair share of headphones/earbuds, etc. I had been considering these as a backup. Having now used them for a few days, I'm thinking I want to buy a few more to replace these when I inevitably break/loose them.

CASE
The S9 case is easier to open than the S8 case. The S9 case is also the small rectangular shape popular with a lot of manufacturers. It can easily fit in a pocket, the S8 case does not. The only downside with the case is the placement of the buds - it's a little more difficult to get the first bud out due to having little space between them - they need to be gripped firmly because the magnets holding them in are quite strong. Once one is out, there's more than enough space to easily get the second bud out. So good, but could be better. They've included a feature I haven't seen on more expensive brands - an led indicator that tells you the battery percentage of the case and shows you when the buds are charging. I've had some buds in the past and it's usually a guessing game, it's great that you don't have to wonder with these.

SOUND
They don't have the best sound, but for casual listening, I'd say they are more than adequate. You cannot hear the lowest bass frequencies if that is important to you.

COMFORT AND FIT
These are very comfortable. They're light, they sit in my small ears well and they don't feel like they're about to fall out at all times like I experienced with the S8. They have a shorter bit that goes in ear compared to the S8, meaning it needs some pushing to go deep enough for a "seal". The S9s can sit comfortably in my ears sort of before the seal point or be pushed in for a more secure, sealed fit.

I move a lot in my sleep. Before I realized the buds could put in far enough for a seal, I thought I'd try sleeping with them in - they didn't fall out! I've had hair ties fall out. I've fallen asleep with wired headphones in - no matter the type or fit, they fall out.

MIC:
I recorded my voice with no background noise and with background noise to compare. It's OK with no background noise, but it's terrible with crowd noise playing in the background. I would not recommend these for phone calls if you're on the go a lot or if a TV/children are making noise in the background - the person on the other end will hear everything.

FINAL THOUGHTS:
These are comfortable, small, and lightweight. At time of purchase they are $8. They play music and podcasts well enough. I would not use these for phone calls because of the microphone. They make a good backup pair, and potentially a good pair for a child who isn't making tons of calls and is just watching TV.

These are better in every way than the S8s (except perhaps, the mic - I decided the other factors made it not worth it even if it has the best mic), but after a ton of searching, I didn't see the S9s. The S8s are advertised on every headphone listing on Amazon and they have really good reviews considering all the issues I experienced with them. It's entirely possible to get good products on a budget, but some reviews seem to be people rating them with the price point in mind. At time of purchase, the S9s were under $10, the S8s were under $15 and the S9s are far superior. I dislike that Kurdene listed them as a color option with two very different style headphones, because the reviews for three different styles are mixed in.

They may in the future remove a version, which is why I mentioned that I am reviewing the S9s.

title: Great price for the quantity
text:
First of all, this is a fantastic deal for a quantity of 100 RJ45 CAT6 connectors. Note that you do need a crimping tool that has the cutter for pass through connectors. Otherwise, you'll be left with difficult to trim wires dangling from the business end of the connector!

Prior to these connectors, I had only used non-pass through connectors. Lining up the wires, and getting them exactly the right length was a challenge, but it can be managed after doing a couple of practice runs. These connectors take all the guesswork out of it though. If you inserted the wires in the incorrect order, you can pull them out and try again fairly easily. With a non-pass through connector, you can try to do the same, but sometimes seeing the connectors through all the plastic can be challenging.

The only nit with these connectors is the somewhat overly tight fit with my monoprice 24awg cat6 stranded UTP cable. Other than that, these are pretty great.

title: Perfect sized carrying sleeve for your 15.6" laptop, not too big, lots of room, excellent quality.
text:
I'm a big fan of "just the right sized" laptop case/bag, otherwise known as the "sleeve". I recently got a 15.6" laptop and needed a bigger sleeve, and this one fit the bill perfectly.

First off is the looks, it has a nice high quality tasteful design, it also has the build quality to go with those looks. Works and feels as good as it looks. Most importantly it fits my 15.6" notebook perfectly, just enough space without being loose, well padded without being bulky, especially around the edges where the hardest hits are likely to happen. It also has a nice sized front compartment as well that can hold your power cord, travel mouse, wallet, sunglasses, etc.

It has a traditional carry handle at the top, great for the normal transport around work, office or the occasionally coffee shop. But I do travel a lot on planes, and I am very fond of the back strap that allows the sleeve to be securely placed on top of a standard travel suitcase or carryon, the ones with a retractable handle for the sleeve to attach to. Note that the outside material is water resistant, not proof. Fine for the rain and spilling drinks, but as with any bag, don't risk dropping the whole thing in water or heavy soaking.

Overall, very impressed with this laptop sleeve, highly recommend.

Now after about 3 months it's starting to act kind of stupid. It's really hard to get the screen to wake when you lift your arm up. It frequently and randomly opens the menu screen to change the watch face (which takes three distinct clicks to reach), so sometimes I look at my watch and the screen is completely different. The touch screen itself isn't great quality, and at times requires multiple attempts to swipe or push the right button, but will also click buttons I'm just trying to scroll passed. It's getting increasingly frustrating as the days go on. The battery always seems to die so early, so I've started plugging it in when it gets close to 30%. I also cut like two inches off the wrist strap because it was absurdly long and annoying.

I definitely got what I paid for... but I'll probably be on the search for a new one and be giving this one to my nephew to have as a toy.

title: Great bang for the buck
text:
After my Samsung UN32EH5300 32-Inch 1080p TV died right before my eyes, after 9+ years of use, I needed a new TV ASAP. My research led me to this one. It was about the cheapest 1080P set that I could find next to the Insignia. Reading a few professional reviews made me select this TV and, though I have only had it for a day, I am very pleased with it. This review will be about set up and initial impressions.

My Samsung had a great picture and I had a ZVOX sound bar which I bought with it in 2013 hooked to it. Also a Blu-Ray player, and OTA antennae and Roku Express player. I pulled the old set out and just swapped the new set in, even using the old Samsung power cord, to avoid pulling that cable as it was buried between my TV cabinet and the wall. As soon as I plugged the power in the set up began and I was finished in about five minutes, ZVOX, OTA antenna, Blu-Ray and Roku Express all worked as soon as I selected which HDMI or other connector they were attached to. I didn't even have to set up my ZVOX sound bar, it just worked with the new set when plugged into the optical audio connector on the back.

I initially used the Roku Express because it was not immediately apparent how to find the MAC address for the TV. It is not mentioned in the manual and I have a MAC filter set up on my router. It also worked without any setup besides plugging it in. BTW, to find the MAC address, just try adding the TV to a network and instead of setting the password, select Help and it will show the MAC address. After I found the MAC address, I was easily able to connect to the Internet and update the software on the TV and connect to Roku. For the time being, I am using the Roku Express so I don't have to worry about updating my passwords to all of the services that I have.

So setup was super easy.

I do not like the flimsy feet. I prefer the solid floor mount on my old Samsung TV which is centered and sits on top of my ZVOX sound bar. The TCL feet, besides being flimsy, sit too far apart and straddle my ZVOX. I am temporarily just using DVD cases to hold it up until I find something more solid. So far that is the worst thing about the TV.

Un-boosted sound is pretty crappy. Glad my ZVOX worked!

Being able to use the old Samsung standard power plug was a nice surprise.

Very happy with the picture. Ten years of advances in 1080p I think make the picture slightly better than my old Samsung 1080p set which cost $360 plus tax in 2013. I cannot be sure of that since it died, but I think the color, while being less rich, is more clear. I have retired since 2013 and more thrifty, these days, so I appreciate getting a good deal more, now.

So, so far, I am very happy with this purchase. I will update my review after I use the TV for a few months.

SIX MONTH UPDATE: Still working as described above. Zero problems. Still very happy with this TV.

title: A very nice Linux machine for the seniors in the audience
text:
We purchased the Ryzen 5 5560U version of the mini-pc. We removed the NVMe containing Windows Pro and installed a fresh Samsung EVO. We copied the hard disk from the old machine to the new Beelink machine. It was mostly trouble free.

We encountered trouble with Linux graphics after we powered up the Beelink machine. The machine lacked hardware acceleration. The Linux 5.4 kernel was too old and does not support the integrated graphics properly. Instead of using the amdgpu driver, the kernel used the {ati,fbdev} drivers. Once we figured out the problem we upgraded to a 5.15 kernel and hardware acceleration using the gpu was available via the amdgpu driver.

One other problem we encountered with the Beelink and Linux was, Alsa and PulseAudio blows. We could not get sound to work using external speakers. The operating system insisted in pumping sound over HDMI even though the monitor lacked speakers. The external speakers used the headphone jack. We had to switch to external USB speakers to get sound to work.

We also would have liked more USB ports. Between keyboard, mouse, printer, scanner, speakers, phone tether, garmin tether, and camera tether, we ran out of ports quickly. You might want to purchase a powered USB hub in you have more than a few devices.

Here is the additional hardware we purchased for the machine:

* SAMSUNG 970 EVO SSD 500GB NVMe, https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07MG119KG
* SABRENT 10-Port USB 3.0 Hub, https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0797NWDCB
* LISRFNIEAN USB External Soundbar Speakers, https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0B296J7D6

All in all, I'd give this machine a 4.5 out of 5. We paid the Microsoft tax for an operating system we did not want. Linux was not as smooth as it could have been due to the hardware, but the hardware has nice specs. I prefer to keep the hardware with nice specs and see Linux catch up.

title: I wear these earbuds all the time.
text:
I bit the bullet and bought the Sonly Linkbuds S after using wired earbuds with my phone for the last 5-6 years. All the talk about ANC hissing and Bluetooth codecs that drop connection had scared me away for a long time. I had bought a few cheaper earbuds and was not impressed at all. I was also a proud audio enthusiast (not quite an audiophile) and was not ready to accept wireless earbuds since I could get much better sounding headphones for the same price.

Now that I have wireless earbuds, I wear them on/off throughout the day and place them back in their case and into my pocket for a quick recharge. A single charge on Sony's case lasts me all-day and should be fine for most people as well. This brings me to the one big downside; this case cannot be charged wirelessly, which means you will have to connect it to a USB cable, and the cable you are supplied with is only a few inches long. Another downside (or upside depending on how you see it) is that you need to download Sony's app to get the most out of these earbuds. I know not everyone will want to use features like an equalizer, speak-to-chat, and custom touch controls; if you do that's all here along with other features.

Sony's noise cancelling feature they call "ambient sound control" is extremely effective at keeping sounds from your surrounding environment out of your ears and is a feature I use often. You can also setup tap controls to turn these features on and off. When someone talks to me, I can just tap my left earbud to turn ambient sound control off in order to hear them speak. There is also a talk-to-chat feature as I previously mentioned which pauses the track you're listening to and turns ambient sound control off when you speak. I like this feature a lot, but I found out while using it that I talk a lot to myself when I'm alone and it was not useful to me because of that. I can also pause/play a track with a tap on my right ear along with skip to the next track with a double-tap. You can setup your commands however you like though sound controls have to be on one earbud and feature controls on the other.

The sound of these earbuds are great overall considering the customization you have with the equalizer and its presets. I have presets set for podcasts, for EDM, Classic/Alternative Rock, and for movies. Whatever your flavor is you can dial it in to suit your listening experience. It's not hi-fi and it definitely is compressed audio, but it still sounds great overall when you consider the usefulness of these earbuds.

I give them 4 1/2 stars or a 9 our of 10.

title: I's better than built in Network adapter but not by much
text: I have HP Z400 Desktop, ISP plan: 800Mbps Down, 20Mbps Up. My wife has Macbook 2021. Router ASUS RT-AX3000 connected to cable Modem Motorola MB86000. All RJ45wires are CAT7 and CAT8. Macbook shows 900Mbps Downloading speed and 24 Mbps Up when connected by wire and up to 560Mbps over WiFi through 2 walls. With HP Z400 built in Network adapter download speed is vary: 220-400 Mbps. Tested by speedtest dot net and XFinity speed test. With this TP-Link TG-3468 card both download speed tests show stable results: speedtest dot net shows around 530Mbps and Xfinity 430 Mbps ( with tolerance of +/- 10 Mbps for both ). Upload speed is always stable : no less than 21 Mbps. So ISP Plan 800, with this card speed test on HP Z400 desktop shows stable half of speed regardless that Macbook 2021 connected to the same router with same type of CAT7 wire shows full speed. title: Great for seniors!!!
text:
So, my dads computer was getting long in the tooth and he needed a new one (he is mid 80’s). I did a lot of research in what kind of computer would be best for him. All he really does is check mail, watch an attachment video here and there, print stuff, and maybe write a letter or something. More research found even the cheapest Dell Vostro started around 600 (just the comp) and it was more than he really needed. Refurbs were much cheaper, but all the hardware was past its due.

I came across CHUWI in the search, I actually wanted to get him a Hero Box but- and I’m not being facetious- I didn’t think he would take it seriously. Let’s be honest, though I think it’s a solid comp, it looks like a toy.

Not that this doesn’t- it looks like you took a tower and zapped it with the shrink ray. It’s a little thicker than a Mac mini, but the MM is much more sturdy and solid feeling. It looks polished but is very light and feels like if you pressured it, it would snap open.

No disc drive, but you can get one for like 10 bucks (he needed one, to install stuff on discs). Only an hdmi port, no VGA.

The performance is surprising. When I got it I hooked it up to an older flat screen TV (all I had free) to update it so he could go out of box. Hearing how well it did with 4K, I found a random vid online to see how it did. It looked stunning. Even on that older TV which doesn’t even have 4K capability, it looked amazing.

As for everything else, it is fairly fast and does everything a senior would need to do- check mail, watch a vid or two, print stuff, etc. I would think even someone who does a little more could do just fine. I wouldn’t be expecting to run Read Dead 2 or anything like that on it. Maybe Fallout 3. Maybe.

So if you’re ever in the same position as I was and you want to find a decent computer that isn’t too expensive (mind you, if it were, I’d never hear the end of it!), can run Windows (which he’s used to...runs Win 10 Home), is pretty quick online and streams nicely, give it a shot before you drop a lot more on an iPad (like Consumer Reports recommended), or a laptop (he’s a desk/monitor guy), or a more pricey tower or mini tower or even bigger name brand mini PC- for seniors especially!

title: Pretty good tv, especially for the price.  Would buy again.
text: The interface gets a little laggy sometimes depending on what you are watching.  I suspect it doesn't have enough RAM.  The Roku os is pretty good, but Roku is lacking any support for twitch.  It is also very locked down (you can't install anything not approved by Roku, which is why you can't watch twitch or run Kodi on it.  They simply won't allow it.)  However, with all it's faults the Roku OS is still miles better than some garbage "roll your own" Smart tv OS of the kind that was popular a few years ago.  The Roku OS will be supported for years to come with updates and new apps.  Picture quality is very good, Sound quality is fair.  I use it without a soundbar or external speakers and while it's not going to knock your socks off, it's perfectly adequate.  The sound is crisp and clear.  The remote control (based upon the standard Roku Remote) is pretty mediocre.  It's not comfortable to hold, the volume buttons seem to have been just stuck on to the right hand side as an after thought so it's hard to press them without dropping the remote.  After a week, the text on my "OK" button has already worn off.  Also, the remote is "IR" which means it's like the old-school remotes that need to have line-of-sight to the tv sensor in order to work.  Also, the signal put out by the remote is pretty weak and you really do need to have it pointed right at the TV or it will miss button presses.  This is balanced out by the fact that because it's "IR" you can use any learning universal remote to replace it or you can get very cheap replacements for around 8 dollars on amazon if you lose or break it or you just want to have a spare.  To summarize, it's a good performing tv with very good build quality with a fantastic price.  Especially when you consider that it has a $50 Roku built in, included in the price.  The roku TV provides a bonus assortment of live streaming channels when you are in "Live TV (Antenna)" mode, which is nice.  If you do happen to need the few things you can't do with Roku, you can always plug in an android tv box or a media center pc and be no worse off.  Overall I'm very happy with the purchase and would buy again without hesitation.

title: It MELTED.
text:
So once this thing arrived, I was initially shocked to find it was plastic, but I assumed, incorrectly, that if it's made of plastic, it must be heat resistant, right? Obviously it SHOULD be, but was it? No.

It melted inside one of my USB ports, that port is now unusable, and while trying to find support, there is little to actually be found. Contacting support directly, they said they'd send me an email after the chat, which to their credit, they did, but there was a statement within that email that said, word for word: "We apologize for your experience. I understand that you are not claiming any extra damage other than your SanDisk product. We would be happy to replace your SanDisk product."

And I made it extremely clear in the chat that my PC sustained damage from this plastic piece of crap, and I'd like something done about it, so I'm not sure why they tried to slide that in, maybe to make me agree without reading? And what makes them think I want a replacement anyway, it MELTED, why would I want a second one? I received a broken link to create an account for SanDisk support as well, because after doing so, trying to log in does not work, and requesting a password reset doesn't work either as it's been 4 hours since requesting a password reset and still I have not received anything in any folder at all in my email.

So far my experience with this has been the absolute worst, and the people designated to "help" seem to lack basic product knowledge, and intelligence considering they think I simply want a replacement of the exact item that melted in my system to begin with.

A lot of you may think that a single USB port being broken isn't a big deal, but it's the principal of it that matters. You don't want new scratches on your car when you pick it up from an autobody shop, right? Large companies shouldn't be able to get away with their products damaging a customers property. It's a shame too, I always liked SanDisk, this is not my first experience with them overall, all of my flash drives are SanDisk, and they all work great, but making this one plastic, especially that isn't heat resistant, was stupid beyond belief.

I'd include the video I took, which shows me using another SanDisk flash drive in two of my front ports, the working one, and the broken one, but if I did that, people would comment saying something stupid like "Hur dur that's not even the right flash drive from this listing" without reading what I wrote here, acknowledging full well that it's a separate drive and explaining the intention is to show the port is broken. So I included the picture of just the melted flash drive instead. No clue if it's still working, I intended to try it in a dummy laptop but the stupid thing melted in such a way that it just won't fit.

Here's hoping tomorrow, when I contact their support again, that I actually get somewhere. If they do good by me, I'll simply remove this review and replace it with a better one, but for now, these are my feelings on this product.

title: Lightweight, big screen, and excellent form factor
text:
This travel monitor has a great screen size at 16 inches. The resolution is 1200p or 1920x1200.

The left side of the monitor has 3 buttons. Up, Menu, Down to control the settings of the monitor.

It has 3 ports to the right side of the monitor if it is facing you. 2 USB-C that works with any usb-c with displayport enabled. and a mini HDMI port that allows another device to send an HDMI signal for display to this device.

The package includes 1 power adapter, a USB-A to USB C cable, a USB C to USB C cable, a mini HDMI to HDMI cable, and a screen cover/case

the monitor is very thin on top but has a less than half an inch thicker bottom part.

I plugged in my galaxy fold using the included USB C to USB C cable and was able to launch samsung dex. It also has built in speakers but it isn't the best sound. It is enough to do simple tasks and good enough audio to understand what you're watching. But I wouldn't expect this to have dolby surround and the like.

One issue I did encounter is that if you increase the brightness too high while on the samsung dex mode, the monitor would restart. I think this is just a limitation of my fold to provide enough power for the brightness. I don't run into this issue when I plug in this monitor to my macbook air or chromebook devices so it is probably an issue with my phone rather than the monitor. That is to say, this monitor can go bright if needed.

It's a great value for the price and would highly recommend this. I'll update about durability in a few months.

title: Works really well on our older bedroom television!
text:
I have bought 2 similar devices before buying this one. Now I would like to say I used them, they failed in some way, or just sucked, but the reality of things is the wife lost them. They were tiny devices in a plastic bag and she either tossed them or put them in a junk drawer to never be seen again. So I bought this one, and it is still small, but not tiny.
Plugged it into the TV USB port after connecting the included RCA stereo (via 1/8) to the appropriate ports. First I paired 2 speakers, mainly to see if I could, and turned off the TV speakers. There was a delay between the two speakers, and I attribute that to the difference in BT specifications. It wasn't terrible, but it was noticeable.
I disconnected the older speaker and ran with the BT 5.0 one and compared it to the TV speakers for delay. There was a slight delay, but you wouldn't notice it if you used the BT speaker as your sole source (as we intend to do at times). That paired with the fact that our TV is mounted on the wall some 15' away and it sounds/looks great.
I did hook up the older speaker (BT3.x I believe) and the delay was a bit more noticeable. Watching football it was no big deal, bit you could just see the sync being off when watching a talk show. But with the age of the speaker and the older specification I kinda expected it. That speaker was built for music and probably never intended for a TV set.
I haven't tested the battery, and probably never will. Maybe I will test distance some time, but I doubt it. I guess if I was watching 'the game' and went to the bathroom I could take the speaker with me.
I am hoping to get an AptX enabled device to see if the slight delay goes away, but, honestly, the performance I am experiencing now probably isn't worth spending close to $100 for a speaker with this ability. As far as sound quality improvements, how much better can Bob Ross or Love Boat reruns sound?
Oh, it says I could mention volume control. Uh, I use the TV to adjust the volume, so can't really comment on that either.
Anyway, if it ever fails of starts to act up I will amend my review. In the couple of weeks I have been using it, it has been doing exactly what I wanted it to do. Would the previous devices have done as well or better? I guess we will never know.

text:
I wasn't expecting anything exceptional from this low cost purchase. I just wanted some earbuds to use in bed in a side sleeping position. So I've been absolutely delighted by what I got here!
First off, these have fantastic, rather deep bass! Far better than from any other earbuds that I currently own. So these are going to be my new everyday buds for cycling and for lounging. I think the really good bass comes from the fact that they're designed to go quite deep into the ear canal for sleeping, which then puts the bass output right where it can really have a great effect.
Second, the buds are very comfortable. The double silicon shields fit my average size ear canal very well.
Third, somehow I didn't notice in the listing that the package includes TWO sets of ear buds. I was more than happy to pay this price for just one set.
Lastly, I'll be curious to see if they might be good at keeping wind noise out while I'm cycling with these. I'm optimistic based on how well they seal and how deep in the ear canal they go. I'll aim to post an update on this subject.
Lastly, a warning: I don't think these would be good for running. When the cord moves around, it reverberates right into the ear with noise. So you can't really use them if you're moving the cord around much.

title: Really nice alternative to ear buds
text:
I bought these as a supplement to my regular ear buds. These open ear headphones are definitely better for working out. Regular ear buds have four major downsides that these open ear headphones solve nicely.

Regular ear buds are problematic for a couple of reasons:

1. They fall out. Have you ever lost an earbud while running on a treadmill?
2. Ear pressure while running. When I run with normal earbuds, I'm uncomfortable with the loud thumping in my head from my footsteps.
3. Outside sound is completely blocked. My wife hates it when she attempts to talk to me and I'm completely deaf because I'm listening to my ear buds.
4. Ear canal fatigue. Ear buds start to hurt after a while.

title: Solid state drive offers solid performance
text:
Solid State Drives (SSDs) are attractive storage alternatives because they contain no moving parts. So unlike traditional hard drives, they don't have parts that will wear down or fail due to internal movement, as a traditional hard drive has moving platters and read/write head(s).

I didn't open up my computer and install it internally. I've tried that previously with other SSDs and found there was some setting that prevented them to be recognized together with my internal hard drive. So I have an external case for testing and using drives like these.

My data transfer was limited by the USB connection on the outside of the case. It transferred at a steady 33 mb/second. Plugging it directly into the SATA cable in your computer would offer better results. The video files I transferred for testing played back smoothly.

EVALUATION: A good alternate choice for storage and as a backup for portable hard drives.

This offers a good price/gb storage value.

title: A great way to store and watch your photos
text:
Mom is 85. I've shared countless videos and photo albums with her but I know that most she has never watched. I scanned everything she owned and I owned (and some of my bother's, sister's, and grandparents' photos also) but they sit in electronic form, waiting. She'd have to take out a disc, put it in the player, turn it on and sit there. It's not going to happen.

So I wanted to try something that would make it easier. The electronic photo frame was the answer.

Getting one that would let me and the sibs upload pics was important, as was a reasonably large screen size. The Vealvion 10.1 inch was an excellent choice for lots of reasons.

- 16 GB MEMORY. If you keep the photo size closer to the maximum resolution of the frame display, I calculated that you could fit over 50,000 photos, or a combo of photos and short videos.
- REMOTE LOADING OF PHOTOS. I successfully got my sister-in-law in Florida and my sister 20 minutes away from me to upload pics to the frame with a phone app using their smart phones as I set up the frame.
- I was able to load photos efficiently off a micro SD card I plugged into the frame.
- The touch screen allowed me to optimize the display for each photo, which is handy with the mix of horizontal- and vertical-oriented pics I had.

I set up times for it to turn on and off, as well. Sound from the built-in speaker is okay, but that's not the primary attraction to the frame.

It is worth spending a few extra bucks to get one with a touch screen and remote access application. Setup was easy. Best of all, Mom loved it when it arrived in the mail.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

title: Biggest Con is How they Sound
text:
Just not a respectable listening experience.

This is the second set of bone conduction headphones I've owned. Sometimes when traveling in unfamiliar neighborhoods I like keeping my ears uncovered to stay alert while still being able to groove to my favorite R&B tunes.

The features found in these Open Ear Wireless Bone Conduction Headphones are innovative, but the sound itself leaves me cold.

Can't put my finger on it but the highs and mid-range sound okay. The bass is bad. It's like listening to an AM station on a classic transistor radio. Just a muffled thump instead of an immersive boom!

The magnetic charging/data cord is great at handling multiple duties. Plugging this cable into the uSB port of a PC or laptop gives you complete access to the 16GB of internal storage. Works nice as a backup music player for MP3 format audio files.

Even the fit is very comfortable. I don't feel like an alien from space walking around wearing them pressed against my cheekbones.

Just can't get past how bad music being played through them sounds. No matter how I position them around my ears/neck nothing seems to improve it.

So, for me these Hostena open ear Bluetooth 5.3 bone conduction headphones are a miss.

Thumbs down on this one. That's The Truth.

I started at 10:15 pm and the unit told me the battery would last until 1:34 am - So 3 1/2 hours use - can't do much during the day if it only lasts 3 1/2 hours.

I'll update if/when I can blow-out the ads and trim the apps to see the results. Very frustrating unit. Certainly not competition for Apple or Samsung.

title: Heavy, clunky hand computer.
text:
This thing is way too heavy. And it's not even the biggest pixel. Surely that's due to the big battery - which has both an upside and a downside. Of course the upside is that this phone does get great battery life. But it's just too impractical to carry around this heavyweight thing in my hand or in my pocket. It will fall out of your hands multiple times so make sure you have a great grippy case otherwise your pixel 6a WILL break.

Also the fingerprint reader is slow and very problematic. I stopped using it because it just simply didn't work any faster than putting in a code or pattern. Not only that but it flashes a bright light at your face in the middle of the night. Very annoying.

I've also been having several little issues with apps malfuntioning. The software is difficult to understand coming from Samsung even though they both use Android, I can't figure out simple things like how to close out open apps.

Photos are good. That's a plus. The renewed condition was excellent as far as wear and battery.

I know this is a "budget" phone but it's also a flagship, and for the price, you can pay $50-80 more and get a renewed Samsung S22 which is a higher quality phone, with comparable camera and lighter weight, though less battery life.

title: Excellent Router
text: I've been in IT for the better part of 20 yrs so I have used a lot of brands. I get bored seeing overly verbose reviews, TLDR. So here is what my general perception is. I have use TP Link on and off for various network items. They've always been solid. This router is no exception. My biggest complaint with setup is that they had to put plastic wrap on the antennas. Everything has to be wrapped. Anyway, this router was replacing a Netgear Orbi mesh system that was just slow to transmit. I didn't have signal issues, firmware updated, it was just slow. Not going to bore you with all my attempts to improve. This system was legitimately out of box and running in 10-15 mins. It's very straightforward and that includes me tweaking settings. I recommend you do it from a PC and not Tether App since you will have more options, as usual, from the web interface. Immediately the speed difference was noticeable and the lag was gone. Everything I loaded was faster. All web, email, etc. speed tests also indicated an increase as well. This is a single unit but with Mesh expanability of course, a feature I liked. In my 2500 SF 2 story, signal strength is strong on all 3 levels and I haven't found any dead zones. All devices immediately grabbed new signal. The one issue I had is that firmware would not auto update. I had to grab it from mfg website. Not a big deal but an extra step. One thing I did love was the addition of a reboot schedule. We all know that from time to time these things need a kick in the butt. Why it took so long to see this option, I have no idea. It's the little things right? So I'm my first 48 hours. I'm very happy. I have an older model Archer running at my Mother in Laws that has served her rock solid for several years. I'm hoping for the same!

title: Good 4K 32" monitor
text:
I use my computer to both consume content and play games so I am in an interesting position where I want a monitor that can do 4K for content consumption and a fast response and refresh rate for gaming. I tried the ViewSonic 32" 4K Mini-led and I ended up returning it as the mouse haloing was unacceptable for a monitor of that price point.
The "Odyssey Neo G7" is 1/3 of the price of the ViewSonic and provides a much better experience. Colors and HRD is good in both content consumption and in gaming. The black levels are good to provide a dark scene when needed and show dark shadows in lighter scenes. There is a very small halo around some items however this is deal-able as you only notice it in very specific settings or configurations.
This is my 1st curved monitor, I wanted a flat panel but decided to give this monitor a try, since Amazon has such a good return policy (30 days) I felt good about giving this monitor a try. The curve is acceptable for where I sit and able to enjoy what I am looking at on the screen.
The core lighting adds a nice accent to what's on your screen and remove the need to setup a LED strip on the back of the monitor to relive eye strain when in a dark room setting.
The controls on the bottom of the monitor take a bit to get use to, once you do it's easy to change modes or settings that you need to.
The only gripe I have for this monitor is the display port deep sleep function. It's common to use a display port cable to connect your PC to a monitor as consoles use the HDMI ports. When the monitor goes to sleep it turns on a deep sleep mode for the display port (you will hear the windows disconnect and reconnect sounds). When the monitor wakes up from the display port deep sleep and you look at your windows that you left open they will be all resized and in different locations on the monitor. So when you monitor wakes up when plugged into display port you will spend the 1st so many minutes moving windows to your preferred location if you setup you monitor to see many things at once like I do.
This display port deep sleep mode can't be turned off at the time of writing this review. Hopefully Samsung will release a firmware update that allows us to turn that mode off if we want. for the time being your options are to just deal with it or use HDMI when connecting to your computer.
Other than this one gripe this is a great monitor and I am glad I purchased it.

If I could give it 5 stars just for the packing alone, I would, as they did a really great hob in the way they packed it. What I really like about this monitor is the picture quality and the ability to use it on the road. When I'm shooting pictures or video with my DSLR, I use the monitor as a reference and the images just blow me away - it's that good. Crisp, clear, bright, dark, etc. - everything you want in an inexpensive monitor for photography and video.

It's very light and thin, has a VESA mount, which is rare for these types of monitors, and I can connect my phone to watch movies. As expected, audio is not the best as none of these thin monitors have good sound, so don't expect the sound to blow you away. To get the best image quality, play with the settings until you reach the levels you like - everyone has different tastes, so there isn't a "killer setting" that will please everyone.

As previously stated, it comes well packed, with USB-C and HDMI cables and a power adapter. The cover is a very nice design as well that integrates with the body of the monitor. They sure do have a nice design team for their products, that's for sure.

title: Best Value CPU Air Cooler
text: The Scythe Mugen Rev. B is a great air cooler for your CPU. I built a pc with a Ryzen 5-3600 in a case that does not have great air flow, so felt the stock air cooler would not be enough, especially with the extra heat generated from the graphics card. I was also trying to keep noise down as I had heard the stock Ryzen Wraith cooler can get loud, especially if pushed to higher speeds. So for $46 this was a great choice. It comes with its own magnetized screwdriver and installation on an AMD-4 socket motherboard was a breeze. It also comes with hardware to install on several other Intel and AMD-based motherboards. This is a quality piece of equipment, well designed and well built. The design is awesome with offset heat transfer pipes which keep the cooler and fan completely clear of your RAM slots. I have found it to be silent and it has kept my CPU temps down. And it looks great (my opinion). The stock cooler probably would have done the job but with my first build I did not want to chance having to replace it after the system was built. I would strongly recommend this CPU cooler to anyone building a PC - especially for those who are using a processor that does not come with a cooler.

title: Good enough for most use cases.
text:
I'm a professional, and I've been using these things all over the place. They're cheap. They're versatile. They're uncomplicated.

The cost point is substantially lower than most of their competition. You can afford to install four of these where you would be able to install a single [[B01I3I9L8M:Nest Cam Outdoor]]. When it comes down to it, you'd rather have more cameras and to be able to replace those cameras more easily. A camera needs to both monitor the general happenings of an area _and_ identify the cause of those happenings. I happily encourage my clients to sacrifice a cheap camera because its last upload to the cloud was a crisp image of the person messing with it.

These are flexible in their application. The option for onboard storage means you don't need the cloud, if you don't want it. The option for RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) means these things can be connected to a security recorder not even affiliated with Wyze. The default mount can be torn off with a single Phillips #2 screw, and replaced with a [[B07R13ZTFQ:dazzling]] [[B07DLXWMCV:array]] of [[B07Y9XH97M:options]]. You can improvise your own mount based on a 1/4" bolt with 20 threads per inch.

Their simplicity is a strength. The default options allow for mounting of a camera without even penetrating a wall. Looking through footage from one or even a selected subset of your cameras is relatively painless, even over days. Setting these up is easy enough to be done from the top of a ladder. With the appropriate [[B07P9SDHRY:gadget]], you can use a light socket instead of an outlet. Whether someone's trying to keep an eye on their elderly parents (watching for falls and the like), perimeter security for a house or even a commercial facility, the Wyze Cam v3 is a solid buy.

title: Headache!
text:
At first I was impressed with the picture quality of this tv, for the price ($150).
However, from the beginning, this tv kept making loud cracking noises, whether the tv was on or off, but especially while it was playing. The only way to stop the noise was to unplug the tv.
I called TCL customer support. They appeared to be genuinely eager to help addressing this problem. They even called me back to check on the problem after guiding me through various steps to stop the cracking noises.
Unfortunately, the noises would not go away, but were not as loud now.
And, as I told the rep who called me, I could live with this minor inconvenience.
Five months later the real problems started to appear. The tv would sometimes take longer to turn on; vertical grey bars started to appear on the edges of the screen. Eventually, the grey bars covered the whole screen, and the picture quality was nowhere near 1080 quality.
And three months after that (eight months after buying it, the tv stopped working all together! I had to get rid of it.
I won't get into any detail about the Roku remote that came with this tv, but it is, by far, the WORST remote I have ever seen!
An additional note. I recently got a TCL cell phone (even after reading reviews about the phone not being able to be activated by the carrier).
Big mistake!
My carrier also could not activate my phone and had me return it to them, which I did.
So, two TCL products, so far this year, and both turned out to be useless.

title: Asus Mesh Solves Problems like “All” Mesh has some quirks
text:
Look at the reviews for “All” Mesh Routers and you will see certain Patterns and Quirks. Asus is a good brand and has some of the same. It has solved my gaps of WiFi coverage and offers backwards compatibility for their previous routers. The problem with Mesh systems is if you have devices that are 2.4ghz only it’s best to assign them to a separate network ID. Same for 5ghz devices. If you go for the default option of one network ID your just asking for problems. Another thing I noticed is the web browser interface allows for more advanced setting but seems to be getting quirky to log in and when changing to different tabs. Seems they have quit updating it? The IOS App is lacking some of the advanced features but seems to get constant updates and more features added as it should.
Ive noticed the 2.4ghz Guest Network either has a major bug or my units are defective. All devices will always connect to the main router and not the closest one. I ended up running a network cable from the modem to the router I needed these devices to connect to. This solved the low signal problem but is only a work around. The regular 2.4ghz network works correctly it’s just the Guest Network that has this issue. I sent a message to Asus tech support with no response but hopefully they will address this in a software or firmware update. Asus provides Free security while most other manufacturers doNot. Unfortunately the browser interface allows for a easier setup and to fix vulnerabilities compared to the IOS app. If you follow the above rules you will be very happy with this router. I doubt you will find another TriBand or WiFi router that doesn’t have some of these quirks. With the exception of the Guest Network issue. Another thing you will find is other router makers have eliminated some of the advanced options that Asus still has. Am I happy with how my router is working, yes. I’m not happy with how long it took to work through these issues. Hopefully this will help someone have less painful experience. I still recommend this router, just hope in another year the mesh market will mature more and resolve some of the quirks.

title: Fast and Easy to Configure
text:
-=Overview=-

In summary, the TP Link AXE5400 is a sleek, easy-to-set-up router that’s fully compatible with the latest generation of wireless connections. Used as an access point, even with older hardware, it increases speeds, while future-proofing your network.

-=Use Case=-

For this review, the AXE5400 was being set up as a wireless access point with a specific use case as a bridge to an Oculus Quest 2 for the new AirPlay capability, which allows wireless streaming of VR titles directly from a network-connected PC.

-=Packaging=-

The router comes in a simple packaging, thankfully using a formed carboard rather than plastic for protection. The router arrived in perfect condition and was protected with two types of removable protective film. The sleek upper surface of the router was covered with a cling film and removed cleanly.

Each antenna was wrapped in plastic, and while the plastic was pre-perforated, it was a little fiddly to remove. Hardly the end of the world, but worth noting for those curious.

Also included were a standard power adapter, and a disappointingly short 3-foot / 1 meter light-grey network cable. While the cable seems of high enough quality, the distance it provides isn’t the most practical. It was, however, fully workable to link to a laptop for the configuration.

-=Case and Housing=-

The body of the router feels sturdy and boasts a decorative plastic “mesh” top across most of its surface. With metal faintly visible beneath the plastic’s grooves, it’s likely this is designed to help with heat, but under regular use at room temperature it never felt hot.

The antennas, 6 in all, boast a wide range of motion. Four emerge from the back and two from the sides, and they can be twisted along several axis points, making it easy to wall-mount the router and run its antennas along the wall surface, should it be needed. Two screw-ready hanging ports on the back make the mounting easier, as well.

The case boasts a physical power switch, meaning there’s no need to unplug the power adapter for a hard reset, should it be needed. It’s also possible via button on the case or using software to deactivate the activity LEDs on the router’s front. Via software only, they can be set to deactivate only for specified hours, allowing the router front lights to turn off at night, or while sleeping, for instance. Note that the individual LAN ports on the back do not appear to have any LEDs (as many do), so this router is one of the few that can boast a true night mode sans network activity blinking.

The back sports a single WAN port, as is usual, and 4 LAN ports.

-=Setup=-

An app is available to aid setup via Apple and Android phones but was not tried. Instead, regular software setup through a network cable and direct IP address was used and resulted in a surprisingly crisp web interface compared to the slow web updates expected.

The web interface itself is clean and functional and boasts a quick setup for those looking to start in default configuration. One excellent facet of this process: no default admin password is offered; users are expected to set and then confirm their own. A nice way to avoid the most obvious security flaw in many routers that start with a factory default.

As this device was being moved to an access point, it was good to note that at any point during the quick setup it was very fast to change to access point mode. Doing so resulted in a 90-second reboot of the machine and reconnection to its access point menus. After a brief initial setup, things were working in seamless access point mode for 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz connections.

Connecting through the Oculus Quest 2 saw a jump of approximately 33% in available bandwidth for streaming VR, and that jump smoothed out numerous hitches in demanding titles such as Half-Life: Alyx that were present in a previous, standard 5 GHz router in similar conditions and use cases.

-=Additional Features=-

The AXE5400 boats several quality-of-life features outside of the core networking features such as port forwarding. Easy updates with a web-check from its menus are there. Guest networks, including the ability to force-isolate guests so connections through that network cannot see other devices, are present and seem robust. The 6GHz connection boasts WPA-3 encryption, while the older bands remain with WPA-2. A single USB 3 external storage port is also available on the device as well but was not extensively tested except to confirm it was able to read a thumb drive.

title: Works Great with the Steam Deck
text:
I've reviewed a ton of these little monitors, and most of them are incredibly similar, with only minor variations. This is my favorite so far for several reasons:

- The indentations in the cover actually work to hold the monitor upright without it sliding while I used it.
- There are multiple menu buttons, making menu navigation fast and easy
- The included cables seem to be high-quality
- It works with the Steam Deck with absolutely zero fiddling
- The screen is large, without being impractical

Out of the box I connected this to my Steam Deck using one of the included USB-C cables, and I was able to immediately start playing. The colors are a little muted, but otherwise faithful, and the brightness is excellent (by default it's set very low). I had no issues with refresh or tearing on Dead Cells, which was my test title.

Menu controls are intuitive, and the build quality feels solid. As always, the cover feels a little cheap, but is still the nicest I have reviewed in this category. As I noted above, it actually holds the monitor in place, which is a pleasant change.

Sound is surprisingly clear, although - of course - lacking in base. I can't imagine anyone would buy a monitor like this for the sound, but expect it to be serviceable for most basic uses.

I can't think of a single complaint other than the necessary tradeoff in footprint to get the larger screen. Smaller laptop bags will definitely not be able to accommodate this monitor. While it's super slim, and relatively light, it's height and width are comparable to that of a 17" gaming laptop.

title: Outstanding Dock
text:
This was used to replace an aging desktop with a gaming laptop. The laptop is Thunderbolt 4, which is backwards compatible with 3, and performance has been excellent - even with a full compliment of devices connected.

Build quality is also quite good. It feels substantial, but not heavy. The brushed aluminum case looks great, and should help cool it as well. Under load, it can get quite warm. The main Thunderbolt port has enough power for an ultrabook, or to trickle charge a gaming laptop. The second Thunderbolt port has enough power for a phone or tablet.

Here is the list of available ports:

1 x Thunderbolt 3 port (60W)
1 x Thunderbolt 3 port (15W)
1 x DisplayPort
2 x USB-C 3.1
1 x USB-A 3.1
2 x USB-A 3.0
2 x USB-A 2.0
1 x SPDIF
1 x 3.5mm Headphone Jack
1 x microSD Card Reader
1 x SD Card Reader
1 x Gigabit Ethernet Port

Overall this is an excellent choice for someone who wants a full desktop experience by connecting one cable to their laptop. Make sure that you are using a Thunderbolt 3 cable, and that your laptop has Thunderbolt capability. (If it has more than one USB-C port, they may not all be Thunderbolt ports. Check the icons next to the ports.)

title: Large - But for a Good Reason
text:
This is a sturdy, well-made, unmanaged switch that is much larger than most 8-port, PoE switched - but for a good reason: the larger footprint also contains the power supply. This means that you can connect a standard IEC power cord (included) to the box, making replacement power cords (or installing a longer one) a snap. It also means that you do not have to find room on the floor or a shelf for a power brick in your wiring closet.

Build quality seems excellent. I was pleasantly surprised with the quality from a manufacturer whose name I did not recognize.

I reviewed both the 5-port and the 8-port, and their form factors were identical. For this reason, I would recommend going ahead and getting the 8 in most cases. I've never had a situation where I complained about having too many ports.

text: Why even get a liquid cooler or a more expensive heavy duty air cooler? This is a beast of a heat sink and fan for this price (currently $48 USD). I have to be honest though, ordering the 2000 RMP version of the fan (which is about $12 USD) will get you better performance for those not minding a bit more noise. More static pressure and airflow than the 1200 RPM fan it comes with, but the regular fan gets the job done well regardless. Not to mention the incredibly easy install AND the included long magnetic tip screwdriver. This is the highest quality install tool I’ve ever seen shipped with a computer product. I use the Ryzen 5 3600 overclocked To 4.0 GHz at 1.41 ish Volts. The wraith stealth it comes with would constantly stay in the 75-87C range under load. Idle, the fan struggled to get me sub 55-40C temps... Often spiking up to 65C. I knew I had to upgrade as soon as possible. Currently with the new cooler installed I easily stay sub 30-40c idle and NEVER MORE THAN 71C UNDER LOAD. Jeez. I do a boat load of gaming and streaming on this rig, cooler keeps my CPU nice and cool on long tasking sessions. Oh, and not to mention quieter. Even with the higher RPM scythe fan I eventually added. Better temps are not only healthy for my system short and long term, but yields better more consistent performance. Scythe has earned my business for the foreseeable future. Do yourself a huge favor and get this darn almost perfect CPU cooler, and thank Scythe, not me for telling you to get it.

title: Excellent single monitor mount! Note that Step 6 was tricky!
text:

I can confirm that the height from the base of my desk to the middle of the attachment is 17" at its highest setting. When I asked the question before purchasing I received two responses: 16.5" (from the company) and 17" (from a customer). Perhaps I attached mine half an inch higher than they recommend. Time will tell and I'll update if I face any issues at this height.

Note from one of my photos that the brand is on the base of the mount that will display on your desktop. I mention it only because it's not too noticeable in the stock photos.

I rated "easy to assemble" 4 out of 5 due to a couple issues I faced during assembly.

First, I struggled with Step 2 for the Clamp Base: I lined up the three bolt holes with the three holes on the pole, affixed one of the bolts, then accidentally moved Clamp Base. Whoops! It took some trial and error moving the Clamp Base some more before I lined up the bolt holes again. My error but be warned about this step!

Second, I was unable to complete Step 6 as described in the instructions. With the monitor attached, I could not for the life of me get the bolt to adjust on the side of the hinge up behind the VESA plate. It just wouldn't budge! By instead removing the monitor, I was able to get leverage with the Allen wrench used the long way and then reattach the monitor to fix it from drifting ever downwards.

It took about thirty minutes to complete installation, with those two issues included.

I am exceedingly happy with my new setup and highly recommend the single monitor mount!

This is a great tool for backing up iPhone or Android Photos and Video. It is actually very easy to use. The only drawback is why I gave it 4 Stars for the overall rating. In order to connect the device to my iPhone 12 Pro, I had to remove the phone case. I kept trying to connect it and finally realized that it wouldn't fit in the slot because the case was too thick. This is a minor issue really. Otherwise, this handy little photo stick is very easy to use. Please always READ INSTRUCTIONS with any new device...

When you connect the device, it will prompt you to download the necessary APP, called LUV SHARE. After you install the app you can continue using the flash drive/photo stick. Follow the instructions and pick 'External Storage', then pick the '+' symbol at the bottom of the screen. It will ask you to pick a library on your phone. Once you've done that, look at the bottom of the screen and click the 'O' on the bottom left. That will select ALL of the photos you have visible on the screen. Then click on DONE at the top right. POOF! All of them will upload to your photo flash drive.

That should solve the dilemma that some reviewers have posted where it seemed clunky to transfer photos and such from their phone. Have fun!

title: Updated Review - 1 Star
text:
UPDATED REVIEW- 1 STAR

I initially gave these a 5 star rating because they seemed to be much better made than the original Apple cable. Unfortunately, this proved to be wrong. About a week after my review the tip of the cable came out inside my daughter's iPad. I was holding the iPad at the time and the cable simply pulled slightly on a chair handle and it caused the tip to separate. I had to use tweezers to get the tip out of the charging port of the iPad. I chalked up that experience to the cable getting stuck in the chair arm but as of today the second cable just had the tip separate . This time it came out while simply trying to remove it from the iPad. This is inexcusable.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

Apple makes some great products but their accessories are truly garbage. I have gone through several apple charging cables... the most recent being my daughter's iPad cable which is only 8 months old! The new Apple chargers have the lighting port but require the USB C on the brick side. This cable allows you to use the newer Type C charging bricks as well as the older USB bricks. The fast charging works flawlessly and it looks like these should be able to last the life of the device rather than just a few months. Overall a 5 Star Product!

*** PROS: ***
- Works flawlessly with my iPad
- Works with older USB charging bricks as well as the newer TYPE C bricks
- Sturdy and looks more durable than the original Apple cable
- Included USB converter is attached with a metal chain so you won't lose it
- Supports fast charging

*** CONS: ***
- This wasn't included in the package with my iPad !

title: Really good and inexpensive for what it is
text:
The Somnambulist 120GB SSD won't be winning any speed or capacity awards anytime soon, but that's not what it's going for. Even at its highest recent price of $23 it was a decent value, but at its current price of $13.49 it's an absolute steal.

If you need a bit more storage on an existing PC or are upgrading an older laptop to a better hard drive, this is a really good option. I would not use it as the only hard disk on a modern machine as 120GB isn't much storage these days, and the operating system will take up a good chunk of it. Several game consoles could also take advantage of it, but as you get more current the case for upgrading to a non-budget SSD gets stronger (for example, it would probably only fit 3-4 PS5 games on it).

Overall though, the Somnambulist performs adequately and does so at an amazingly low price. As long as you don't need high capacity and high speed, this is definitely worth a look.

title: Easily Digitize Your Old Tapes
text: This a self-contained video capture device for capturing audio and video from analog sources. It features RCA ports for video and left/right audio, plus a S-Video port. There is a HDMI port for external monitoring. No computer is needed for capturing video - in fact, the built-in battery is good enough for capturing over two hours of video. The device is charged via USB-C - a cable and wall charger are included. Captures are stored on either a USB flash drive or MicroSD card. I used a Sandisk Ultra flash drive and experienced no problems with captures. It will not capture from copy-protected sources, such as some commercially recorded video tapes. I had no problems digitizing my archive of old tapes I shot with my camcorder. Video looks good - colors are as cleanly reproduced as can be expected from these older formats. The mp4 files are compact - an hour of video is a bit over 1.9 GB. By default it is configured for 4:3 aspect ratio content, which is what I needed. The built in display is super handy and the speaker works fine for monitoring audio. Menus are intuitive, simple and easy to navigate. Overall, I’m pleased with this capture device. It greatly streamlines archiving my old video tapes.

title: Good Budget Laptop with Easy Upgrades
text:
This budget laptop features Windows 11, and a nice display. It is a familiar wedge shape, and weight is moderate. The top part is made of aluminum for stiffness, the bottom part is plastic. The nice, bright 1080p display has thin borders on two side to give the laptop a clean, modern look. There are plenty of ports, including USB-A and USB-C, plus HDMI and ethernet. Sound quality is decent for watching streaming videos - good at reproducing voices. The trackpad is a nice size and the keyboard has a good enough feel for typing.

The laptop is easy to upgrade. There is one free memory slot, and space for a second 2.5 inch hard drive or SSD. Screws for mounting the drive are included. The laptop ships with 4 GB of ram, and a small 128GB SSD. Adding an additional 8GB of ram, and a second drive are inexpensive upgrades well worth doing. I commend Acer for making it simple to upgrade, as this is not always the case with laptops.

Performance is fine for day-to-day tasks. Web pages load fairly quickly, and streaming media plays smoothly. Setup is easy to do, but be prepared to wait for a while for it to complete. Overall, this is a nice, inexpensive entry level laptop that should work well for those who need a basic laptop for web surfing, word processing and watching streaming media. I’m pleased with it.

The camera build quality is pretty bad, to start with. It is very plasticky, and the front plate on the vaunted glass lens fell off on its own after a few days, despite it being on a desktop monitor that was never moved.

The software is another issue. You are supposed to be able to store settings in the camera but that simply did not work for Zoom or Teams calls. After researching it, I saw that the feature was fixed in a firmware update, itself an arcane process that involved clicking on an onscreen button in the Camera Hub software while holding down the “Control” key on your keyboard. I upgraded the firmware, and the camera seems to now hod my zoom settings, but after the firmware update the Camera Hub software would no longer boot. I uninstalled it, reinstalled I several times and rebooted my computer but I could not get it to work. I guess I need to wait for an update to that too.

On the positive side, the color accuracy of this camera is amazing. But that’s simply not enough to recommend it – there are many better options available.

title: A good amplifier for the hard of hearing
text:
The Jteman phone amplifier works well. Operation is simple and so far reliable. I am hard of hearing and so this amplifier helps significantly to improve my hearing of phone conversations. The maximum volute level is fairly good. It works for me. I have not tried this with several people on my end participating in the call, but I am confident that it will do the job adequately.

I would say that the build quality if about the same as with most electronics made in China . It seems to be sturdy and well made.

The phone stand is adjustable for the angle you wish. It is simply a holder for your phone. You can set your phone of almost any size and shape on the stand. The phone can be in either a horizontal position or vertical position. The base of the holder folds up into the unit so that the back portion can be folded down against the speaker.

The self contained rechargeable batteries are charged using a USB-C connector, so any USB charger with a "C" type connector on one end of the cable will work. The proper cable is provided with the amplifier.

If I were to fault this phone amplifier, I think there are two things I would mention. The first is that the clarity of the speaker is somewhat mellow, so that higher frequencies are lost to a degree. I find this to be the major fault for me with my hearing loss. I would like a crisper tone designed to give clear voice amplification as that is what I primarily use this amplifier for.

The second criticism I have for this amplifier which is really nit picking, but could have easily been eliminated with a minimal design change. The power/charging/bluetooth LED is hidden from view when the unit is folded up for storage or charging. You have to lift the phone holder out of the storage position in order to view this LED.

Once setup, when you press the POWER button, you will get a audio message "POWER ON", "BLUETOOTH MOUNT" and "CONNECTED". This process will take about 3 to 5 seconds. You will need to hold the POWER button down several seconds for this to happen. To power off, a simple press of the POWER button will turn the unit off with the message "POWER OFF".

I found the instructions relatively clear and I had no difficulty in getting the phone amplifier to connect via bluetooth to my Samsung Android phone.

When receiving a phone call, your phone will ring and after a second or two, the phone amplifier will connect with the call. To accept a call, you press the "Phone/Fast Forward" button. To disconnect to the call, you press the same button again. Be careful not to double click this button as that will hang up the call.

I have not tried other phone amplifiers, so for the moment,the Jteman seems to be a good choice.

title: Looks and functions great, but those hex-shaped mounting holes are ridiculous
text:
Pros: Great camera quality for the price. It's a nicely made piece, high quality. I like that the camera pitch angle is adjustable.

Cons: Who on earth thought the hex-shaped holes on the face of this thing was a good idea. Lemme paint this picture for you. The hex-shaped heads of your installation bolts fit cleanly into the hex-shaped holes on the face. It looks really spiffy. Nice and clean. But for cryin' out loud, you can't turn the bolts to tighten them! The only way to install this is if you have access to the space behind the license plate so you can put on nuts from behind. I don't know if you've noticed lately, but car manufacturers these days don't exactly leave those kinds of details exposed. No, not at all. They go for the more refined look of not having big cavities in your bumper or trunk lid for you to stick your hand in.

Solution? Either use round-head screws/bolts - which completely defeats the purpose of having the hex-shaped sockets on the frame - or peel the skin off of your hands trying to get them into a place that was designed to never have hands inside of it.

I definitely have pros and cons with these headphones. I have been hating all the in ear Bluetooth headphones, so decided to try these. I do actually wear these with sun glasses and it hasn't been a problem for me. Maybe a little strange at first but I got used to it quickly.

I think the sound is on par with all my other $30 Bluetooth headphones. I also get plenty of volume for just listening to music while walking. I am not terribly sure I would run in these.

title: Keeps you aware of your surroundings, but the bass is very faint
text:
I'm normally a big fan of open-ear headphones, as they allow for maintaining situational awareness while enjoying music. My other pair of open-ears is expensive and has short battery life, so I picked up these Nearphones in the hopes of finding a longer lasting and more affordable alternative. Sadly, they’re a mixed bag. The price is right and the battery life is great, but the sound quality is disappointing.

Audio from the Nearphones is unbalanced, strongly emphasizing the treble and midrange frequencies but offering very little bass. The sound isn't quite what I'd call it tinny, but the bass is subdued enough to be problematic for most types of music. Turning up the volume doesn't help, as the treble becomes quite harsh when played loud. Unless your phone offers a strong bass boost/equalizer to compensate, these headphones are better suited for listening to spoken word (a podcast, lecture, or audio book) than for music enjoyment.

Sound quality aside, the Nearphones are otherwise reasonably decent. Touch controls work fine, and battery life is impressive. The earpieces fit me comfortably enough, but they have a flexible linkage in the middle that seems to work against stability. If I shake my head, the Nearphones start coming loose, in contrast to the secure fit and rigid construction of my other open-ear headphones.

The Nearphones come with their own rechargeable case, great for extended use while traveling, but fiddly to open due to an overly smooth/rounded design. A USB A-to-C cable is included for charging, but its 11" of length doesn’t offer much reach.

Overall, it’s difficult to recommend the Nearphones for music listening, as their bass reproduction is severely lacking. They could be worth consideration for audio books and podcasts, but look to other open-ear headphones for a more well-rounded experience.
