title: It DOES light up..... with a little effort on YOUR part
text:
Dont expect to take it out of the box and light up. You MUST EXPOSE IT TO LIGHT for 10 + minutes before this will illuminate. I tried it with natural sunlight, an LED bulb and an incandescent bulb. All 3 work.
How LONG it will stay illuminated is determined by how long you expose it to light. You wont get more than a couple of hours of solid brightness if you're in a blacked out room.
If you've got your remote INSIDE the cover, what ever is exposed to the light is what's going to be lit up. If the back isn't getting light, it's not going to illuminate. Same with the front. So, I take mine out of the cover, put the cover on top of a lamp shade and set for about 20 minutes. If you keep your remote in a den or living room, set it under a lamp and it will gather light while sitting there and which ever side you expose to the lamp, that side will illuminate . Flip it over from time to time, or remove the remote and let it soak up the light through and through

title: I’m DELIGHTED So Far, So Good…..
text:
Was blown away when I got it up and running. The picture clarity is stunning, colors true, no lagging, no voice syncing problems. I couldn’t be more pleased. It’s perfect!
I was sweating with the thought of setting it up. I’m here to tell you, this 1080p TCL/ROKU made the process so EASY. It literally walks you through every step. It found my Wifi and I plugged in the data and BINGO… I’m set. HINT, A COUPLE DAYS BEFORE HOOKING THIS UP, I PRE REGISTERED with a Roku account. The TV and found me and I just verified my password and I was all set. When it asks for a credit card, ITS ONLY IF YOU WANT TO PAY TO SUBSCRIBE TO ROKU TV, which I DIDNT, so I scrolled down to the bottom and clicked where it says “ SKIP THIS”, and it did.
I bought a Blu-Ray player and plugged into an HDMI port with an HDMI cord. The TV found that Too. Next I bought the TCL TSR1 WIRELESS SOUND BAR. It should be noted the SOUND BAR ONLY WORKS WITH A BRANDED ROKU TV. The bar won’t work with TV’s ROKU STICKS to add on Roku devices. If your TV HAS THE ROKU BADGE IN THE LOWER RIGHT HAND CORNER , THE SOUND BAR WILL,WORK
This sound bar DOESNT hook up to the TV WITH ANY WIRES!! YOU PLUG IT INTO ANY OUTLET IN YOUR ROOM. The TV FOUND THAT TOO. It’s puts out awesome sound. Note, it’s too tall to SET in front of the 32” TV as it will block the RF eye that your remote signals need to get through to the TV’s. You could put something under the TV’s legs to raise it up higher. The sound bar is 31.5 inches long. Good news, the sound bar does comes with a wall mount.

I JUST subscribe to SPECTRUM CABLE and ROKU has the app to upload. No Spectrum Cable box needed. I can watch any live Spectrum program via the ROKU’s Spectrum App. I also found this TCL/ROKU TV ALSO HAS AIR PLAY! I was able to set up my IPhone 6S Plus and IPad Pro to link my Spectrum account credentials to the TV, AND USE MY iPHONE/IPAD to access SPECTRUM’s TV GUIDE, scroll through the shows, select the show and it instantly shows up on the TV. NO MORE SINGLE CLICKING THE TCL/ROKU REMOTE ARROWS TO GET FROM SAY CHANNEL 4 TO CHANNEL 592! It also allows you to use your i Phone or iPad to control the TV’s volume.
To TURN OFF THE TV’s STANDBY RF WHITE LIGHT, GO TO HOME>SETTINGS>SYSTEM>POWER>STANBY LED> AND CHANGE IT TO “OFF”.
I purchased the 1-Clicktech ROKU remote and never needed to set it up. It immediately worked with the TV. I like the added functions of this remote over the TV’s included OEM RC 280 model

title: Satisfied on Day One (+ update two weeks later)
text:
Just got done setting this machine up to my preferences for a Windows laptop and have used it for a few hours. Very satisfied so far. One thing that immediately impressed me is the nearly incredible light weight of this laptop for this price. Turns out it is an absolute joy to use a machine that weights no more than a medium-thickness paper file folder. Pick it up, Set it down. Grab it for a minute or plop it on your lap for an hour or two. The light weight really grew on me quickly. Makes my old laptop feel like it is made of cast iron. I've been using this Acer for six hours so far today and still have 40% of a battery charge left. Pretty good performance. Nice keyboard. Easy to type on and the backlighting feature is great. Nice touchpad -- not jumpy like some touch devices. Display good, not superb, but more than adequate for general computing. Definitely glad I did my homework and chose this laptop. I call it a real value -- and again, Boy do it like the super light weight.

Two weeks later: I remain fully satisfied. I did need to reinstall the audio drive software, but that's been about it. I have been using PCs since (are you ready?) the 1970s, before that outfit called Microsoft even existed, so I like to think I know a couple of things about PCs and I'm not the easiest user to satisfy. If you want a really lightweight laptop, with quite decent performance, I'd tell you that this one is worth your consideration.

title: Breathe some fresh life and crazy speed into some older hardware.
text:
I put this into an 12 year old Dell full tower which I have been using for a file server for years. There was a network port on the motherboard which was working just fine, but it was only a 10/100 port, so the speed wasn't what it could be with a faster card.

Speed became important when it came time to backup my data. Backing up over 30Tbs was a several day process and, as such, I wasn't backing up my data as often as I should.

Anyway, installation into the single PCIe slot was a breeze, and using the old network port I downloaded the latest driver from TP-Link's website. Installation was painless and, when done, I moved the cable to the new port and I was good to go.

It is making a huge difference in data transfer speeds and backups are going much faster.

title: Great Performance and Copious External Storage with a Relatively Small Footprint
text:
I have three immutable maxims when it comes to backing up important computer files: redundancy, redundancy, and redundancy. I've been working with computers since the earliest days of personal and home computing, and if I've learned anything over the years, it's that you can't have too many copies of your important stuff. It should come as no surprise, then, when I say that I'm perpetually on the lookout for new storage media on which I can stash backups of my precious computer files. Still, I was a bit dubious about getting this 128-gig USB-A 3.1 Gen2 flash drive from LinkMore, mainly because the brand was unfamiliar to me. The very reasonable price is too good to resist, however, so I decided to take the leap and give the drive a whirl. And am I ever glad I did.

Measuring roughly 2.25" by 0.75" and about one quarter of an inch thick, this flash drive is admittedly not the physically smallest one I've ever used. But it's nonetheless a lot smaller than any of my external solid-state hard drives, and yet it's nearly just as fast. With the LinkMore drive connected to my computer's USB-A 3.1 port, it took me barely two minutes to transfer over thirty gigabytes of MP3 files from the computer's internal mechanical hard drive to the flash drive. That's about a fourth of the time it took to transfer those same files to my mechanical 500-gig Western Digital My Book via the USB 3.1 port, and it's only about thirty seconds longer than it took to transfer those same files to my Lexar SL100 500-gig solid-state external hard drive via my computer's Thunderbolt port. Now you gotta admit, that's pretty darned fast for a USB-A thumb drive!

At the time of this writing, I've only had this LinkMore flash drive for a few hours, so I have no firsthand knowledge regarding the potential longevity of the device. And since I've had no experience with other LinkMore products, I can't even make an educated guess as to how long this unit will function before it starts to fail. But seeing as how I will only be using it for backups, the device will not be subject to daily nonstop workouts. Besides, new and improved data-storage technologies are being developed at a rapid pace these days, so I imagine some other type of storage technology will come along and supersede this unit long before it bites the dust.

So, the bottom line? If you're like me and you can't have too many external storage devices on which to back up your important data, and if you're also looking for an inexpensive USB 3.1 external drive that offers speed, large storage capacity, and a relatively small footprint, then you can't go wrong in choosing this LinkMore 128-gig flash drive. I think you'll be pleased with the overall quality and performance of the device, and I definitely think you'll feel like you've gotten your money's worth.

title: Ok tv but not what works for me.
text:
[Edited to add]
I dropped this down to 1 star. After having the tv for a month or less we've had audio problems & the left hand bottom corner of the tv is dark now. Roku is off my list of products to choose from.

[Original review]
This was my 1st Roku product.

Pros: Easy setup, simple remote, easy to add/remove channels. I like the number of choices for channels to add (multiple freebies to choose). The size was perfect for the piece of furniture it was placed on. The type of stand is more stable than the stand on our previous tv. Screen resolution is very nice. Going from a 24in tv to a 32in tv was very nice for my aging eyes. The picture quality stays the same no matter what angle I view it from. I like that the settings can be reached via a single button on the remote. It's nice to not be searching on a black remote with black buttons for the right button at night without having to turn on the lights. I have no need for the 4 buttons at the bottom for subscription services however.

Cons: Videos don't show the proper ratio aspect a lot of the time & there was no setting that would correct that. The casting didn't work or work properly (out of sync, etc) for multiple devices even though the manual said they should have worked. As a lefty the volume/mute buttons on the side of the remote are very inconvenient & too easily pushed unintentionally. I wish 1 button would be added to the remote-sleep timer. I don't care for having to go to the home screen on the tv to set that. I don't care for the Roku media player at all. I wish there were a way to adjust subtitles/cc to my preferred viewing style (this is true of the tv itself, the Roku media player & now our bluray player). After adding our cable to the tv finding our cable to watch was a bit confusing (after going to 'Live TV' I had to figure out what channel of all channels listed was the right one for cable) & the tv does not show our cable in the proper ratio no matter what setting is chosen for that.

Overall for the cost of the tv it is a good bargain. I can understand the good reviews it's gotten. However for me, a couple of the cons makes it less than the most pleasurable viewing experience. It will do until I can find a tv more suited to my viewing preferences but I doubt I'll be getting any other Roku products.

title: Doesn't work for Surface 9 with dual monitors
text:
I'll start off with I'm not a computer geek, so perhaps I was expecting too much from this dock. I've been running dual monitors for many years on my old desktop computer but it recently gave up the ghost. I decided to go with a new Surface Pro 9 laptop. It only has 2 USB-C Thunderbolt ports, but I thought that would be enough with a docking station.

So I connected the first monitor to one of the ports and it works just fine. I then connected the dock to the second port and then ran a HDMI cable to the second monitor. Nothing happened! The description of this dock says that it's compatible with a Surface Pro 9, but apparently not. Either that or they sent me a defective product. Either way, I'm going to have to send it back for a refund.

I ordered a Microsoft Surface 2 dock. I hope I have more luck with that one.

ADDENDUM: I purchased a Microsoft Surface 2 dock and it works beautifully! Not only does it work as advertised with the Surface Pro 9, it attaches to the charging port so it frees up both of the USB-C Thunderbolt 4 ports for peripherals as shown in the second photo, I connected the two external monitors to the dock via the USB-C ports on the dock which then connects to the computer power port. I also connected three external drives to the computer through a USB-C to USB-A hub. This still leaves me with one of the USB-C ports on the computer free!

BOTTOM LINE: If you purchased a Microsoft Surface Pro 9, do yourself a favor and don't mess around with second party docks that claim they are Surface Pro 9 compatible (they are not). Buy an authentic Microsoft Surface 2 dock and save yourself the time and hassle of having to return the other docks. Thank you AMAZON for your hassle free return policy!

I made it dual boot, and installed openSUSE Leap 15.3 next to Windows. The dual boot works fine. However, I haven't been successful yet getting the Ryzen to work at full resolution. That's not HP's fault, but rather AMD which doesn't provide its Radeon drivers as public domain.

text:
This is an entry level device. And, as an entry level device it's a pretty solid entry. I've been tinkering with it for a while now and it compares pretty favorably to the performance of my children's Fire tablet. Sound is decent, picture is pretty decent, and it runs all the basic apps I've put on it very well. I've streamed video to it, checked email, all the tasks you expect to work on an entry level device and they all work.

This does run Android 11, but it is Android 11 Go. That "Go" is important. That is not the build of Android that you get if you get a flagship Google or Samsung device, it is a version of Android that is stripped down to run more effectively on devices with limited memory and processing power. But, that's ok because it means this device is not going bogged down by the operating system. It does mean that you might not find all of the apps in the Play Store that you might find on a higher end device. But, again, that's ok. The apps you can install will work, and they will work well on this tablet.

Setup was pretty straight forward. I was able to get set up without any headaches and I did notice there was a separate path for setting up as a children's device. I might wipe it and try it out as a children's device sometime but for now this is my Android tinkering device so I can test out building Android apps.

title: Better than I was expecting
text:
I've been using this for a solid week before posting this review. I wasn't expecting too much and early issues not related to the headset had me leaning negative, but honestly, I can't find anything seriously amiss with these.

Let's get detailed because there is a lot here in this little package:
+ The headphones are very light, but well built. I don't feel like I might break them from normal use.
+ The headband is padded on top and nicely adjustable, very comfortable to wear on my bald head.
+ The Bluetooth setup is really easy, more importantly, it's easy to switch from one device to another. Just push the power button up for a few seconds, it says "pairing," then click on the device on the computer or phone. I find I'm constantly switching back and forth between my Mac and my iPhone because it is so easy and reliable.
+ The headphones announce the power when you turn them on. I was on 100% for about 3 days of casual use. Only today did it finally say 90%. The battery lasts a long time.
+ There is a really cool feature, swing the microphone up over 90 degrees and it automatically mutes, and gives a voice confirmation. I have to say, I really like that and use it all the time.
+ The sound is clear for both me and the people I spoke with on the other end of my calls.
+ It comes with a small Bluetooth dongle. At first I used it to connect to my Mac before I realized it wasn't doing anything, my laptop already has BT. I'm not sure what I would need the dongle for, but I'll keep it.
+ The package included a nice draw string pouch with a small velcro pocket up at the top for the aforementioned BT dongle.

I have two negatives:
- The earpiece is a soft plastic that sits flush on your ear. I find my ear tends to get sweaty, there is no gap. This means I have to remove the headphones when I'm not using them. In comparison, my Bose headphones have very large ear cups that surround my ear. I wear them for hours on long flights with no ear sweating.
- The max volume on these is a little lower than I would like. I do not have hearing issues, but I find I am often using this at full volume if there is any background noise.

These are marketed as noise canceling. I don't dispute that they are, but when only one of your ears is covered, the other ear is hearing all the background noise. Maybe the mic isn't picking it up, I really can't tell.

So could you wear them for hours and talk while driving or working - absolutely. I love the freedom it gave me to pace around the house while on a call. I really like these and will most likely use them every day. Priced in the $35 range, I think these are a good investment.

title: Throw away the enclosed instructions
text:
I wanted some earbuds that I could use with my Windows laptop and my Android phone. I was pleased to find a set on Amazon. After using these for several weeks, this is my takeaway.

Pros:
1. The sound is good and in stereo, which is important when listening to music or movies on my PC
2. They are comfortable in the ears
3. They are handy to use
4. They don't fall out easily
5. You can use voice control for Siri and Google

Cons:
1. Throw away the instructions. You can learn more about the true operation of the earbuds from the Amazon description
2. They are very hard to control. If you use them for music like Spotify, you can fast forward as many songs as you like, but will only back up one song
3. There are little tiny holes on each earbud to help control the volume and to pause the use. They tend to be either too sensitive or not sensitive enough. They are very hard to use.
4. The instructions say that you can answer the phone, but that does not work for Android phones
5. Once you use them for voice assistance, you have to manually turn the earbuds back on
6. The charge time is supposed to be for 7 hours, and be fully charged at approximately 1 and a half hours. You are supposed to get 30 hours total time of use, but I found it to be less than that
7. The instructions do not tell you how to use the charger at all. I learned through trial and error

While I really wanted to love these earbuds, I found them lacking in instructions and difficult to use. That being said, I still use them, warts and all. They are not as easy to use as it seems, but in the long run I like them better than plugging in headphones on my devices. I would not recommend these if you want all of the bells and whistles, but for just listening to music and movies they work just fine.

title: Good POE Switch for IP Cameras
text:
I needed another switch to add more IP cameras to my network. Previously I went with an Aumox switch which is great but they only have up to 5 ports (at this time) and I needed more. This Mokerlink had what I wanted: 8-port 802.3af/at, IEC C13 power cable (i.e. no wall wort or custom transformer!), it is fanless, it can take the same temperatures (-10 C to 55 C) I wanted from the Aumox, and it appears well made (metal case which includes rack mount hardware). While a managed switch would be preferred, this particular use-case was fine with an unmanged switch since I had a managed switch to drive this with.

What surprised me was that, despite having 2x 1000mbps uplinks, the ports max out at just 100mbps! i.e. 2gbps uplink to cover just 800mbps of saturated switching. However, if you're installing this in a hard-to-access location, it means you have two uplinks which would have to fail before you loose connection to anything attached to this switch.

For IP Cameras, this is a great switch. You can easily have, say, a 10 megapixel camera (~20mbps for MJPEG or ~4mbps for H.264), powered by POE, on each port and it should work great! However, don't plan on using this to run your POE Access Point or anything that requires more bandwidth!

What's interesting, and I did not test since I didn't need it, is that you can set it to an extended mode which will give you extra range for your CAT cables. However, doing so also limits you to just 10mbps of bandwidth.

Overall, I've been happy with it. It's a well-built, unmanaged switch with POE at a great price. If you use it for what it was designed for, it will work very well for you!

title: NOT TERRIBLE, One of the Better EMR Pens with Erasers (of the extremely few)
text:
I have 50 EMR Styluses over a 10 year period, and being a hoarder rarely throw them out. So... KIND OF AN EXPERT ON this tech and the stylus. I bought this for my S22 Ultra and my Tab S 8 Plus.

Pros:
-Same price as official Samsung Tab S8 stylus, or similar enough. BUT with the added benefit of an eraser.
-Good weight to it and length.
-Has an eraser, and the eraser has the best spring I've felt on these, it's nice and smooth, and depresses easily. Even on the official Samsung versions, their erasers felt terrible and were also squared off. This is nice and round; meaning you can use it at a more natural angle.

Cons:
-The side button is hard to find blindly. It's too flush with the shaft.
-Wished the eraser was a more rubber/TPU like material, a little softer.
-Sensitivity, this seems to be a thing with samsung, like samsung is VERY PARTICULAR with the frequency of these pens. Since this one isn't sensitive enough and I do need slightly more force than an official Samsung pen. NOW, I could pop open that side button and play with the pot under it and increase the sensitivity (or decrease it, either way, turn the potentiometer to make it register better). THOUGH, I think I figured this pen's issue, the stem on the nibs is ever so slightly too far, so the distance from the two coils is slightly too much, requiring slightly more force for it to start to register. Now this isn't a TERRIBLE example of this problem. I have a ton of styluses that worked well with the Tab S3 and Note 7FE that now magically don't work on the S22 Ultra or the Tab S8, as well as they used to.

Conclusion:
I bought this one and the King Write, but I returned the king write even though it was $10 cheaper, it wasn't sensitive enough to register as easily with the new Samsung devices as this pen does. I would recommend it, a little pricey for what's on offer, but finding an EMR pen with an eraser is rare, unless you want to pay the scalper price of ReMarkable, those prices are straight up criminal for an EMR pen. $80 for a 12 pack of plastic nibs, really? So, yes, I do recommend this one.

title: Works Great with 4K TV
text:
I wanted to replace the HDMI cable on my Sony 4K TV I bought a few years back. Not totally necessary, but since cables are supporting more bandwidth and/or resolution, and they are cheap...why not.

Hooked it up from my cable box to the TV and it worked great. No problems. In fact, I think there may be a slight improvement over the picture quality from the cable box.

The cable appears to be made very well. No problems I can see in the quality of the materials used.

It was able to flex/bend the way I wanted to without issue.

While I don't have any 8K devices to test the max resolution on, it certainly seems to work well on 4K televisions.

Of course, there's lots and lots of HDMI cables out there. If you are looking for an inexpensive yet effective way to get the maximum an HDMI cable can give you, this should suffice.

One last thing - another reviewer showed a fancy box that their cable arrived in. Mine was in a different, plain white box. Not sure if that has anything to do with anything, but you may not get the fancy box if that is what you are expecting.

To conclude - a very good cable at a very good price. If I need more HDMI cables, I'd buy more of them without hesitation.

title: It works fine
text:
My usual go-to brand for USB cables is Anker. These cables strike me as being of somewhat cheaper construction, but even so they inspire far more confidence than the frail-looking cable that Apple bundled with my iPhone. But there is another brand for about the same price, SMALLElectric, that I think is the better value if you don't want to pay for Anker. The SMALLElectric brand cables have a little bit of flexibility in the strain relief, whereas the portions of the Amaitree cable that look like they're meant for strain relief are so stiff that I don't feel like they actually relieve any strain. The nylon wrapping on the Amaitree cable does feel significantly smoother to the touch than the SMALLElectric one, if that matters to you.

The connector easily fits into the charging port of my iPhone 11 without removing its Otterbox Commuter case. With 63% battery, I plugged into a fairly ordinary 10.5W charger. Twenty minutes later, it was showing 77%. I think there are somewhat better options out there, but this works and it certainly feels like an improvement over the Apple-bundled cable.

title: Before you buy, check out Chuwi tech support forum
text:
I would like to change my review to be fair with the seller. After installed Nord VPN, my LarkBox has been working well for about 1 month so far. I had felt some kind of hot air coming out the tiny box each time the PC crashed, it's suspicious to me, so I installed Norton 360 and it didn't solve the problem. Then I activated my Nord VPN; now all things seem to be good.

I purchased a Chuwi Larkbox, it was good and I gave it a good review. 6 months later, after several automatic Window's OS updates, Chuwi Larkbox will automatically shut down in less than 1 hour internet surfing. I don't play no game, no intensive calculating. This box basically becomes useless. I sent email to tech support and no answer, I went to manufacturer tech support forum and saw other users had same problem, and no response. I gave a bad review to Chuwi Larkbox, and guess what, a couple days later, the Larkbox disappeared from Amazon.

For these less know brand, before you buy, you should go to the manufacturer's web site, check out the tech support forum, find out how they treat their customers, do they have firmware updates? do they respond to customer problems promptly? Because Window has updates frequently, the PC's firmware also needs updates. If the manufacturer can not provide firmware updates, the PC will become useless once Window has a major update.

text:

The port is on the side with the logo and controls .. which is really the main unit including the charge port .. the unit is inside of a pocket near the top seam above the logo .. which itself is inside a larger pocket .. deceiving as you look in the 'outer pocket' you see wires and the actual earphone and think the port is there .. the unit with the battery is inside the smaller 'inner' slit pocket .. strangely the user manual, while having instructions for disassembly and washing, makes no mention of charging or the port.

Even after finding the port it is really a PITA to insert the charging cable. An easy fix for me was to use a very short USB cable .. 6 inches and inexpensive .. leave it in and just tuck the cable into the pocket .. does not interfere with anything .. cannot 'feel' the cable when the muffs are on ... works so far.

The net did come with nice cable ties. The were not necessary for my application as the net alone stashed away all the cables. However, it was a nice addition that you can use to tie up any excess cable or secure cables to the net.
The net installed quickly. The wood screws bit and drilled easily without too much wobble in the anchors. Once in, you can route wire through or easily unhook the net to add wires and reattach quickly. You could also use it to store lightweight devices such as a small KVM, hub, splitter, etc.
This was a great net that did the job well.

title: Magnets are on the wrong part of the product
text:
I wanted to get one of these magnetic wire management kits for a bit. I chose Anker because I've had great luck with their products, and it looked a lot nicer. Unfortunately, they made a design choice that ruins the product for me.

Every other product I've used like this had it so you were attaching magnets to the wire, and they'd connect to something with a ferrous metal plate in it. This makes it so the wires can attach to any ferrous metal: filing cabinet, monitor arms, table lamp, etc. Anker decided to put the magnet in the 'base' and the wire part just has some metal in it. So the wires will only stick to the Anker base...

The listing for this product specifically says "the 5 included magnetic clips secure any 3.5 mm cable". But there aren't actually any magnetic clips. Getting returned.

It is really too bad, because their product is the only one that looks like it was designed by someone who cared about how it looks.

title: A nice portable video gaming and PC monitor
text:
There's a slew of 15.6" monitors like this available from various sources and essentially they're all the same if they fit into a category based on resolution. The 1080p FHD's like this are great, then there's 4K newer versions but that's got a price tag on them at the moment.

These all have mini HDMI ports along with 2 USB-C ports on the one side, the power source comes from a USB-C cable and you get a converter from mini-HDMI to full HDMI cable in the box. The opposite side has controls for the OSD to change all your settings, volume, brightness, etc. It auto-recognizes just about anything plugged into it and comes with a nice hardboard folding case like you can buy for tablets and iPads which allows you to protect the screen, flip it open and use it as a stand for the monitor.

On the back is a 75 x 75 standard VESA mounting area so this could easily be put up on a wall, in multi-monitor rigs or even like I did - a clamp-on swing arm monitor mount. Volume levels are excellent as is the brightness and response times didn't show any large noticeable lag.

title: Does make a difference
text: I did a lot of research on laptop cooling stands and finally settled on the KLIM Ultimate. My ultimate reason for this decision was having a single, large fan and the ability to adjust the angle. I suspected that some of the competing stands with multiple fans had to be louder. Since I use my MacBook Pro as part of my Zoom conferencing set up, with highly sensitive condenser microphones, it was very important that the cooler stand was quiet. As any recording musician can tell you, microphones hear EVERY sound in the house! The KLIM Ultimate is very quiet: barely noticeable during Zoom meetings. The fan does keep the surface of the laptop chilly. However, I also cleaned out the dust inside my Mac and replaced the thermal paste, so it's difficult to know how much the improved performance (complete lack of thermal throttling, MUCH faster processing times for CPU intensive things like iMovie video exports, etc.) is due to the KLIM Ultimate and how much is due to fixing my Mac. title: Quite good for their size & price – much louder than you would expect!
text:
These speakers are really quite good for their size and price. And the Bluetooth saved the day!

I verified these work with my phone, over both Bluetooth and the 3.5mm audio jack. Interestingly enough, the volume when using Bluetooth seemed to have a much higher maximum, and I was able to blast them quite loud. Much, much louder than I would have expected from their very small size. I mean, they fit in your hand and are about the size of a standard Rubik’s Cube (if anyone knows what those are anymore). Yes, they have most of the standard problems of very small speakers – namely very little bass and the EQ tilts much more to the treble side of the spectrum. However, volume is NOT a problem, they get pretty loud.

I initially planned to use these in a wired configuration, by tapping the audio signal off of the HDMI output of a little stick PC I travel with (and sending the rest of the video signal to a VGA converter, for a very old monitor). However, the HDMI audio tap I have introduces some audio noise that I don’t like. Well, that little stick PC also has Bluetooth, so after switching to Bluetooth and connecting to these speakers, the noise problems were solved! It was super easy to connect both the phone and stick PC to these via Bluetooth.

There are a few things I don’t like about this system. First, the LED lights just flash between colors of the rainbow (including orange and purple), or are solid Red, Green, or Blue ONLY, or off. I want the lights to be solid orange, or purple, but that’s not one of the settings for solid colors. They also switch abruptly between colors, rather than “breathing”, which I also don’t like. I much prefer breathing, so I just keep these on a solid blue. The other thing I don’t like is the control button. It’s located almost too close to the speakers, and it’s one of those multi-function buttons that looks like a scroll wheel, but isn’t. You can momentary press it left, right, or center. And it does different things for long hold or short hold. You will have to read the manual, but one example is a long center-hold switches between Bluetooth and wired mode. It beeps while switching modes, and has a voice that announces “connected” and such when pairing to Bluetooth. Short press left/right changes the volume – but its actually sending a signal to the device and changing the volume in software, so you can see your PC or phone volume setting changing. A long press left/right is supposed to skip to the next/previous song. . . but this ONLY worked in Bluetooth mode, not in wired mode. A bit odd. . . but not a problem for me.

Final Rating: 5 stars. I would normally take off a star for the several minor problems I described, but for just under $12, you’re really getting a lot of value here, so I’m going to give that star back!

title: Worked perfectly to connect Android Phone to Windows 10 PC.
text:
This Bluetooth dongle worked exactly as advertised. I got this to add Bluetooth capability to my computer, so I could transfer files from my phone, etc. The directions literally don’t tell you anything useful. However, I did google how to set up a Bluetooth dongle on PC, and the process is pretty much identical for all of them. It worked for me the first time, and I’ll describe it below, so you don’t have to go look for it. It only took about 5 minutes to figure out.

1) Insert the dongle into the PC, wait for auto installation of the drivers (Windows says “setting up device” or something like that). This happened automatically in Windows 10.

2) Click on the (now present) Bluetooth icon in the Windows 10 system tray (mine was hidden and I had to click the up arrow in the tray to see extra stuff) and select “add Bluetooth device”. This takes you to the Windows control panel, and shows available Bluetooth devices. Make sure Bluetooth is turned on, and the PC will be discoverable as “Your PC’s Name” (whatever you named the PC when you installed Windows). This isn’t mentioned in the instruction at all (I wasted some time scanning the instructions for the Bluetooth name, but there was literally zero mention of it), but was easy to notice when the PC name showed upon my phone. From here on, it’s fairly standard Bluetooth pairing procedures.

3) Make sure your device’s (phone) Bluetooth is on, and scan for Bluetooth devices, and select the computer’s Bluetooth name. Click “add device” or “pair” on each device, and there will be a pairing code to match, to verify you are pairing each to the right device.

4) Once paired to the PC, you need to go back to the system tray on the PC and click on the Bluetooth icon again, and select “receive a file” or “send a file” or whatever you want to do, and it goes into a mode in which it’s waiting to receive something. From your phone, or paired device, click the “share” button, and share via Bluetooth. Your PC name should be one of the options to share with.

5) Back on the PC, it will ask you to set up a folder location for the shared files to go into. Then, it’s done. File transferred.

To verify this, I took the photo of the dongle for this review on my phone, and transferred them to my PC via Bluetooth, to post them for this review. I’d say it works fine, kind of slow (plenty of time for me to capture a screen shot of the transfer). The only thing I don’t like is that every time you transfer a file from Phone to PC, you MUST tell the PC first to “receive a file”, then send with the phone. You can’t just send them, and have the PC automatically receive them, but this is most likely a Windows security feature, not any problem with the Ugreen dongle.

Note, there are a few confusing directions on the seller’s page. The printed instructions and the seller’s description say this is ONLY for Windows 8.1/10/11. However, also on the seller’s page, under “operating systems” it says “Linux, Windows XP”, but then later is says it’s NOT for Linux, Mac, or Windows XP, or even Windows 8.0. Which is right? I suspect the numerous warnings about it not being for anything else but Windows 8.1/10/11 dominate here. I didn’t even try it on Linux, and probably won’t bother because of these warnings.

Also, I didn’t try to set up game controllers, keyboards, speakers, or other things like that. I got this primarily for file transferring, and it’s working perfectly for that.

Final Rating: 5 stars. Pretty easy set up, once you know how.

title: Better (but different) than canned air dusters.
text:
I've used cans of compressed air to dust out my computer innards for several years, and I like this hand held blower better. However, it is different than a can of compressed air, so I'll try to cover some things that other reviewers haven't.

Pros:
1) It never runs out (like canned air does). You can just keep recharging it. It saves money and cuts down on waste over the long run.
2) It has 3 speeds, unlike canned air, and sometimes you want a lower speed.
3) You can turn it UPSIDE DOWN. Very often I want to turn a can of compressed air upside down to dust some nook or cranny and all the liquid CO2 and propellent chemicals just squirt out. That's very dangerous and can harm your electronics. This battery powered blower can be turned at any angle. This, for me, is the PRIMARY reason I got this.
4) It has several attachments of various sorts. My canned air just comes with a single tube.
5) Because it's rechargeable and doesn't run out, I'm not as worried about "wasting" my canned air, so I'm more likely to use this in more situations.

Neutral:
1) The button has to be pressed for 3 seconds to turn on. Then each subsequent press cycles the speed, including turning it "off" into a standby mode. One press from standby puts you back on the low speed setting, but only if you do it within about 20 seconds or so. After that, it just turns off, and you have to hold it down for 3 seconds again to turn on. This is not a big deal to me, so I rate it as neutral.
2) It's loud, but not any louder than a blow dryer. My wife and I both agree that the highest setting is about blow-dryer loud, and slower speeds are quieter than a typical blow dryer. So, it's louder than canned air, but not louder than a blow dryer, so I think this is neutral.
3) I have no way to verify if it's really reaching the advertised RPMs, power, etc., but it doesn't really matter. It just matters how much air it blows.

Cons:
1) Yes, it's true, it's not as powerful as canned air dusters. I'd say at the max setting, it seems only about 1/2 to 2/3 as powerful as a can of air. However, it's rare that I need the full power of the canned air, and I still keep an air can around for just these instances. Since they're rare, I'm still not going through air cans very much. Sometimes the lower power is welcome, since now I can use it to dust off knick-knacks and things that compressed air is way too powerful for. So, it's a con, but not one I'm going to take a star off for.
2) The attachments just friction-fit on the end. They do NOT screw on/off, like I wish they would. I could imagine after many fittings of different attachments; they MAY get a bit loose. But it hasn't happened yet, and I don't know for sure if it ever will.
3) It didn't come with any kind of reusable box or bag or anything to keep the device or it's attachments in. This is actually not a big deal for me. I tend to just use the same attachment all the time, and I keep the blower right by my lab bench.

Overall, the pros far outweigh the cons, in my opinion. The only real (maybe) drawback is that it's less powerful than canned air. But, I'm not sure the technology exists to get the same power from a non-canned source, so this little device is still pushing the limits of what's possible in such a small package.

Final Rating: 5 Stars! This has replaced my canned air in 98% of uses.

title: USB 3.2 Hub works great!
text:
I needed to get this hub for a new PC I recently acquired. It only had 4 USB ports and NO SD card reader, but I needed a couple more USB ports and DEFINITELY and SD card reader. This unit from Rosonway was just what I needed. It gave me the couple of extra ports I needed and the card reader as well, all in a compact, well designed, and well-made package! The cable is a bit short at 2 feet - not a problem for me, but might be for some folks.

The case design is visually stunning: all black metal except for shiny chrome details here and there - around each port and around the top and bottom circumferences. There is a small but bright blue led at each port that visually shows that the port is active, and each port also has a button so they can be individually be turned on and off. I plugged it in to my new PC today and tested the ports and the SD card reader and everything worked perfectly! And because it's small, it hardly takes up any space on my already crowded desktop.

The only thing that was a bit of a miss on Rosonway's part is the barrel connector jack on the top of the case where the USB input cable is. It isn't explained anywhere in the documentation that came with the unit (except a sentence that says the power supply is not included), nor in the ad on Amazon. I presume that it's a way to add more power to the USB ports for devices that need it, but why slap a barrel connector on there instead of a USB3 port like most other hubs on the market? If the power supply was going to be included then that would be OK, but since it wasn't included, then that's just inconsiderate to the customer - leaving them to try to find a power supply with a compatible plug. They don't even mention the barrel dimensions, making a purchase even harder.

Anyway, this last point was an annoyance, but I think that even with that miss the device itself still deserves 5 stars for what it is. It really is a good piece of equipment.

title: Works Well, BUT...
text:
So... These cameras work, BUT, there are some things to consider:

1 - The time and date on the cameras WILL NOT update properly if your internet connection is poor. My cameras currently show the timestamp from the 21st of June (6 days ago), and not today. Even though it is still recording in real time.

2 - If you go around your cameras a lot, they will go off A LOT, regardless of the motion detecting or any other settings. This is good, but, gets rather annoying if you have your phone on you, and suddenly get 20+ notifications because the camera detects every little movement that you make and notifies you.

3 - These cameras need to be charged. They do not take batteries. You plug them in and charge them. So far, my batteries last about 2+ weeks if there is nothing to detect. The simple recording live feed does not take much battery life at all. It is when it detects motion that the battery begins to be used a lot.

Overall, for the price, these cameras are worth it if you need a simple security system to detect motion and alert you of anything suspicious. It has great options and they can be placed just about anywhere.

title: It ain't working right.  FIXED!!!!  See update below.
text:
First I want to say I gave it one star for gaming because I have NO IDEA how it is for gaming. Had I been able to skip that rating, I would have. Color seems fine, screen quality seems fine. However, my desktop comes up with 1-1/2 blue lines on the left and right hand sides. A thin blue line at the top of my desktop picture. And some kind of "ghost" just above the system tray gizmo that's always at the bottom of the screen. I called Acer tech support and got a very nice gentleman who could barely speak English. His final conclusion was that the monitor if faulty and now I have to ship it back for repair or replacement. The good news is I will be reimbursed for shipment and won't have to pay a dime to fulfill this annoying operation. I read so many good reviews about this model, I didn't hesitate to buy it. Right now I'm frustrated to the max. I'm no techie and have no techies near me who could help me out, so I have to go with what the Acer rep said. This monitor if very close to the one that died on me, and yet, after pulling up a program on hulu, I see I have 1-1/2" black bars on either side of the screen.

When this finally gets resolved, I will update--if I can figure out how to do that. LOL.

UPDATE 4-15-19: I was pretty sure the problem was some setting in the monitor. I emailed a brilliant techie friend of mine about the problem, including sending him screen shots of what the desktop looked like and what the setting for resolution said. He said there was nothing wrong with the monitor. [Oddly enough, the screen resolution was set to properly.] He took over my computer remotely, went into various settings--I have no idea what he actually changed. He was moving the cursor around so fast, clicking on this, that and the other thing, that I couldn't follow the procedure. After maybe 10 or 15 minutes, the monitor was working perfectly. So much for Acer tech support. I've upgraded the rating to 5 stars because now that it's working properly, I love this monitor. Colors are bold, Iris Mini works well to block out "blue light" without distorting colors, text is in focus and as sharp as I'm used to seeing it. All in all, I'd recommend this monitor. I didn't see a review here mentioning the same problem I had, but I'd still give my recommendation with the caveat to have a techie friend available who can easily fix the same problem I had should you run into it.

title: Runs hot, stops working
text:
In general, I'm a big fan of mokerlink products. I d been using their 8-port gigabit POE switches in hot Texas attics for a couple of years with no problems to run security cameras in two different locations. So, when searching for a multigig switch I didn't think twice about choosing this one.
Initially, for the first couple of hours, it worked great and I was getting the expected throughput at 2.5gbps from my PC to my NAS. I went to bed and the next morning woke up to no internet connection and a very, very hot switch.
I have the switch on a nice and cool desk with nothing on its sides or top.
Just to confirm it was the switch (hot doesn't always mean nonfunctional) I swapped to the other 2.5Gbe NIC in my PC (from Intel built-in to realtek pci-e) and changed the primary NIC on my NAS (QNAP TS-x53D with dual Intel NICs) and no luck. Unplugging the switch for around 30 minutes and then plugging it back in when it had cooled down would let me connect again, but eventually fail.

As a note, I wasn't doing any crazy file transfers at this point. Just basic web browsing and the NAS not doing much of anything.

The last piece of the puzzle is my uplink. I had the fifth port of the switch connected to the 2.5Gbe port on an Asus XT8 mesh node. With the switch not working, plugging my computer into this port gave me internet again instantly.

Unfortunately, giving mokerlink the benefit of the doubt and trying to troubleshoot every possible issue led to me missing the return window. It's too bad as I was seriously considering getting their more-expensive managed version to do port trunking but now I'm not confident that it would be any better.

So, I can't say if this was a one-off or if they are all like this. When it works, it works nicely. Maybe I'll try sticking it on top of a/next to a fan and seeing if I can get any more stability from it, but it's a shame considering how much I trust their gigabit products that this would happen.

title: Decent tablet
text:
My first tablet was a Google Nexus 7 in 2012. I've always used Android. I can't imagine using a tablet that doesn't have a micro SD card slot or some provision for storing data locally. I don't want a device that requires proprietary connectors. I can't imagine using a tablet for anything but content consumption. Without a decent user input interface you can't really do much else. A touch screen keyboard is best suited for the old Twitter character limit. Beyond that it's torture.

This tablet does what I want. It has a nice 2K display. It has more built in storage than I need and enough ram (6 GB) that most everything goes smoothly. It could use a stronger processor but it has what you'd expect at this price level. I stream video, browse the web, read, and play music with it. It has a capable wifi adapter. It can connect to my router at a usable speed from the house across the street. I doubt that you could play many games with it but I prefer a controller or keyboard. Again, think content consumption. I've been looking for a tablet that's cheaper than an [name of well known very expensive tablet that starts with a vowel goes here] that will run the web interface for Moode Audio, my preferred streaming software, for several years. This one does. It has an occasional lag but so does my i7 desktop machine.

I bought this tablet for the RAM, storage, and processor. At the Prime Day price the keyboard didn't matter. It cost less than the same model without a keyboard from other sources. The keyboard is disappointing. It's large enough for human hands and it's possible to type on it but it doesn't interact well with the screen. It's difficult to impossible to click on window controls like close and sizing. It's difficult to resize a window without using the touch screen. I wouldn't want to do work with it.

I was a little surprised that a standard 5v 2a charger doesn't work well. I'm a little behind the times. An ordinary USB charger generates a check cable error message. A 20w fast charger, like the one that comes with it, works fine. A 2a charger will work but very slowly. A 5v 3a charger is strong enough to avoid the error message but isn't as fast as the supplied charger. Oh well, technology marches on.

title: First thing is to update to Windows 10 (edit: or Ubuntu 16.04)
text:
I purchased this laptop for it being lightweight, long battery life, and bootable via external devices, specifically USB. Unfortunately, Ubuntu 15.04 did not detect the touchpad. So, I tried, tried, tried using Windows 8.1 and it was terrible compared to Windows 7 (did I mentioned I really tried to get use to Windows 8). As a result of not having a respectable OS to use, this laptop was unused for 4 months until Windows 10 was released.

This laptop works well with Windows 10. I did a clean install of Windows 10 after the update (many online guides on how to do this baremetal Window 10 easy install via USB stick after upgrade), download and install some lenovo drivers not automatically discovered with windows 10. Works very well with Windows 10 for a < $200 portable laptop.

Issues I ran into:
- Not use to having a 2 button mouse without a defined divider.
- Physical feedback from the power button could be improved. (did it turn it on?)
- Wish it had a full size SD card reader instead

It does satisfy my needs and works well as a portable laptop.

Last note: update bios to remove Lenovo Service Engine - online search will give details on why you should do this.

Edit 2016-07-10: This laptop is now my primary travel laptop after installing Ubuntu 16.04 with hard drive encryption, which works great.

title: Sounds Great for $158
text:
I've been eyeing these buds since they were released but was hesitant to purchase them due to the mixed reviews for the ANC, even with the initial launch discount. That said, my new neighbors are frat boys who party at any hour and are destroying my night-shift body's minimal sleep schedule. And, while I do have noise canceling technology (Bose Headphones), they aren't devices that one can wear comfortably in bed. As such, I decided to bite the bullet when these buds went on sale on Prime Day for $158.

Having worn these now for a few hours, I'll share my current thoughts:
- ANC is far from sub-par. You might notice a decrease in quality if you're used to the high-end stuff, but if you're like me and your only experience with NC are headphones that create pressure on your ears, this is certainly a worthy purchase. The Sony app is still learning to adjust (it has only been a few hours after all) so I'll sometimes hear my fan on full blast if I move locations, but the earbuds adjust and make the fan noise completely vanish within about 15 seconds.
- I consider myself to have ears on the smaller scale (I'm 5'1") and am usually skeptical of earbuds that have a round body. That said, these have not yet caused any ear pain and the Medium ear tips (these are the tips that are on the earbuds when you open the box) had a fairly comfortable fit. After a few hours, I decided to try the Small ear tips and realized that they were the better fit for the fact that the earbud bodies sat more snugly in my ears and didn't protrude as much. Unfortunately, I found that the Small tips were a tad too small for my ears as the NC could no longer completely block out the sound of my fan. After about 5-10 minutes of bouncing between the Medium and Small tips, I decided to stick with the Medium tips since NC was of better quality. And it's not like I'm worried about the buds falling out of my ears.
- Charging is fairly simple, both for the buds and the case. I did notice that some folks here were upset about the lack of wireless charging but, as a cat parent, I find the ability to charge my case via a secure cable extremely reassuring.

title: Outstanding Customer Service, very high quality product, very easy to use, a must buy!
text:
I used this product to connect to my old Sony Video camera to transfer countless old family video tapes to digital MP4 files. It would have been cost prohibitive to have sent my tapes out to a service to do the conversion. (Not to mention the risk of a service loosing a tape or the tape being damaged through the mail.)

Previously, I had tried to use another product that allowed a direct download to my PC from my camera, but these tapes are 120 min in length, and inevitably Windows would perform a housekeeping chore and I would get frame drops. What that means for the final product would be a slight disconnect between the audio and video. A person would be talking, but the dialog and video would be out of sync.

Because ClearClick stands on its own, there are far fewer opportunities for frame drops. Only once did I experience a frame drop, likely because of something that happened on the camera side, and a reprocess of the tape resolved it. Whereas the PC I had frame drops on the majority of tapes I tried to convert. I took countless measures to eliminate them, but it was just not possible.

There are many amazing features to this product, one of which is the ability to set a fixed time for it to run before writing out an MP4 file. What that means is that I can download a tape from the camera to digital MP4 in an unattended mode.

I strongly recommend the purchase of the recommended Sandisk 512gb USB 3.0 device for capturing the final MP4 files. This brand was recommended by ClearClick, and it worked directly out of the box, no issues, no need to format it etc.

From a customer service perspective, there is no question about the high degree of support for this product. I had a question for customer service, which I communicated via an email to Clear Click customer support and received an almost immediate response. VERY responsive and helpful.

I highly recommend this product if you have tapes to convert, it works great, it is simple to use, you do not need to have a technical background to operate it. If you can plug a cable from your video camera to ClearClick and press the record button on ClearClick, you are qualified!

title: Protective case
text:
This case can protect the AirTag, though opening the case is difficult.

This package contained helpful instructions.
- Open the case from the groove at the bottom; this takes much effort.
- Slide a finger from the groove around both sides until the two pieces separate. Opening from the groove takes extra effort, as does sliding a finger around the perimeter of the case.
- Remove the two rings (keyring and clamp).
- Place the AirTag inside one of the pieces.
- Align the two plastic pieces together.
- Press the plastic pieces together from one side to the other to ensure a proper seal.

So I really wanted to be able to give 5 stars for these earbuds but I had issues with phone calls. I have an iPhone 11 Pro Max and every time I used them with calls, I had complaints that my words were muffled and hard to hear. I could hear everything clearly and made sure nothing obstructed the mic on the ear buds but the person on the other end had a hard time hearing me. I also couldn’t use just one ear bud on a call. I had to always put the second ear bud in if I wanted to use the ear buds.

However, these are great for listening to music, movies or audiobooks. They have fantastic sound and have a great battery life. I had no problems getting them to last for 8 hours. They also connect super easy to your device. I tried them on my ipad and iPhone and both connected instantly. I did have to disconnect from the first device so it could connect to a new device but no problems at all. The case itself fits easily in the palm of my hand and came with a partial charge so it didn’t take too long for the first charge. Directions are provided and easy to understand.

So would I recommend these? If you just want them for listening to music or movies or books then yes. They have terrific sound. If you make a lot of calls then I’m not so sure.

BUT THIS! I don't know what this cover is made from and frankly don't care. IT IS AWESOME. Excellent fit. No sliding around. Fantastically thin. title: Good picture but Vertical Banding
text:
This TCL 55" TV has a lot of promise; the picture quality is truly stunning and it was pretty easy to setup. The sound is quite adequate for general movie listening and the inputs are well placed and easy to access. We had one big issue, though, that caused us to have to return it. We noticed only after a short time of watching that it had noticeable vertical "fogging" or banding, a form Dirty Screen Effect (DSE). This couldn't be seen when the images contained lots of color, but watching a hockey game showed the bands up pretty quickly. Loading a pure white blank screen caused it to show even more prominently. Now, in fairness, it didn't interfere with watching most things, but when a scene came up with a bright light-blue sky, for example, we could see the banding - most noticeably from side angles - direct on it was nearly unnoticeable.

If you can live with a bit of vertical banding, for the price this TV is an excellent value. Our concern was that if it came this way out of the box, it might get worse, as some reviewers have noted, plus after about a week the banding got a bit worse than the picture I included.

Finally, TCL really needs to step up their packaging. Delivery companies seem to like kicking expensive electronics around and ours was no exception. The box had all kinds of creases, dents, a few punctures and lots of wear marks. The cardboard should be thicker and the inside foam padding was pretty skimpy. LG double boxes their TVs and the Styrofoam completely encases the TV. Not so with the TCL. A simple upgrade to the shipping materials could save them LOTS of returns.

One final word: Amazon was absolutely outstanding in handling the return and providing a refund.

title: Nice starter watch for the price.
text:
Many will immediately judge these watch as cheap knock off while these watches are actually very functional. To start the battery life is actually pretty good as I was able to use it for 5 days before having to charge it. The accuracy of the watch is as good as the users settings and if you don't set it up it's not going to do much. I couldn't bring myself to test the Waterproofing.

Setting up this watch or binding it to your phone is easy. Download the app, turn on the watch and get to the QR code screen, scan, and you'll be ready to go.

The screen is a step up from the older TFT displays. The brightness can be adjust to dim or bright and what's in-between. The home screen can be changed to a variety of choices. Though you will find the selections ultimately finite there is a few that each user will like. There are a few animated ones and that list is even shorter. Since there doesn't seem to be any way to get a user base to create more screens you'll be stuck with what is on there.

The heart beat monitor function was a little weird to me but, it did its job. The sleep function didn't seem too accurate to me as it said I got 3 hours of sleep when I slept in for almost 14hours. So, I don't know how that works. Charging the watch is fast with the included magnetic charger I was able to get a full charge in about and hour. The watch band is a standard watch band. Nothing to make it stand out and shine just an old band, we've gotten since the first LCD quartz watches from the 70s and 80s.

SMS did not work too well with my phone as I didn't use the default SMS app with the phone. The text messages I did manage to get looked pixelated and looked like an old MS DOS screen. The watch was able to accept calls and decline them. Calls quality was not the greatest and you have to remember to not walk away from your phone. Being on the phone drained the battery a lot faster than being idle. For the price this is great starter watch for those who don't want to spring for a brand name but, has some functions to match more expensive brands.

title: Upgrade today
text:
With the ever evolving technology we all want the best of our tech. Even with the already UHD resolution smart TVs we would like to think; just plug an play and we should have the best of it all. However the world isn't perfect and we're force to make sure our TV is capable of hot terms like 120hz, VRR, ALLM, Freesync, HDR10+, Dolby Atmos, and/or Dolby Vision. With that in mind this cable was the perfect solution for cheap factory supplied cables most companies package with their products. While many TVs have HDMI only the current up to date have HDMI 2.1, some are lucky to even have HDMI 2.0

So, without having to take pictures of my TV and setup I took screenshots of my PlayStation 5 Video output information screen. For those that are unaware the PlayStation 5 actually demands a lot from your TV with HDMI 2.1. I have a PS5 hooked up to my Television set with a Dolby Atmos Speaker system to create the ultimate Immersive experience. The PS5 was hit with a large update which made a lot people run to the store and look up their TV specs to make sure they can support the New VRR feature and to many peoples' surprise they ended up losing out on things such as resolution and HDR colors just to have a higher FPS using VRR 120hz. Given that same predicament prior I sprang for extra cables and the results were on point. I ran the test and the games are smooth without losing HDR or resolution. I like to run may games on Resolution Mode as I am a fan of games with photo mode. Some games have High Resolution mode with VRR/High FPS makes for some of the best visuals I've ever seen, making me glad we're in this generation of gaming/tech. So if you're looking for a well priced HDMI 2.1 cable stop here and give this a try.

The Nylon braided cables gives the wires a premium look and feel vs a plain rubber wire and for those that have cables running through the wall it adds a bit of extra protection (Supposedly). The Wire alone stands out giving you a visual/physical attribute to sort your cables/system without having to think too much about what it's hooked up to. So far I haven't had any bad handshake issues with this cable as I've already played the latest installment of a popular FPS shooter as of writing this, at 120hz with zero hiccups. This cable is definitely a big upgrade while some may trust the cable supplied by SONY I've ran into a few handshake issues such as long blank screens, as the TV tries to figure out what signal is being sent to it. Definitely worth the buck and I grabbed an extra for other devices.

title: Do not fear the light...
text:
We've been wanting a really dark ND filter to play with things like shooting wide open in bright light and taking very long exposures. We are all about the long exposures around here. This filter reduces the exposure by a mighty 10 f-stops, so with it we can shoot at f/1.2 even in bright sun, or take exposures of thirty seconds or more.

For the test we sadly didn’t have any waterfalls or seashores handy (favorite subjects for long exposures), but we do have trees, and wind. In the first picture, top photo is 1/4s exposure at f/1.2, bottom is thirty seconds at f/14. You can see that the shadows on the fence are very different - softer and less distinct - in the long exposure. You can also see that my tomatoes are really struggling this season but I don't blame the filter for that.

The second photo is to show a shot with extremely shallow depth of field, despite being brightly lit. We also chose a brightly-colored subject to test color neutrality. The filter is very color-neutral and the construction feels solid. This is going to be a fun toy to use for a long time to come.

I am comparing these to some serious duty noise canceling headphones a family member of mine has, where you literally can’t hear a thing with them on. title: A decent port for the price. May not have all of the fasts capabilities but its a good balance.
text:
I got this for my son to use with a monitor since his notebook doesn’t have a DP or HDMI port on it.

The Unit:
The docking station quite compact for the number of ports it has on it. It is compact enough to put easily in a backpack pocket or a small(ish) size purse. Considering it has a metal casing and a 100W power capability, it is quite light. The design is attractive enough and has a solid quality feeling and look to it.

The Ports:
It is sort of confusing trying to figure out what ports this dock really has by the written description. There is an image that explains them, but I’ll outline it here for your easy reference.

3 x USB-A 2.0
1 x USB-C PD w/ 100W charging capacity
2 x USB-A 3.1
1 x USB-C 3.1
2 x SD Card readers (standard and min)
VGA Port
2 x HDMI 4K @ 30 Hz
1 x Gigabit ethernet
1 x 3.5 audio jack

The USB ports offered are a good balance when it comes to speed and type. You can choose which devices need faster transfer speeds and use the ports accordingly. USB-C are also similarly split. One of the weaker aspects of this dock is the lack of Display Ports. This is sort of strange considering the HDMI limitations. The product material isn’t very clear and at times seems to contradict itself. From my experience, you can only run one monitor at 4K @30Hz. If you what to increase the refresh to 60Hz you have to go down to 2K. If you want to run dual monitors with the two HDMI ports, the max is 2K @30. Beyond this, I haven’t tested. A nice feature to this dock is the gigabit ethernet. Most dock that I have seen near this price range only have 10/100 mbs. If you do work off a wire connection, it is great to be able to access the greater throughput. One thing to note, this does not come with a cable to power the dock so unless you get one/have one, you’ll be running on battery or the computers power adapter.

The Evaluation:
As mentioned above, the reason I got this was to hook up a monitor. For normal work in windows running Office or streaming video over the web, the HDMIs delivered clear images and video with out lag or blurring. Text was clear as well. I didn’t have any issues with the USB A or C’s. All seems to transfer at good data speeds. Gigabit was okay. I wasn’t reaching similar speeds to another laptop that had an internal gigabit port.

For the number of ports, compact size and overall performance relative to the price, the Intpw dock is a solid value. Yes, it could be better, but this fills the roll of being a desktop dock, but also being able to be portable. I would recommend this dock for those reasons.

title: This is a fine projector, based on its price point and specs
text:
I have an Epson 5050 full 4K HDR projector, and this Wewatch does not pretend to be that higher end machine.
What this Wewatch is, is a very portable, lightweight, all in one machine. He has a fine picture, and works well, even projected on a lightly textured wall. It will benefit form a pretty dark viewing area. Its brightness is fine for dark conditions, but it can not overpower ambient light. Its contrast is fine for impromptu movie watching, or a campout, but again not a primary component for your home theater.
This does have apple tv connectivity built in, and it will allow you to stream from your iphone, via wifi. I watched some YouTube videos, and Disney plus content. It was a little laggy, and the audio did not match up perfectly, but it was very watchable, and entertaining, again, especially at this price point. I am sure a wired connection would be better.
I got this projector as a display device for my child to play video games on. I did not want to add a television to his room. We will be connecting an Xbox to it, and I think it will be great for that purpose. I think the need for darkness will help limit how much time he spends on the videogame as well.
Overall this is a serviceable projector, for secondary video needs, with great ease of portability. It does not come with a case, but the packaging is neatly designed to be a functional case. It was well protected within the packaging, and is completely encompassed in soft foam. It comes with a remote, but no batteries. It has hard buttons on top to operate all the features, however having on hand 2 triple A batteries, will allow you to use the included remote, and make operation much easier.

title: A most for digital Nomads
text:
This is a lightweight display. It has a foldable flap cover that protects the LCD screen and doubles as a stand. It comes nicely packaged with various cable connections to your laptop, including HDMI and USB-C.

The INGNOK is plug-and-play. It’s as easy as connecting the USB-C cable that comes in the accessories box to my MacBook, and bam. And we are rolling.

Overall I am very impressed with the performance of the INGNOK 16-inch display. I’ve been working as a digital nomad for years and have used my iPad as a secondary display to my MacBook Pro. The dream was to have a secondary display the same size as the 16-inch MacBook Pro display. The INGNOK is a dream come true by providing a lightweight, portable display with HDR capabilities while maintaining decent sharpness. Although the INGNOK can’t match the exact sharpness and color of the MacBook Retina display, it makes a formidable companion.

The straight-out-of-the-box settings are a bit flat and dim, but with a few adjustments, I made it a formidable companion to my MacBook Pro’s 16-inch display.

I recommend the following settings to match the color and brightness of the MacBook.

Brightness: 70 Percent
Contrast: 70 Percent
Sharpness: 3

Color Settings:
Red 50
Green 49
Blue 50

Other Settings:
HDR: Auto
OD: On

title: Keeps dropping connections on random devices
text:
So we were forced to upgrade to gigabit because of changes at our ISP (Cox). We were using the older google WiFi, which was pretty good but some parts of the house didn't get very good coverage. So I researched and researched and decided to go with the ASUS ZenWifi. It's... worse. Much worse. When it does work the speed is a little bit faster but it just drops things randomly (and yes, I turned the roaming assistant off). Plus the second "Mesh" router will just randomly drop for a while and lose everything it is connected to (which is my NAS, plex server and Wyze camera hub) until it randomly decides to come back up or I cycle the power.

For reference: We have about 45 wireless devices and 4 wired devices on the network. We're in suburbia, so there are between 6 and 10 other wifi networks visible from houses around us. Congested, but not as much as an apartment building. 2 story house, 2800 sqft, 2 ZenWifi devices in "AI Mesh" mode with a dedicated 5Ghz backhaul. Cox "gigablast" (940Gbps) with a Motorola DOCSIS 3.1 modem.

Honestly I think I'm going to go with the newer google WiFi. It doesn't support gigabit speeds, but it's faster than the old one and if it's as stable then it's a whole lot better than this.

Also... where are the parental controls? I want to setup my 9 year old triplets so that I can shut them off when needed or setup schedules (like on google wifi), but when I go to the family settings I have to choose an "age group" and then accept an extremely invasive terms of agreement for Trend Micro. I'm not at all interested in Trend Micro looking at my network traffic whenever they want. It doesn't appear to be possible unless I accept that, and I'm not going to. If there is another easy way to disconnect a group of devices I haven't found it. (And no, I'm not interested in using Trend Micro as a network filter - I have other, better, ways to solve that problem already).

I have to say, this is the most trouble I've ever had with IQShield stuff. Not sure if I got a bad batch or whatever, but it took me 3 tries to get a "bubble-free", "particle-free" installation on my watch. The first two times, I was doing the exact same thing as the instructional video recommends, but always ended up with something under the shield, like a particle of some sort, not bubble. I could not fix it. I suspect that the glue itself may have the particle in it already before I applied. Anyway, the third time was a charm, I got one installed with just  one small thing at the edge. I call it success for now. Good thing is that they include 6 of these shields inside one package, you I could afford a couple retries. I would use these again; I've been using them forever, and they do a good job of protecting the phone/watch face from accidentally bumping into walls, and such. No regrets buying these.

title: So far so VERY good!
text:
I bought this laptop just to have something "mobile" when I want to get online or do some "light work" out of the house (I normally use my desktop computer which is a BEAST!)

I will be using this to watch movies/videos, surf the net, check emails, go on social media and a couple other programs such a OBDII reader that I will use with my OBDII device via wifi or usb to work on my cars.

4GB of ram is good enough for what I will be doing. If I ever feel that it needs a little more power/speed I will add another 4 or 8 but so far it is perfect.

The 128GB SSD is more than enough for what I need and this was one of the key factors that made me buy this computer. Cheaper ones come with eMMC storage which is slower and normally only 32GB or 64GB

It does not have backlit keyboard, I wish it did but it is not a deal breaker and I already knew it didn't have it before placing my order.

It takes about 45 seconds to boot (a little bit on the slow side) but once its loaded it runs pretty smoothly

It came with Windows 11 S More which won't allow you to install anything except from the Microsoft store (I think that's what's called), but getting out of S mode is SUPER EASY, takes less than 1 minute. There are plenty of YouTube videos on how to do that. But, be aware, seems like if you get out of S mode there is no turning back!

In a few words, this is a very good machine for the price. I am not intending to use it for gaming, editing videos or designing. It is strictly for light use (browse the net, documents, watching videos/movies, and a couple of programs that I like that don't require much to run).

It is pretty lightweight, the casing looks nice, the screen is matte and bright enough, the speakers are OK, seems a little bit fragile if you were to drop it or step on it (I am always careful, so this is not a concern). I also like the fact that is a name brand and is not a chrome book!

I don't give it 5 stars because it would've been nice to get it with 8GB and a backlit keyboard. Other than that is perfect for what I need!

title: Amazing Monitor with a few caveats..
text:
Overall this is likely the best monitor on the market today with a few caveats. I rarely play games but since I work in tech and stay at a screen for over 8 hours having a good monitor to protect my eyes and make work most pleasant is very important. This monitor replaced a very good LG dual 27" QHD monitor set, that retails a little more than half the price.

Let's get the negatives out of the way first...

1. My monitor seems to be perfect, but I hear quality control issues are rampant with prior-model Samsung OLED monitors so inspect carefully.

2. Connectivity mini DP and mini HDMI stink. No reason not to include full sized cables. USB C is great as is the included ability of power delivery, but it does not have a USB hub meaning only one additional USB device can be plugged other than the PC. I solved this by adding a small USB-c to A hub so I could use my web cam and DAC. While it has speakers it has no audio output which would be nice.

3. The stand is just ok. It height adjustment stopped short of going as high as I would like, tilt swivel range of motion is tiny as well. Thankfully a VESA mount is included so a superior stand or arm can be added.

4. The "smarts" are little obtrusive and annoying. While it is nice to have the ability to run apps directly on the screen. The biggest use case of this screen is running with PC, I wish I wasn't confronted wish popups and menus constantly, full instance every time I wake my PC samsung overlays unnecessary text and options on the screen for several seconds. I can't find anyway to disable it either. On top of that the menu system is quite complicated and it requires a remote to use.

On to the positives.

1. It has an amazing picture the inky blacks and subpixel rendering deliver an immersive experience without stressing your eyes in a way a normal LED screen can't

2. The 34" wide screen is actually ideal. I find it more organized that two screens while maintaining the same amount of windows open, my eyes more easily manage the wider single screen rather shifting from one screen to another.

Overall this is a very good screen and if you can justify the price it is worth it. It may be marketed as a gaming display but outside of resolution which is somewhat made up for with subpixeling this display rivals things like the apple pro-display, studio display and LG Ultrafine OLED which costs multiples of this screen.
